Benchmark.title: CIS Ubuntu Linux 24.04 LTS Benchmark
Benchmark.description:
<xhtml:p>This document provides prescriptive guidance for establishing a secure configuration posture for Ubuntu Linux 24.04 LTS systems running on x86_64 platforms.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>This guide was developed and tested against Ubuntu Linux 24.04 LTS</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The guidance within broadly assumes that operations are being performed as the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span> user, and executed under the default Bash version for the applicable distribution. Operations performed using <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo</xhtml:span> instead of the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span> user, or executed under another shell, may produce unexpected results, or fail to make the intended changes to the system. Non-root users may not be able to access certain areas of the system, especially after remediation has been performed. It is advisable to verify <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span> users path integrity and the integrity of any programs being run prior to execution of commands and scripts included in this benchmark.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The default prompt for the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span> user is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">#</xhtml:span>, and as such all sample commands will have <xhtml:span class="inline_block">#</xhtml:span> as an additional indication that it is to be executed as <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>To obtain the latest version of this guide, please visit <xhtml:a href="http://workbench.cisecurity.org">http://workbench.cisecurity.org</xhtml:a>. If you have questions, comments, or have identified ways to improve this guide, please write us at <xhtml:a href="mailto:feedback@cisecurity.org">feedback@cisecurity.org</xhtml:a>.</xhtml:p>

Group.title: Initial Setup
Group.description: <xhtml:p>Items in this section are advised for all systems but may be difficult or require extensive preparation after the initial setup of the system.</xhtml:p>

Group.title: Filesystem
Group.description: <xhtml:p>The file system is generally a built-in layer used to handle the data management of the storage.</xhtml:p>

Group.title: Configure Filesystem Kernel Modules
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>Several uncommon filesystem types are supported under Linux. Removing support for unneeded filesystem types reduces the local attack surface of the system. If a filesystem type is not needed it should be disabled. Native Linux file systems are designed to ensure that built-in security controls function as expected. Non-native filesystems can lead to unexpected consequences to both the security and functionality of the system and should be used with caution. Many filesystems are created for niche use cases and are not maintained and supported as the operating systems are updated and patched. Users of non-native filesystems should ensure that there is attention and ongoing support for them, especially in light of frequent operating system changes.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Standard network connectivity and Internet access to cloud storage may make the use of non-standard filesystem formats to directly attach heterogeneous devices much less attractive.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note</xhtml:strong>: This should not be considered a comprehensive list of filesystems. You may wish to consider additions to those listed here for your environment. For the current available file system modules on the system see <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel/fs</xhtml:span></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Start up scripts</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Kernel modules loaded directly via <xhtml:span class="inline_block">insmod</xhtml:span> will ignore what is configured in the relevant <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/modprobe.d/*.conf</xhtml:span> files. If modules are still being loaded after a reboot whilst having the correctly configured <xhtml:span class="inline_block">blacklist</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">install</xhtml:span> command, check for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">insmod</xhtml:span> entries in start up scripts such as <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.bashrc</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>You may also want to check <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/lib/modprobe.d/</xhtml:span>. Please note that this directory should not be used for user defined module loading. Ensure that all such entries resides in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/modprobe.d/*.conf</xhtml:span> files.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Return values</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Using <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/bin/false</xhtml:span> as the command in disabling a particular module serves two purposes; to convey the meaning of the entry to the user and cause a non-zero return value. The latter can be tested for in scripts. Please note that <xhtml:span class="inline_block">insmod</xhtml:span> will ignore what is configured in the relevant <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/modprobe.d/*.conf</xhtml:span> files. The preferred way to load modules is with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">modprobe</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure cramfs kernel module is not available
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cramfs</xhtml:span> filesystem type is a compressed read-only Linux filesystem embedded in small footprint systems. A <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cramfs</xhtml:span> image can be used without having to first decompress the image.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software
Ensure Only Approved Ports, Protocols and Services Are Running

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Removing support for unneeded filesystem types reduces the local attack surface of the system. If this filesystem type is not needed, disable it.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to unload and disable the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cramfs</xhtml:span> module:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cramfs</xhtml:span> kernel module is available in ANY installed kernel:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Create a file ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">install cramfs /bin/false</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/modprobe.d/</xhtml:span> directory</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Create a file ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">blacklist cramfs</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/modprobe.d/</xhtml:span> directory</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Run <xhtml:span class="inline_block">modprobe -r cramfs 2>/dev/null; rmmod cramfs 2>/dev/null</xhtml:span> to remove <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cramfs</xhtml:span> from the kernel</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cramfs</xhtml:span> kernel module is not available on the system, or pre-compiled into the kernel, no remediation is necessary</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_output2=() a_output3=() l_dl="" l_mod_name="cramfs" l_mod_type="fs"<br />   l_mod_path="$(readlink -f /lib/modules/**/kernel/$l_mod_type | sort -u)"<br />   f_module_fix()<br />   {<br />      l_dl="y" a_showconfig=()<br />      while IFS= read -r l_showconfig; do<br />         a_showconfig+=("$l_showconfig")<br />      done < <(modprobe --showconfig | grep -P -- '\b(install|blacklist)\h+'"${l_mod_chk_name//-/_}"'\b')<br />      if  lsmod | grep "$l_mod_chk_name" &> /dev/null; then<br />         a_output2+=(" - unloading kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\"")<br />         modprobe -r "$l_mod_chk_name" 2>/dev/null; rmmod "$l_mod_name" 2>/dev/null<br />      fi<br />      if ! grep -Pq -- '\binstall\h+'"${l_mod_chk_name//-/_}"'\h+(\/usr)?\/bin\/(true|false)\b' <<< "${a_showconfig[*]}"; then<br />         a_output2+=(" - setting kernel  module: \"$l_mod_name\" to \"$(readlink -f /bin/false)\"")<br />         printf '%s\n' "install $l_mod_chk_name $(readlink -f /bin/false)" >> /etc/modprobe.d/"$l_mod_name".conf<br />      fi<br />      if ! grep -Pq -- '\bblacklist\h+'"${l_mod_chk_name//-/_}"'\b' <<< "${a_showconfig[*]}"; then<br />         a_output2+=(" - denylisting kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\"")<br />         printf '%s\n' "blacklist $l_mod_chk_name" >> /etc/modprobe.d/"$l_mod_name".conf<br />      fi<br />   }<br />   for l_mod_base_directory in $l_mod_path; do # Check if the module exists on the system<br />      if [ -d "$l_mod_base_directory/${l_mod_name/-/\/}" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$l_mod_base_directory/${l_mod_name/-/\/}")" ]; then<br />         a_output3+=("  - \"$l_mod_base_directory\"")<br />         l_mod_chk_name="$l_mod_name"<br />         [[ "$l_mod_name" =~ overlay ]] && l_mod_chk_name="${l_mod_name::-2}"        <br />         [ "$l_dl" != "y" ] && f_module_fix<br />      else<br />         printf '%s\n' " - kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\" doesn't exist in \"$l_mod_base_directory\""<br />      fi<br />   done<br />   [ "${#a_output3[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "" " -- INFO --" " - module: \"$l_mod_name\" exists in:" "${a_output3[@]}"<br />   [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "" "${a_output2[@]}" || printf '%s\n' "" " - No changes needed"<br />   printf '%s\n' "" " - remediation of kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\" complete" ""<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to verify:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cramfs</xhtml:span> kernel module is available in ANY installed kernel, verify:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>An entry including <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/bin/true</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/bin/false</xhtml:span> exists in a file within the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/modprobe.d/</xhtml:span> directory</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The module is deny listed in a file within the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/modprobe.d/</xhtml:span> directory</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The module is not loaded in the running kernel</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cramfs</xhtml:span> kernel module is not available on the system, or pre-compiled into the kernel, no additional configuration is necessary</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_output=() a_output2=() a_output3=() l_dl="" l_mod_name="cramfs" l_mod_type="fs"<br />   l_mod_path="$(readlink -f /lib/modules/**/kernel/$l_mod_type | sort -u)"<br />   f_module_chk()<br />   {<br />      l_dl="y" a_showconfig=()<br />      while IFS= read -r l_showconfig; do<br />         a_showconfig+=("$l_showconfig")<br />      done < <(modprobe --showconfig | grep -P -- '\b(install|blacklist)\h+'"${l_mod_chk_name//-/_}"'\b')<br />      if ! lsmod | grep "$l_mod_chk_name" &> /dev/null; then<br />         a_output+=("  - kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\" is not loaded")<br />      else<br />         a_output2+=("  - kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\" is loaded")<br />      fi<br />      if grep -Pq -- '\binstall\h+'"${l_mod_chk_name//-/_}"'\h+(\/usr)?\/bin\/(true|false)\b' <<< "${a_showconfig[*]}"; then<br />         a_output+=("  - kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\" is not loadable")<br />      else<br />         a_output2+=("  - kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\" is loadable")<br />      fi<br />      if grep -Pq -- '\bblacklist\h+'"${l_mod_chk_name//-/_}"'\b' <<< "${a_showconfig[*]}"; then<br />         a_output+=("  - kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\" is deny listed")<br />      else<br />         a_output2+=("  - kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\" is not deny listed")<br />      fi<br />   }<br />   for l_mod_base_directory in $l_mod_path; do<br />      if [ -d "$l_mod_base_directory/${l_mod_name/-/\/}" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$l_mod_base_directory/${l_mod_name/-/\/}")" ]; then<br />         a_output3+=("  - \"$l_mod_base_directory\"")<br />         l_mod_chk_name="$l_mod_name"<br />         [[ "$l_mod_name" =~ overlay ]] && l_mod_chk_name="${l_mod_name::-2}"        <br />         [ "$l_dl" != "y" ] && f_module_chk<br />      else<br />         a_output+=(" - kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\" doesn't exist in \"$l_mod_base_directory\"")<br />      fi<br />   done<br />   [ "${#a_output3[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "" " -- INFO --" " - module: \"$l_mod_name\" exists in:" "${a_output3[@]}"<br />   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}"<br />   else<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" " - Reason(s) for audit failure:" "${a_output2[@]}"<br />      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}"<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

safeguard.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Removing support for unneeded filesystem types reduces the local attack surface of the system. If this filesystem type is not needed, disable it.</xhtml:p>

<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">jffs2</xhtml:span> kernel module is available in ANY installed kernel:</xhtml:p>

<xhtml:li>Unload the filesystem kernel module from the kernel</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Create a file ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> with install filesystem kernel modules <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/bin/false</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/modprobe.d/</xhtml:span> directory</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Create a file ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> with deny list filesystem kernel modules in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/modprobe.d/</xhtml:span> directory</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>WARNING</xhtml:strong>: unloading, disabling or denylisting filesystem modules that are in use on the system maybe FATAL. It is extremely important to thoroughly review the filesystems returned by the audit before following the remediation procedure.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example of unloading the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">gfs2</xhtml:span>kernel module:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># modprobe -r gfs2 2>/dev/null<br /># rmmod gfs2 2>/dev/null
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example of fully disabling the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">gfs2</xhtml:span> kernel module:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># printf '%s\n' "blacklist gfs2" "install gfs2 /bin/false" >> /etc/modprobe.d/gfs2.conf
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Disabling a kernel module by modifying the command above for each unused filesystem kernel module</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The example <xhtml:span class="inline_block">gfs2</xhtml:span> must be updated with the appropriate module name for the command or example script bellow to run correctly.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Below is an example Script that can be modified to use on various filesystem kernel modules manual remediation process:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example Script</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_output2=(); a_output3=(); l_dl="" # Initialize arrays and clear variables<br />   l_mod_name="gfs2" # set module name<br />   l_mod_type="fs" # set module type<br />   l_mod_path="$(readlink -f /lib/modules/**/kernel/$l_mod_type | sort -u)"<br />   f_module_fix()<br />   {<br />      l_dl="y" # Set to ignore duplicate checks<br />      a_showconfig=() # Create array with modprobe output<br />      while IFS= read -r l_showconfig; do<br />         a_showconfig+=("$l_showconfig")<br />      done < <(modprobe --showconfig | grep -P -- '\b(install|blacklist)\h+'"${l_mod_name//-/_}"'\b')<br />      if  lsmod | grep "$l_mod_name" &> /dev/null; then # Check if the module is currently loaded<br />         a_output2+=(" - unloading kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\"")<br />         modprobe -r "$l_mod_name" 2>/dev/null; rmmod "$l_mod_name" 2>/dev/null<br />      fi<br />      if ! grep -Pq -- '\binstall\h+'"${l_mod_name//-/_}"'\h+(\/usr)?\/bin\/(true|false)\b' <<< "${a_showconfig[*]}"; then<br />         a_output2+=(" - setting kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\" to \"$(readlink -f /bin/false)\"")<br />         printf '%s\n' "install $l_mod_name $(readlink -f /bin/false)" >> /etc/modprobe.d/"$l_mod_name".conf<br />      fi<br />      if ! grep -Pq -- '\bblacklist\h+'"${l_mod_name//-/_}"'\b' <<< "${a_showconfig[*]}"; then<br />         a_output2+=(" - denylisting kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\"")<br />         printf '%s\n' "blacklist $l_mod_name" >> /etc/modprobe.d/"$l_mod_name".conf<br />      fi<br />   }<br />   for l_mod_base_directory in $l_mod_path; do # Check if the module exists on the system<br />      if [ -d "$l_mod_base_directory/${l_mod_name/-/\/}" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$l_mod_base_directory/${l_mod_name/-/\/}")" ]; then<br />         a_output3+=("  - \"$l_mod_base_directory\"")<br />         [[ "$l_mod_name" =~ overlay ]] && l_mod_name="${l_mod_name::-2}"        <br />         [ "$l_dl" != "y" ] && f_module_fix<br />      else<br />         echo -e " - kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\" doesn't exist in \"$l_mod_base_directory\""<br />      fi<br />   done<br />   [ "${#a_output3[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "" " -- INFO --" " - module: \"$l_mod_name\" exists in:" "${a_output3[@]}"<br />   [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "" "${a_output2[@]}" || printf '%s\n' "" " - No changes needed"<br />   printf '%s\n' "" " - remediation of kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\" complete" ""<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>This list may be quite extensive and covering all edges cases is difficult. Therefore, it's crucial to carefully consider the implications and dependencies before making any changes to the filesystem kernel module configurations.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Look at the filesystem kernel modules available to the currently running kernel.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Exclude mounted filesystem kernel modules that don't currently have a CVE</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>List filesystem kernel modules that are not fully disabled, or are loaded into the kernel</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>Review the generated output</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#! /usr/bin/env bash

{
   a_output=(); a_output2=(); a_modprope_config=(); a_excluded=(); a_available_modules=()
   a_ignore=("xfs" "vfat" "ext2" "ext3" "ext4")
   a_cve_exists=("afs" "ceph" "cifs" "exfat" "ext" "fat" "fscache" "fuse" "gfs2" "nfs_common" "nfsd" "smbfs_common")
   f_module_chk()
   {
      l_out2=""; grep -Pq -- "\b$l_mod_name\b" <<< "${a_cve_exists[*]}" && l_out2=" <- CVE exists!"
      if ! grep -Pq -- '\bblacklist\h+'"$l_mod_name"'\b' <<< "${a_modprope_config[*]}"; then
         a_output2+=("  - Kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\" is not fully disabled $l_out2")
      elif ! grep -Pq -- '\binstall\h+'"$l_mod_name"'\h+(\/usr)?\/bin\/(false|true)\b' <<< "${a_modprope_config[*]}"; then
         a_output2+=("  - Kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\" is not fully disabled $l_out2")
      fi
      if lsmod | grep "$l_mod_name" &> /dev/null; then # Check if the module is currently loaded
         l_output2+=("  - Kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\" is loaded" "")
      fi
   }
   while IFS= read -r -d $'\0' l_module_dir; do
      a_available_modules+=("$(basename "$l_module_dir")")
   done < <(find "$(readlink -f /lib/modules/"$(uname -r)"/kernel/fs)" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d ! -empty -print0)
   while IFS= read -r l_exclude; do
      if grep -Pq -- "\b$l_exclude\b" <<< "${a_cve_exists[*]}"; then
         a_output2+=("  - ** WARNING: kernel module: \"$l_exclude\" has a CVE and is currently mounted! **")
      elif 
         grep -Pq -- "\b$l_exclude\b" <<< "${a_available_modules[*]}"; then
         a_output+=("  - Kernel module: \"$l_exclude\" is currently mounted - do NOT unload or disable")
      fi
      ! grep -Pq -- "\b$l_exclude\b" <<< "${a_ignore[*]}" && a_ignore+=("$l_exclude")
   done < <(findmnt -knD | awk '{print $2}' | sort -u)
   while IFS= read -r l_config; do
      a_modprope_config+=("$l_config")
   done < <(modprobe --showconfig | grep -P '^\h*(blacklist|install)')
   for l_mod_name in "${a_available_modules[@]}"; do # Iterate over all filesystem modules
      [[ "$l_mod_name" =~ overlay ]] && l_mod_name="${l_mod_name::-2}"
      if grep -Pq -- "\b$l_mod_name\b" <<< "${a_ignore[*]}"; then
         a_excluded+=(" - Kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\"")
      else
         f_module_chk
      fi
   done
   [ "${#a_excluded[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "" " -- INFO --" \
   "The following intentionally skipped" \
    "${a_excluded[@]}"
   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "" "  - No unused filesystem kernel modules are enabled" "${a_output[@]}" ""
   else
      printf '%s\n' "" "-- Audit Result: --" "  ** REVIEW the following **" "${a_output2[@]}"
      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "" "-- Correctly set: --" "${a_output[@]}" ""
   fi
}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>WARNING</xhtml:strong>: disabling or denylisting filesystem modules that are in use on the system may be FATAL. It is extremely important to thoroughly review this list.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Group.title: Configure Filesystem Partitions
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>Directories that are used for system-wide functions can be further protected by placing them on separate partitions. This provides protection for resource exhaustion and enables the use of mounting options that are applicable to the directory's intended use. Users' data can be stored on separate partitions and have stricter mount options. A user partition is a filesystem that has been established for use by the users and does not contain software for system operations.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The recommendations in this section are easier to perform during initial system installation. If the system is already installed, it is recommended that a full backup be performed before repartitioning the system.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>-IF-</xhtml:strong> you are repartitioning a system that has already been installed (This may require the system to be in single-user mode):</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Mount the new partition to a temporary mountpoint e.g. <xhtml:span class="inline_block">mount /dev/sda2 /mnt</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Copy data from the original partition to the new partition. e.g. <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cp -a /var/tmp/* /mnt</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Verify that all data is present on the new partition. e.g. <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ls -la /mnt</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Unmount the new partition. e.g. <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umount /mnt</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Remove the data from the original directory that was in the old partition. e.g. <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rm -Rf /var/tmp/*</xhtml:span> Otherwise it will still consume space in the old partition that will be masked when the new filesystem is mounted.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Mount the new partition to the desired mountpoint. e.g. <xhtml:span class="inline_block">mount /dev/sda2 /var/tmp</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Update <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/fstab</xhtml:span> with the new mountpoint. e.g. <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/dev/sda2  /var/tmp  xfs   defaults,rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime 0 0</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

Group.title: Configure /tmp
Group.description: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span> directory is a world-writable directory used to store data used by the system and user applications for a short period of time. This data should have no expectation of surviving a reboot, as this directory is intended to be emptied after each reboot.</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure /tmp is a separate partition
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span> directory is a world-writable directory used for temporary storage by all users and some applications.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> an entry for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span> exists in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/fstab</xhtml:span> it will take precedence over entries in systemd default unit file.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> In an environment where the main system is diskless and connected to iSCSI, entries in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/fstab</xhtml:span> may not take precedence.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span> can be configured to use <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tmpfs</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">tmpfs</xhtml:span> puts everything into the kernel internal caches and grows and shrinks to accommodate the files it contains and is able to swap unneeded pages out to swap space. It has maximum size limits which can be adjusted on the fly via <xhtml:span class="inline_block">mount -o remount</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Since <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tmpfs</xhtml:span> lives completely in the page cache and on swap, all <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tmpfs</xhtml:span> pages will be shown as "Shmem" in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/proc/meminfo</xhtml:span> and "Shared" in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">free</xhtml:span>. Notice that these counters also include shared memory. The most reliable way to get the count is using <xhtml:span class="inline_block">df</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">du</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">tmpfs</xhtml:span> has three mount options for sizing:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">size</xhtml:span>: The limit of allocated bytes for this <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tmpfs</xhtml:span> instance. The default is half of your physical RAM without swap. If you oversize your <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tmpfs</xhtml:span> instances the machine will deadlock since the OOM handler will not be able to free that memory.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">nr_blocks</xhtml:span>: The same as size, but in blocks of PAGE_SIZE.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">nr_inodes</xhtml:span>: The maximum number of inodes for this instance. The default is half of the number of your physical RAM pages, or (on a machine with highmem) the number of lowmem RAM pages, whichever is the lower.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>These parameters accept a suffix k, m or g and can be changed on remount. The size parameter also accepts a suffix % to limit this <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tmpfs</xhtml:span> instance to that percentage of your physical RAM. The default, when neither <xhtml:span class="inline_block">size</xhtml:span> nor <xhtml:span class="inline_block">nr_blocks</xhtml:span> is specified, is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">size=50%</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software
Ensure Only Approved Ports, Protocols and Services Are Running

Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>Making <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span> its own file system allows an administrator to set additional mount options such as the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">noexec</xhtml:span> option on the mount, making <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span> useless for an attacker to install executable code. It would also prevent an attacker from establishing a hard link to a system <xhtml:span class="inline_block">setuid</xhtml:span> program and wait for it to be updated. Once the program was updated, the hard link would be broken, and the attacker would have his own copy of the program. If the program happened to have a security vulnerability, the attacker could continue to exploit the known flaw.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>This can be accomplished by either mounting <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tmpfs</xhtml:span> to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span>, or creating a separate partition for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>First ensure that systemd is correctly configured to ensure that <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span> will be mounted at boot time.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl unmask tmp.mount
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>For specific configuration requirements of the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span> mount for your environment, modify <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/fstab</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Example of using <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tmpfs</xhtml:span> with specific mount options:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">tmpfs	/tmp	tmpfs     defaults,rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime,size=2G  0 0
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">size=2G</xhtml:span> is an example of setting a specific size for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tmpfs</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Example of using a volume or disk with specific mount options. The source location of the volume or disk will vary depending on your environment:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"><device> /tmp    <fstype>    defaults,nodev,nosuid,noexec   0 0
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>By design files saved to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span> should have no expectation of surviving a reboot of the system. <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tmpfs</xhtml:span> is ram based and all files stored to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tmpfs</xhtml:span> will be lost when the system is rebooted.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>If files need to be persistent through a reboot, they should be saved to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/var/tmp</xhtml:span> not <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Since the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span> directory is intended to be world-writable, there is a risk of resource exhaustion if it is not bound to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tmpfs</xhtml:span> or a separate partition.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Running out of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span> space is a problem regardless of what kind of filesystem lies under it, but in a configuration where <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span> is not a separate file system it will essentially have the whole disk available, as the default installation only creates a single <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/</xhtml:span> partition. On the other hand, a RAM-based <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span> (as with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tmpfs</xhtml:span>) will almost certainly be much smaller, which can lead to applications filling up the filesystem much more easily. Another alternative is to create a dedicated partition for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span> from a separate volume or disk. One of the downsides of a disk-based dedicated partition is that it will be slower than <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tmpfs</xhtml:span> which is RAM-based.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command and verify the output shows that <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span> is mounted. Particular requirements pertaining to mount options are covered in ensuing sections.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># findmnt -kn /tmp
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example output:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">/tmp   tmpfs  tmpfs  rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Ensure that systemd will mount the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span> partition at boot time.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl is-enabled tmp.mount
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example output:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">generated
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Verify output is not <xhtml:span class="inline_block">masked</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">disabled</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> By default, systemd will output <xhtml:span class="inline_block">generated</xhtml:span> if there is an entry in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/fstab</xhtml:span> for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span>. This just means systemd will use the entry in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/fstab</xhtml:span> instead of its default unit file configuration for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

<xhtml:p>Making <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/dev/shm</xhtml:span> its own file system allows an administrator to set additional mount options such as the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">noexec</xhtml:span> option on the mount, making <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/dev/shm</xhtml:span> useless for an attacker to install executable code. Group.title: Configure /home
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>Please note that home directories can be mounted anywhere and are not necessarily restricted to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/home</xhtml:span>, nor restricted to a single location, nor is the name restricted in any way.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Finding user home directories can be done by looking in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span>, looking over the mounted file systems with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">mount</xhtml:span> or querying the relevant database with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">getent</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">for user in $(awk -F ':' '{print $1}' /etc/passwd); do echo "${user} - $(sudo getent passwd ${user} | awk -F ':' '{print $NF}')"; done
</xhtml:code>

Protect Information through  Access Control Lists

metadata.notes: <xhtml:p>When modifying <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/home</xhtml:span> it is advisable to bring the system to emergency mode (so auditd is not running), rename the existing directory, mount the new file system, and migrate the data over before returning to multi-user mode.</xhtml:p>

<xhtml:p>The default installation only creates a single <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/</xhtml:span> partition. Since the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/home</xhtml:span> directory contains user generated data, there is a risk of resource exhaustion. It will essentially have the whole disk available to fill up and impact the system as a whole. In addition, other operations on the system could fill up the disk unrelated to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/home</xhtml:span> and impact all local users.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Configuring <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/home</xhtml:span> as its own file system allows an administrator to set additional mount options such as <xhtml:span class="inline_block">noexec/nosuid/nodev</xhtml:span>. These options limit an attacker's ability to create exploits on the system. In the case of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/home</xhtml:span> options such as <xhtml:span class="inline_block">usrquota/grpquota</xhtml:span> may be considered to limit the impact that users can have on each other with regards to disk resource exhaustion. Other options allow for specific behavior. See <xhtml:span class="inline_block">man mount</xhtml:span> for exact details regarding filesystem-independent and filesystem-specific options.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>As <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/home</xhtml:span> contains user data, care should be taken to ensure the security and integrity of the data and mount point.</xhtml:p>

<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>For new installations, during installation create a custom partition setup and specify a separate partition for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/home</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>For systems that were previously installed, create a new partition and configure <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/fstab</xhtml:span> as appropriate.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Resizing filesystems is a common activity in cloud-hosted servers. Separate filesystem partitions may prevent successful resizing or may require the installation of additional tools solely for the purpose of resizing operations. </xhtml:p>

In addition, other operations on the system could fill up the disk unrelated to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/var/log/audit</xhtml:span> and cause <xhtml:span class="inline_block">auditd</xhtml:span> to trigger its <xhtml:span class="inline_block">space_left_action</xhtml:span> as the disk is full. See <xhtml:span class="inline_block">man auditd.conf</xhtml:span> for details.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Configuring <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/var/log/audit</xhtml:span> as its own file system allows an administrator to set additional mount options such as <xhtml:span class="inline_block">noexec/nosuid/nodev</xhtml:span>. These options limit an attacker's ability to create exploits on the system. Other options allow for specific behavior. See <xhtml:span class="inline_block">man mount</xhtml:span> for exact details regarding filesystem-independent and filesystem-specific options.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>As <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/var/log/audit</xhtml:span> contains audit logs, care should be taken to ensure the security and integrity of the data and mount point.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>For new installations, during installation create a custom partition setup and specify a separate partition for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/var/log/audit</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>For systems that were previously installed, create a new partition and configure <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/fstab</xhtml:span> as appropriate.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Resizing filesystems is a common activity in cloud-hosted servers. Separate filesystem partitions may prevent successful resizing or may require the installation of additional tools solely for the purpose of resizing operations. The use of these additional tools may introduce their own security considerations.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Group.title: Package Management
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>Patch management procedures may vary widely between enterprises. Large enterprises may choose to install a local updates server that can be used in place of their distributions servers, whereas a single deployment of a system may prefer to get updates directly. Updates can be performed automatically or manually, depending on the site's policy for patch management. Organizations may prefer to test patches against their environment on a non-production system before rolling out to production.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Outdated software is vulnerable to cyber criminals and hackers. Software updates help reduce the risk to your organization. The release of software update notes often reveals the patched exploitable entry points to the public. Public knowledge of these exploits can make your organization more vulnerable to malicious actors attempting to gain entry to your system's data.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Software updates often offer new and improved features and speed enhancements.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>For the purpose of this benchmark, the requirement is to ensure that a patch management process is defined and maintained, the specifics of which are left to the organization.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>It is important to ensure that updates are obtained from a valid source to protect against spoofing that could lead to the inadvertent installation of malware on the system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Update your package manager GPG keys in accordance with site policy.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Verify GPG keys are configured correctly for your package manager:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># apt-key list
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">apt-key list</xhtml:span> is deprecated. Manage keyring files in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">trusted.gpg.d</xhtml:span> instead (see apt-key(8)).</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>With the deprecation of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">apt-key</xhtml:span> it is recommended to use the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Signed-By</xhtml:span> option in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sources.list</xhtml:span> to require a repository to pass apt-secure(8) verification with a certain set of keys rather than all trusted keys apt has configured.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:li>Run the following script and verify GPG keys are configured correctly for your package manager:</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#! /usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   for file in /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/*.{gpg,asc} /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*.{gpg,asc} ; do<br />      if [ -f "$file" ]; then<br />         echo -e "File: $file"<br />         gpg --list-packets "$file" 2>/dev/null | awk '/keyid/ && !seen[$NF]++ {print "keyid:", $NF}'<br />         gpg --list-packets "$file" 2>/dev/null | awk '/Signed-By:/ {print "signed-by:", $NF}'<br />         echo -e<br />      fi<br />   done<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:ol start="2">
<xhtml:li>REVIEW and VERIFY to ensure that GPG keys are configured correctly for your package manager IAW site policy.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

metadata.notes:
<xhtml:p>Site policy may mandate a testing period before installation onto production systems for available updates.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>upgrade - is used to install the newest versions of all packages currently installed on the system from the sources enumerated in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/apt/sources.list</xhtml:span> - OR - <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources</xhtml:span>. Packages currently installed with new versions available are retrieved and upgraded; under no  circumstances are currently installed packages removed, or packages not already installed retrieved and installed. New versions of currently installed packages that cannot be upgraded without changing the install status of another package will be left at     their current version. An update must be performed first so that apt knows that new versions of packages are available.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>dist-upgrade - in addition to performing the function of upgrade, also intelligently handles changing dependencies with new versions of packages; apt has a "smart" conflict resolution system, and it will attempt to upgrade the most important packages at the expense of less important ones if necessary. So, dist-upgrade command may remove some packages. The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/apt/sources.list</xhtml:span> - OR - <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources</xhtml:span> file contains a list of locations from which to retrieve desired package files. See also apt_preferences(5) for a mechanism for overriding the general settings for individual packages.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Newer patches may contain security enhancements that would not be available through the latest full update. As a result, it is recommended that the latest software patches be used to take advantage of the latest functionality. As with any software installation, organizations need to determine if a given update meets their requirements and verify the compatibility and supportability of any additional software against the update revision that is selected.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to update all packages following local site policy guidance on applying updates and patches:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># apt update<br /><br /># apt upgrade<br />  - OR -<br /># apt dist-upgrade
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Verify there are no updates or patches to install:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># apt update<br /># apt -s upgrade
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Group.title: Mandatory Access Control
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>Mandatory Access Control (MAC) provides an additional layer of access restrictions to processes on top of the base Discretionary Access Controls. By restricting how processes can access files and resources on a system the potential impact from vulnerabilities in the processes can be reduced.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Impact:</xhtml:strong> Mandatory Access Control limits the capabilities of applications and daemons on a system, while this can prevent unauthorized access the configuration of MAC can be complex and difficult to implement correctly preventing legitimate access from occurring.</xhtml:p>

Group.title: Configure AppArmor
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>AppArmor provides a Mandatory Access Control (MAC) system that greatly augments the default Discretionary Access Control (DAC) model. Under AppArmor MAC rules are applied by file paths instead of by security contexts as in other MAC systems. As such it does not require support in the filesystem and can be applied to network mounted filesystems for example. AppArmor security policies define what system resources applications can access and what privileges they can do so with. This automatically limits the damage that the software can do to files accessible by the calling user. The user does not need to take any action to gain this benefit. For an action to occur, both the traditional DAC permissions must be satisfied as well as the AppArmor MAC rules. The action will not be allowed if either one of these models does not permit the action. In this way, AppArmor rules can only make a system's permissions more restrictive and secure.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>References:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:li>AppArmor Documentation: <xhtml:a href="http://wiki.apparmor.net/index.php/Documentation">http://wiki.apparmor.net/index.php/Documentation</xhtml:a></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Ubuntu AppArmor Documentation: <xhtml:a href="https://help.ubuntu.com/community/AppArmor">https://help.ubuntu.com/community/AppArmor</xhtml:a></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>SUSE AppArmor Documentation: <xhtml:a href="https://www.suse.com/documentation/apparmor/">https://www.suse.com/documentation/apparmor/</xhtml:a></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>

Group.title: Configure Bootloader
Group.description: <xhtml:p>The recommendations in this section focus on securing the bootloader and settings involved in the boot process directly.</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure bootloader password is set
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>Setting the boot loader password will require that anyone rebooting the system must enter a password before being able to set command line boot parameters</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Protect Information through  Access Control Lists

metadata.notes: <xhtml:p>Changes to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/grub.d/10_linux</xhtml:span> may be overwritten during updates to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">grub-common</xhtml:span> package. You should review any changes to this file before rebooting otherwise the system may unexpectedly prompt for a password on the next boot.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Requiring a boot password upon execution of the boot loader will prevent an unauthorized user from entering boot parameters or changing the boot partition. This prevents users from weakening security (e.g. turning off AppArmor at boot time).</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Create an encrypted password with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">grub-mkpasswd-pbkdf2</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grub-mkpasswd-pbkdf2 --iteration-count=600000 --salt=64<br /><br />Enter password: <password><br />Reenter password: <password><br />PBKDF2 hash of your password is <encrypted-password>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Add the following into a custom <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/grub.d</xhtml:span> configuration file:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">cat <<EOF<br />exec tail -n +2 $0<br />set superusers="<username>"<br />password_pbkdf2 <username> <encrypted-password><br />EOF
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>The superuser/user information and password should not be contained in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/grub.d/00_header</xhtml:span> file as this file could be overwritten in a package update.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>If there is a requirement to be able to boot/reboot without entering the password, edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/grub.d/10_linux</xhtml:span> and add <xhtml:span class="inline_block">--unrestricted</xhtml:span> to the line <xhtml:span class="inline_block">CLASS=</xhtml:span></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">CLASS="--class gnu-linux --class gnu --class os --unrestricted"
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to update the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">grub2</xhtml:span> configuration:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># update-grub
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>If password protection is enabled, only the designated superuser can edit a GRUB 2 menu item by pressing "e" or access the GRUB 2 command line by pressing "c"</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>If GRUB 2 is set up to boot automatically to a password-protected menu entry the user has no option to back out of the password prompt to select another menu entry. Holding the SHIFT key will not display the menu in this case. The user must enter the correct username and password. If unable to do so, the configuration files will have to be edited via a LiveCD or other means to fix the problem</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>You can add <xhtml:span class="inline_block">--unrestricted</xhtml:span> to the menu entries to allow the system to boot without entering a password.  A password will still be required to edit menu items.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>More Information:  <xhtml:a href="https://help.ubuntu.com/community/Grub2/Passwords">https://help.ubuntu.com/community/Grub2/Passwords</xhtml:a></xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following commands and verify output matches:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep "^set superusers" /boot/grub/grub.cfg<br /><br />set superusers="<username>"
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># awk -F. '/^\s*password/ {print $1"."$2"."$3}' /boot/grub/grub.cfg<br /><br />password_pbkdf2 <username> grub.pbkdf2.sha512
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure ptrace_scope is restricted
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ptrace()</xhtml:span> system call provides a means by which one process (the "tracer") may observe and control the execution of another process (the "tracee"), and examine and change the tracee's memory and registers.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The sysctl settings (writable only with CAP_SYS_PTRACE) are:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> - classic ptrace permissions: a process can PTRACE_ATTACH to any other process running under the same uid, as long as it is dumpable (i.e. did not transition uids, start privileged, or have called prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE...) already). Similarly, PTRACE_TRACEME is unchanged.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">1</xhtml:span> - restricted ptrace: a process must have a predefined relationship with the inferior it wants to call PTRACE_ATTACH on. By default, this relationship is that of only its descendants when the above classic criteria is also met. To change the relationship, an inferior can call prctl(PR_SET_PTRACER, debugger, ...) to declare an allowed debugger PID to call PTRACE_ATTACH on the inferior. Using PTRACE_TRACEME is unchanged.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">2</xhtml:span> - admin-only attach: only processes with CAP_SYS_PTRACE may use ptrace with PTRACE_ATTACH, or through children calling PTRACE_TRACEME.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">3</xhtml:span> - no attach: no processes may use ptrace with PTRACE_ATTACH nor via PTRACE_TRACEME. Once set, this sysctl value cannot be changed.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

safeguard.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software
Ensure Only Approved Ports, Protocols and Services Are Running

metadata.notes: <xhtml:p>Ptrace is very rarely used by regular applications and is mostly used by debuggers such as <xhtml:span class="inline_block">gdb</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">strace</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>If one application is compromised, it would be possible for an attacker to attach to other running processes (e.g. Bash, Firefox, SSH sessions, GPG agent, etc) to extract additional credentials and continue to expand the scope of their attack.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Enabling restricted mode will limit the ability of a compromised process to PTRACE_ATTACH on other processes running under the same user. With restricted mode, ptrace will continue to work with root user.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Set the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">kernel.yama.ptrace_scope</xhtml:span> parameter in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.conf</xhtml:span> or a file in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.d/</xhtml:span> ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> to a value of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">1</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">2</xhtml:span>, or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">3</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">kernel.yama.ptrace_scope = 1<br />    - OR -<br />kernel.yama.ptrace_scope = 2<br />    - OR -<br />kernel.yama.ptrace_scope = 3
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># printf "%s\n" "kernel.yama.ptrace_scope = 1" >> /etc/sysctl.d/60-kernel_sysctl.conf
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to set the active kernel parameter:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># sysctl -w kernel.yama.ptrace_scope=1
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>If a value of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">2</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">3</xhtml:span> is preferred, or required by local site policy, replace the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">1</xhtml:span> with the desired value of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">2</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">3</xhtml:span> in the example above</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>If this setting appears in a canonically later file, or later in the same file, the setting will be overwritten</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure core dumps are restricted
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>A core dump is the memory of an executable program. It is generally used to determine why a program aborted. It can also be used to glean confidential information from a core file. The system provides the ability to set a soft limit for core dumps, but this can be overridden by the user.</xhtml:p>
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Setting a hard limit on core dumps prevents users from overriding the soft variable. If core dumps are required, consider setting limits for user groups (see <xhtml:span class="inline_block">limits.conf(5)</xhtml:span> ). In addition, setting the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">fs.suid_dumpable</xhtml:span>  variable to 0 will prevent setuid programs from dumping core.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Add the following line to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/limits.conf</xhtml:span> or a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/limits.d/*</xhtml:span> file:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">* hard core 0
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Set the following parameter in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.conf</xhtml:span> or a file in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.d/</xhtml:span> ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">fs.suid_dumpable = 0</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>

<xhtml:p>Run the following script to verify the following kernel parameter is set in the running configuration and correctly loaded from a kernel parameter configuration file:</xhtml:p>

<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> kernel parameters are loaded by file and parameter order precedence. The following script observes this precedence as part of the auditing procedure. The parameters being checked may be set correctly in a file. If that file is superseded, the parameter is overridden by an incorrect setting later in that file, or in a canonically later file, that "correct" setting will be ignored both by the script and by the system during a normal kernel parameter load sequence.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_output=(); a_output2=(); a_parlist=("fs.suid_dumpable=0")<br />   l_ufwscf="$([ -f /etc/default/ufw ] && awk -F= '/^\s*IPT_SYSCTL=/ {print $2}' /etc/default/ufw)"<br />   f_kernel_parameter_chk()<br />   {  <br />      l_running_parameter_value="$(sysctl "$l_parameter_name" | awk -F= '{print $2}' | xargs)" # Check running configuration<br />      if grep -Pq -- '\b'"$l_parameter_value"'\b' <<< "$l_running_parameter_value"; then<br />         a_output+=(" - \"$l_parameter_name\" is correctly set to \"$l_running_parameter_value\""<br />         "    in the running configuration")<br />      else<br />         a_output2+=(" - \"$l_parameter_name\" is incorrectly set to \"$l_running_parameter_value\"" \<br />         "    in the running configuration" \<br />         "    and should have a value of: \"$l_value_out\"")<br />      fi<br />      unset A_out; declare -A A_out # Check durable setting (files)<br />      while read -r l_out; do<br />         if [ -n "$l_out" ]; then<br />            if [[ $l_out =~ ^\s*# ]]; then<br />               l_file="${l_out//# /}"<br />            else<br />               l_kpar="$(awk -F= '{print $1}' <<< "$l_out" | xargs)"<br />               [ "$l_kpar" = "$l_parameter_name" ] && A_out+=(["$l_kpar"]="$l_file")<br />            fi<br />         fi<br />      done < <("$l_systemdsysctl" --cat-config | grep -Po '^\h*([^#\n\r]+|#\h*\/[^#\n\r\h]+\.conf\b)')<br />      if [ -n "$l_ufwscf" ]; then # Account for systems with UFW (Not covered by systemd-sysctl --cat-config)<br />         l_kpar="$(grep -Po "^\h*$l_parameter_name\b" "$l_ufwscf" | xargs)"<br />         l_kpar="${l_kpar//\//.}"<br />         [ "$l_kpar" = "$l_parameter_name" ] && A_out+=(["$l_kpar"]="$l_ufwscf")<br />      fi<br />      if (( ${#A_out[@]} > 0 )); then # Assess output from files and generate output<br />         while IFS="=" read -r l_fkpname l_file_parameter_value; do<br />            l_fkpname="${l_fkpname// /}"; l_file_parameter_value="${l_file_parameter_value// /}"<br />            if grep -Pq -- '\b'"$l_parameter_value"'\b' <<< "$l_file_parameter_value"; then<br />               a_output+=(" - \"$l_parameter_name\" is correctly set to \"$l_file_parameter_value\"" \<br />               "    in \"$(printf '%s' "${A_out[@]}")\"")<br />            else<br />               a_output2+=(" - \"$l_parameter_name\" is incorrectly set to \"$l_file_parameter_value\""<br />               "    in \"$(printf '%s' "${A_out[@]}")\"" \<br />               "    and should have a value of: \"$l_value_out\"")<br />            fi<br />         done < <(grep -Po -- "^\h*$l_parameter_name\h*=\h*\H+" "${A_out[@]}")<br />      else<br />         a_output2+=(" - \"$l_parameter_name\" is not set in an included file" \<br />         "    ** Note: \"$l_parameter_name\" May be set in a file that's ignored by load procedure **")<br />      fi<br />   }<br />   l_systemdsysctl="$(readlink -f /lib/systemd/systemd-sysctl)"<br />   while IFS="=" read -r l_parameter_name l_parameter_value; do # Assess and check parameters<br />      l_parameter_name="${l_parameter_name// /}"; l_parameter_value="${l_parameter_value// /}"<br />      l_value_out="${l_parameter_value//-/ through }"; l_value_out="${l_value_out//|/ or }"<br />      l_value_out="$(tr -d '(){}' <<< "$l_value_out")"<br />      f_kernel_parameter_chk<br />   done < <(printf '%s\n' "${a_parlist[@]}")<br />   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}" ""<br />   else<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" " - Reason(s) for audit failure:" "${a_output2[@]}"<br />      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "" "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}" ""<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to check if systemd-coredump is installed:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl list-unit-files | grep coredump
</xhtml:code>

Group.title: Configure Command Line Warning Banners
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>Presenting a warning message prior to the normal user login may assist in the prosecution of trespassers on the computer system. Changing some of these login banners also has the side effect of hiding OS version information and other detailed system information from attackers attempting to target specific exploits at a system.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Guidelines published by the US Department of Defense require that warning messages include at least the name of the organization that owns the system, the fact that the system is subject to monitoring and that such monitoring is in compliance with local statutes, and that use of the system implies consent to such monitoring. It is important that the organization's legal counsel review the content of all messages before any system modifications are made, as these warning messages are inherently site-specific. More information (including citations of relevant case law) can be found at <xhtml:a href="http://www.justice.gov/criminal/cybercrime/">http://www.justice.gov/criminal/cybercrime/</xhtml:a></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/motd</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/issue</xhtml:span>, and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/issue.net</xhtml:span> files govern warning banners for standard command line logins for both local and remote users.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> The text provided in the remediation actions for these items is intended as an example only. Please edit to include the specific text for your organization as approved by your legal department.</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure message of the day is configured properly
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>The contents of the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/motd</xhtml:span>  file are displayed to users after login and function as a message of the day for authenticated users.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Unix-based systems have typically displayed information about the OS release and patch level upon logging in to the system. This information can be useful to developers who are developing software for a particular OS platform. If <xhtml:span class="inline_block">mingetty(8)</xhtml:span> supports the following options, they display operating system information: <xhtml:span class="inline_block">\m</xhtml:span>  - machine architecture <xhtml:span class="inline_block">\r</xhtml:span>  - operating system release <xhtml:span class="inline_block">\s</xhtml:span>  - operating system name <xhtml:span class="inline_block">\v</xhtml:span>  - operating system version</xhtml:p>
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Warning messages inform users who are attempting to login to the system of their legal status regarding the system and must include the name of the organization that owns the system and any monitoring policies that are in place. Displaying OS and patch level information in login banners also has the side effect of providing detailed system information to attackers attempting to target specific exploits of a system. Authorized users can easily get this information by running the " <xhtml:span class="inline_block">uname -a</xhtml:span> " command once they have logged in.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: CM-6, CM-1, CM-3

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/motd</xhtml:span>  file with the appropriate contents according to your site policy, remove any instances of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">\m</xhtml:span> , <xhtml:span class="inline_block">\r</xhtml:span> , <xhtml:span class="inline_block">\s</xhtml:span> , <xhtml:span class="inline_block">\v</xhtml:span> or references to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">OS platform</xhtml:span></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">motd</xhtml:span> is not used, this file can be removed.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to remove the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">motd</xhtml:span> file:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># rm /etc/motd
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command and verify that the contents match site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># cat /etc/motd
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command and verify no results are returned:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -E -i "(\\\v|\\\r|\\\m|\\\s|$(grep '^ID=' /etc/os-release | cut -d= -f2 | sed -e 's/"//g'))" /etc/motd
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Group.title: Configure GNOME Display Manager
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>The GNOME Display Manager (GDM) is a program that manages graphical display servers and handles graphical user logins.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>This subsection requires user profiles to already exist on the system. A profile is a list of configuration databases.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Sample profile:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">user-db:user<br />system-db:local<br />system-db:site
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Configuring a single user and multiple system databases allows for layering of preferences. Settings from the user database file take precedence over the settings in the local database file, and the local database file in turn takes precedence over the site database file.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> GDM is not installed on the system, this section can be skipped</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The Remediation Procedure commands in this section <xhtml:strong>MUST</xhtml:strong> be done from a command window on a graphical desktop or an error will be returned.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

Rule.title: Ensure GDM login banner is configured
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>GDM is the GNOME Display Manager which handles graphical login for GNOME based systems.</xhtml:p>

metadata.notes:
<xhtml:p>Additional options and sections may appear in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/dconf/db/gdm.d/01-banner-message</xhtml:span> file.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>If a different GUI login service is in use, consult your documentation and apply an equivalent banner.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Warning messages inform users who are attempting to login to the system of their legal status regarding the system and must include the name of the organization that owns the system and any monitoring policies that are in place.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: CM-1,CM-2, CM-6, CM-7, IA-5

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> A user profile is already created run the following commands to set and enable the text banner message on the login screen:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># gsettings set org.gnome.login-screen banner-message-text 'Authorized uses only. All activity may be monitored and reported'
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># gsettings set org.gnome.login-screen banner-message-enable true
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">banner-message-text</xhtml:span> may be set in accordance with local site policy</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">gsettings</xhtml:span> commands in this section MUST be done from a command window on a graphical desktop or an error will be returned.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The system must be restarted after all <xhtml:span class="inline_block">gsettings</xhtml:span> configurations have been set in order for CIS-CAT Assessor to appropriately assess.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- OR/IF -</xhtml:strong> A user profile does not exist:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:li>Create or edit the gdm profile in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/dconf/profile/gdm</xhtml:span> with the following lines:</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">user-db:user<br />system-db:gdm<br />file-db:/usr/share/gdm/greeter-dconf-defaults
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> gdm is the name of a dconf database.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ol start="2">
<xhtml:li>Create a gdm keyfile for machine-wide settings in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/dconf/db/gdm.d/01-banner-message</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">[org/gnome/login-screen]<br />banner-message-enable=true<br />banner-message-text='Type the banner message here.'
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:ol start="3">
<xhtml:li>Update the system databases</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># dconf update
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Users must log out and back in again before the system-wide settings take effect.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>There is no character limit for the banner message. gnome-shell autodetects longer stretches of text and enters two column mode.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The banner message cannot be read from an external file.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following commands to verify that the text banner on the login screen is enabled and set:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># gsettings get org.gnome.login-screen banner-message-enable <br />true
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># gsettings get org.gnome.login-screen banner-message-text <br />'Authorized uses only. All activity may be monitored and reported'
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure GDM screen locks when the user is idle
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>GNOME Desktop Manager can make the screen lock automatically whenever the user is idle for some amount of time.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Configure Automatic Session Locking on Enterprise Assets
Lock Workstation Sessions After Inactivity

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Setting a lock-out value reduces the window of opportunity for unauthorized user access to another user's session that has been left unattended.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> A user profile is already created run the following commands to enable screen locks when the user is idle:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.screensaver lock-delay 5
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.session idle-delay 900
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">gsettings</xhtml:span> commands in this section MUST be done from a command window on a graphical desktop or an error will be returned.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The system must be restarted after all <xhtml:span class="inline_block">gsettings</xhtml:span> configurations have been set in order for CIS-CAT Assessor to appropriately assess.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- OR/IF-</xhtml:strong> A user profile does not exist:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:li>Create or edit the user profile in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/dconf/profile/</xhtml:span> and verify it includes the following:</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">user-db:user<br />system-db:{NAME_OF_DCONF_DATABASE}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">local</xhtml:span> is the name of a dconf database used in the examples.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ol start="2">
<xhtml:li>
<xhtml:p>Create the directory <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/dconf/db/local.d/</xhtml:span> if it doesn't already exist:</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>
<xhtml:p>Create the key file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/dconf/db/local.d/00-screensaver</xhtml:span> to provide information for the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">local</xhtml:span> database:</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example key file:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># Specify the dconf path<br />[org/gnome/desktop/session]<br /><br /># Number of seconds of inactivity before the screen goes blank<br /># Set to 0 seconds if you want to deactivate the screensaver.<br />idle-delay=uint32 180<br /><br /># Specify the dconf path<br />[org/gnome/desktop/screensaver]<br /><br /># Number of seconds after the screen is blank before locking the screen<br />lock-delay=uint32 0
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> You must include the uint32 along with the integer key values as shown.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ol start="4">
<xhtml:li>Run the following command to update the system databases:</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># dconf update
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:ol start="5">
<xhtml:li>Users must log out and back in again before the system-wide settings take effect.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following commands to verify that the screen locks when the user is idle:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.screensaver lock-delay<br />uint32 5
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.session idle-delay<br />uint32 900
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Notes:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">lock-delay=uint32 {n}</xhtml:span> - should be 5 seconds or less and follow local site policy</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">idle-delay=uint32 {n}</xhtml:span> - Should be 900 seconds (15 minutes) or less, not <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> (disabled) and follow local site policy</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure GDM screen locks cannot be overridden
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>GNOME Desktop Manager can lock down specific settings by using the lockdown mode in dconf to prevent users from changing specific settings.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>To lock down a dconf key or subpath,  create a locks subdirectory in the keyfile directory. The files inside this directory contain a list of keys or subpaths to lock. Just as with the keyfiles, you may add any number of files to this directory.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Configure Automatic Session Locking on Enterprise Assets
Lock Workstation Sessions After Inactivity

Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>Setting a lock-out value reduces the window of opportunity for unauthorized user access to another user's session that has been left unattended.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Without locking down the system settings, user settings take precedence over the system settings.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:li>To prevent the user from overriding these settings, create the file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/dconf/db/local.d/locks/00-screensaver</xhtml:span> with the following content:</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># Lock desktop screensaver settings<br />/org/gnome/desktop/session/idle-delay<br />/org/gnome/desktop/screensaver/lock-delay
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:ol start="2">
<xhtml:li>Update the system databases:</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># dconf update
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>A user profile must exist in order to apply locks.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Users must log out and back in again before the system-wide settings take effect.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to verify that the screen lock cannot be overridden:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_output=() a_output2=()<br />   f_check_setting() <br />   {<br />      grep -Psrilq -- "^\h*$2 " /etc/dconf/db/local.d/locks/* && \<br />      echo "- "$3" is locked" || echo "- "$3" is not locked or not set"<br />   }<br />   declare -A settings=(<br />      ["idle-delay"]="/org/gnome/desktop/session/idle-delay"<br />      ["lock-delay"]="/org/gnome/desktop/screensaver/lock-delay"<br />   )<br />   for setting in "${!settings[@]}"; do<br />      result=$(f_check_setting "$setting" "${settings[$setting]}" "$setting")<br />      if [[ $result == *"is not locked"* || $result == *"not set to false"* ]]; then<br />         a_output2+=("$result")<br />      else<br />         a_output+=("$result")<br />      fi<br />   done<br />   printf '%s
' "" "- Audit Result:"<br />   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then<br />      printf '%s
' "  ** FAIL **" " - Reason(s) for audit failure:" "${a_output2[@]}"<br />      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s
' "" "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}"<br />   else<br />      printf '%s
' "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}"<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

safeguard.title: Disable Autorun and Autoplay for Removable Media

<xhtml:li>The system must be restarted after all <xhtml:span class="inline_block">gsettings</xhtml:span> configurations have been set in order for CIS-CAT Assessor to appropriately assess.</xhtml:li>

<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- OR/IF -</xhtml:strong> A user profile does not exist:</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure XDMCP is not enabled
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>X Display Manager Control Protocol (XDMCP) is designed to provide authenticated access to display management services for remote displays</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software
