Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>XDMCP is inherently insecure.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>XDMCP is not a ciphered protocol. This may allow an attacker to capture keystrokes entered by a user</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>XDMCP is vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks. This may allow an attacker to steal the credentials of legitimate users by impersonating the XDMCP server.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit all files returned by the audit and remove or commend out the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Enable=true</xhtml:span> line in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">[xdmcp]</xhtml:span> block:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example file:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># GDM configuration storage<br />#<br /># See /usr/share/gdm/gdm.schemas for a list of available options.<br /><br />[daemon]<br /># Uncomment the line below to force the login screen to use Xorg<br />#WaylandEnable=false<br /><br /># Enabling automatic login<br />#  AutomaticLoginEnable = true<br />#  AutomaticLogin = user1<br /><br /># Enabling timed login<br />#  TimedLoginEnable = true<br />#  TimedLogin = user1<br />#  TimedLoginDelay = 10<br /><br />[security]<br /><br />[xdmcp]<br /># Enable=true <- **This line should be removed or commented out**<br /><br />[chooser]<br /><br />[debug]<br /># Uncomment the line below to turn on debugging<br /># More verbose logs<br /># Additionally lets the X server dump core if it crashes<br />#Enable=true
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script and verify the output:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   while IFS= read -r l_file; do<br />      awk '/\[xdmcp\]/{ f = 1;next } /\[/{ f = 0 } f {if (/^\s*Enable\s*=\s*true/) print "The file: \"'"$l_file"'\" includes: \"" $0 "\" in the \"[xdmcp]\" block"}' "$l_file"<br />   done < <(grep -Psil -- '^\h*\[xdmcp\]' /etc/{gdm3,gdm}/{custom,daemon}.conf)<br />}

Group.title: Services
Group.description: <xhtml:p>While applying system updates and patches helps correct known vulnerabilities, one of the best ways to protect the system against as yet unreported vulnerabilities is to disable all services that are not required for normal system operation. This prevents the exploitation of vulnerabilities discovered at a later date. If a service is not enabled, it cannot be exploited. The actions in this section of the document provide guidance on some services which can be safely disabled and under which circumstances, greatly reducing the number of possible threats to the resulting system. Additionally, some services which should remain enabled but with secure configuration are covered as well as insecure service clients.</xhtml:p>

Group.title: Configure Server Services
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>This section describes services that are installed on systems that specifically need to run these services. If any of these services are not required, it is recommended that the package be removed.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> the package is required for a dependency:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Ensure the dependent package is approved by local site policy</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Ensure stopping and masking the service and/or socket meets local site policy</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Stop and mask the service and/or socket to reduce the potential attack surface</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>The following commands can be used to stop and mask the service and socket:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl stop <service_name>.socket <service_name>.service<br /># systemctl mask <service_name>.socket <service_name>.service
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> This should not be considered a comprehensive list of services not required for normal system operation. You may wish to consider additions to those listed here for your environment</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure autofs services are not in use
Rule.description: <xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">autofs</xhtml:span> allows automatic mounting of devices, typically including CD/DVDs and USB drives.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Disable Autorun and Autoplay for Removable Media
Configure Devices Not To Auto-run Content

metadata.notes: <xhtml:p>This control should align with the tolerance of the use of portable drives and optical media in the organization. On a server, requiring an admin to manually mount media can be part of defense-in-depth to reduce the risk of unapproved software or information being introduced or proprietary software or information being exfiltrated. If admins commonly use flash drives and Server access has sufficient physical controls, requiring manual mounting may not increase security.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>With automounting enabled anyone with physical access could attach a USB drive or disc and have its contents available in the filesystem even if they lacked permissions to mount it themselves.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following commands to stop <xhtml:span class="inline_block">autofs.service</xhtml:span> and remove the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">autofs</xhtml:span> package:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl stop autofs.service<br /># apt purge autofs
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">autofs</xhtml:span> package is required as a dependency:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to stop and mask <xhtml:span class="inline_block">autofs.service</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl stop autofs.service<br /># systemctl mask autofs.service
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The use of portable hard drives is very common for workstation users. If your organization allows the use of portable storage or media on workstations and physical access controls to workstations is considered adequate there is little value add in turning off automounting.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>There may be packages that are dependent on the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">autofs</xhtml:span> package.  If the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">autofs</xhtml:span> package is removed, these dependent packages will be removed as well. Before removing the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">autofs</xhtml:span> package, review any dependent packages to determine if they are required on the system.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> a dependent package is required: stop and mask the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">autofs.service</xhtml:span>  leaving the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">autofs</xhtml:span> package installed.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> If the package is required for a dependency</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure rpcbind services are not in use
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rpcbind</xhtml:span> utility maps RPC services to the ports on which they listen. The client system then contacts <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rpcbind</xhtml:span> on the server with a particular RPC program number. The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rpcbind.service</xhtml:span> redirects the client to the proper port number so it can communicate with the requested service.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Portmapper is an RPC service, which always listens on tcp and udp 111, and is used to map other RPC services (such as nfs, nlockmgr, quotad, mountd, etc.) to their corresponding port number on the server. When a remote host makes an RPC call to that server, it first consults with portmap to determine where the RPC server is listening.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software
Ensure Only Approved Ports, Protocols and Services Are Running

Rule.title: Ensure tftp server services are not in use
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP) is a simple protocol for exchanging files between two TCP/IP machines. TFTP servers allow connections from a TFTP Client for sending and receiving files.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software
Ensure Only Approved Ports, Protocols and Services Are Running

Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>Unless there is a need to run the system as a TFTP server, it is recommended that the package be removed to reduce the potential attack surface.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>TFTP does not have built-in encryption, access control or authentication. This makes it very easy for an attacker to exploit TFTP to gain access to files</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following commands to stop <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tftpd-hpa.service</xhtml:span>, and remove the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tftpd-hpa</xhtml:span> package:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl stop tftpd-hpa.service<br /># apt purge tftpd-hpa
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tftpd-hpa</xhtml:span> package is required as a dependency:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to stop and mask <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tftpd-hpa.service</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl stop tftpd-hpa.service<br /># systemctl mask tftpd-hpa.service
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>TFTP is often used to provide files for network booting such as for PXE based installation of servers.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>There may be packages that are dependent on the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tftpd-hpa</xhtml:span> package.  If the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tftpd-hpa</xhtml:span> package is removed, these dependent packages will be removed as well. Before removing the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tftpd-hpa</xhtml:span> package, review any dependent packages to determine if they are required on the system.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> a dependent package is required: stop and mask <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tftpd-hpa.service</xhtml:span> leaving the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">tftpd-hpa</xhtml:span> package installed.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software

Rule.title: Ensure mail transfer agent is configured for local-only mode
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>Mail Transfer Agents (MTA), such as sendmail and Postfix, are used to listen for incoming mail and transfer the messages to the appropriate user or mail server. If the system is not intended to be a mail server, it is recommended that the MTA be configured to only process local mail.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software
Ensure Only Approved Ports, Protocols and Services Are Running

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>The software for all Mail Transfer Agents is complex and most have a long history of security issues. While it is important to ensure that the system can process local mail messages, it is not necessary to have the MTA's daemon listening on a port unless the server is intended to be a mail server that receives and processes mail from other systems.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/postfix/main.cf</xhtml:span> and add the following line to the RECEIVING MAIL section. If the line already exists, change it to look like the line below:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">inet_interfaces = loopback-only
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to restart <xhtml:span class="inline_block">postfix</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl restart postfix
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>This recommendation is designed around the postfix mail server.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Depending on your environment you may have an alternative MTA installed such as exim4. If this is the case consult the documentation for your installed MTA to configure the recommended state.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to verify that the MTA is not listening on any non-loopback address ( <xhtml:span class="inline_block">127.0.0.1</xhtml:span>  or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">::1</xhtml:span></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_output=(); a_output2=(); a_port_list=("25" "465" "587")<br />   for l_port_number in "${a_port_list[@]}"; do<br />      if ss -plntu | grep -P -- ':'"$l_port_number"'\b' | grep -Pvq -- '\h+(127\.0\.0\.1|\[?::1\]?):'"$l_port_number"'\b'; then<br />         a_output2+=(" - Port \"$l_port_number\" is listening on a non-loopback network interface")<br />      else<br />         a_output+=(" - Port \"$l_port_number\" is not listening on a non-loopback network interface")<br />      fi<br />   done<br />   if command -v postconf &> /dev/null; then<br />      l_interfaces="$(postconf -n inet_interfaces)"<br />   elif command -v exim &> /dev/null; then<br />      l_interfaces="$(exim -bP local_interfaces)"<br />   elif command -v sendmail &> /dev/null; then<br />      l_interfaces="$(grep -i "0 DaemonPortOptions=" /etc/mail/sendmail.cr | grep -oP '?<=Addr=)[^,+]+')"<br />   fi<br />   if [ -n "$l_interfaces" ]; then<br />      if grep -Pqi '\ball\b' <<< "$l_interfaces"; then<br />         a_output2+=(" - MTA is bound to all network interfaces")<br />      elif ! grep -Pqi '(inet_interfaces\h*=\h*)?(0\.0\.0\.0|::1|loopback-only)' <<< "$l_interfaces"; then<br />         a_output2+=(" - MTA is bound to a network interface" "   \"$l_interfaces\"")<br />      else<br />         a_output+=(" - MTA is not bound to a non loopback network interface" "   \"$l_interfaces\"")<br />      fi<br />   else<br />      a_output+=(" - MTA not detected or in use")<br />   fi<br />   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}"<br />   else<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" "  * Reasons for audit failure *" "${a_output2[@]}" ""<br />      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}"<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure only approved services are listening on a network interface
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>A network port is identified by its number, the associated IP address, and the type of the communication protocol such as TCP or UDP.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>A listening port is a network port on which an application or process listens on, acting as a communication endpoint.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Each listening port can be open or closed (filtered) using a firewall. In general terms, an open port is a network port that accepts incoming packets from remote locations.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software
Ensure Only Approved Ports, Protocols and Services Are Running

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Services listening on the system pose a potential risk as an attack vector.  These services should be reviewed, and if not required, the service should be stopped, and the package containing the service should be removed.  If required packages have a dependency, the service should be stopped and masked to reduce the attack surface of the system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following commands to stop the service and remove the package containing the service:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl stop <service_name>.socket <service_name>.service<br /># apt purge <package_name>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong> If required packages have a dependency:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to stop and mask the service and socket:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl stop <service_name>.socket <service_name>.service<br /># systemctl mask <service_name>.socket <service_name>.service
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> replace <xhtml:span class="inline_block"><service_name></xhtml:span> with the appropriate service name.</xhtml:p>

Group.title: Configure Time Synchronization
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>It is recommended that systems be configured to synchronize their time using a service such as <xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-timesyncd</xhtml:span>, or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chrony</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Virtual systems may be configured to receive their time synchronization from their host system.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The host system must be configured to synchronize its time from an authoritative source to be considered compliant with this section.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Any "physical" clock present on a system should be synchronized from an authoritative time source.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Only one time synchronization method should be in use on the system</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Notes:</xhtml:strong> Only the section related to the time synchronization method in use on the system should be followed, all other time synchronization recommendations should be skipped</xhtml:p>

Group.title: Ensure time synchronization is in use
Group.description: <xhtml:p>It is recommended that physical systems and virtual guests lacking direct access to the physical host's clock be configured to synchronize their time using a service such as <xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-timesyncd</xhtml:span>, or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chrony</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure a single time synchronization daemon is in use
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>System time should be synchronized between all systems in an environment. This is typically done by establishing an authoritative time server or set of servers and having all systems synchronize their clocks to them.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:strong>On virtual systems where host based time synchronization is available consult your virtualization software documentation and verify that host based synchronization is in use and follows local site policy. In this scenario, this section should be skipped</xhtml:strong></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Only <xhtml:strong>one</xhtml:strong> time synchronization method should be in use on the system. Configuring multiple time synchronization methods could lead to unexpected or unreliable results</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

safeguard.title: Standardize Time Synchronization
Utilize Three Synchronized Time Sources

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Time synchronization is important to support time sensitive security mechanisms and ensures log files have consistent time records across the enterprise, which aids in forensic investigations.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>On physical systems, and virtual systems where host based time synchronization is not available.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Select <xhtml:strong>one</xhtml:strong> of the two time synchronization daemons; <xhtml:strong><xhtml:span class="inline_block">chrony (1)</xhtml:span></xhtml:strong> or <xhtml:strong><xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-timesyncd (2)</xhtml:span></xhtml:strong> and following the remediation procedure for the selected daemon.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> enabling more than one synchronization daemon could lead to unexpected or unreliable results:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:strong><xhtml:span class="inline_block">chrony</xhtml:span></xhtml:strong></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to install <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chrony</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># apt install chrony 
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to stop and mask the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-timesyncd</xhtml:span> daemon:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl stop systemd-timesyncd.service<br /><br /># systemctl mask systemd-timesyncd.service
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Subsection: <xhtml:strong><xhtml:em>Configure chrony</xhtml:em></xhtml:strong> should be followed</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Subsection: <xhtml:strong><xhtml:em>Configure systemd-timesyncd</xhtml:em></xhtml:strong> should be skipped</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:ol start="2">
<xhtml:li><xhtml:strong><xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-timesyncd</xhtml:span></xhtml:strong></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to remove the chrony package:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># apt purge chrony<br /># apt autoremove chrony
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Subsection: <xhtml:strong><xhtml:em>Configure systemd-timesyncd</xhtml:em></xhtml:strong> should be followed</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Subsection: <xhtml:strong><xhtml:em>Configure chrony</xhtml:em></xhtml:strong> should be skipped</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>On physical systems, and virtual systems where host based time synchronization is not available.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>One</xhtml:strong> of the two time synchronization daemons should be available; <xhtml:strong><xhtml:span class="inline_block">chrony</xhtml:span></xhtml:strong> or <xhtml:strong><xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-timesyncd</xhtml:span></xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following script to verify that a single time synchronization daemon is available on the system:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />    l_output="" l_output2=""<br />    service_not_enabled_chk()<br />    {<br />        l_out2=""<br />        if systemctl is-enabled "$l_service_name" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'enabled'; then<br />            l_out2="$l_out2
  - Daemon: "$l_service_name" is enabled on the system"<br />        fi<br />        if systemctl is-active "$l_service_name" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^active'; then<br />            l_out2="$l_out2
  - Daemon: "$l_service_name" is active on the system"<br />        fi<br />    }   <br />    l_service_name="systemd-timesyncd.service" # Check systemd-timesyncd daemon<br />    service_not_enabled_chk<br />    if [ -n "$l_out2" ]; then<br />        l_timesyncd="y"<br />        l_out_tsd="$l_out2"<br />    else<br />        l_timesyncd="n"<br />        l_out_tsd="
  - Daemon: "$l_service_name" is not enabled and not active on the system"<br />    fi<br />    l_service_name="chrony.service" # Check chrony<br />    service_not_enabled_chk<br />    if [ -n "$l_out2" ]; then<br />        l_chrony="y"<br />        l_out_chrony="$l_out2"<br />    else<br />        l_chrony="n"<br />        l_out_chrony="
  - Daemon: "$l_service_name" is not enabled and not active on the system"<br />    fi<br />    l_status="$l_timesyncd$l_chrony"<br />    case "$l_status" in<br />        yy)<br />            l_output2=" - More than one time sync daemon is in use on the system$l_out_tsd$l_out_chrony"<br />            ;;<br />        nn)<br />            l_output2=" - No time sync daemon is in use on the system$l_out_tsd$l_out_chrony"<br />            ;;<br />        yn|ny)<br />            l_output=" - Only one time sync daemon is in use on the system$l_out_tsd$l_out_chrony"<br />            ;;<br />        *)<br />            l_output2=" - Unable to determine time sync daemon(s) status"<br />            ;;<br />    esac<br /><br />    if [ -z "$l_output2" ]; then<br />        echo -e "
- Audit Result:
  ** PASS **
$l_output
"<br />    else<br />        echo -e "
- Audit Result:
  ** FAIL **
 - * Reasons for audit failure * :
$l_output2
"<br />    fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> Follow the guidance in the subsection for the time synchronization daemon available on the system and skip the other time synchronization daemon subsection.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Group.title: Configure systemd-timesyncd
Group.description:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-timesyncd</xhtml:span> is a daemon that has been added for synchronizing the system clock across the network. It implements an SNTP client. In contrast to NTP implementations such as chrony or the NTP reference server this only implements a client side, and does not bother with the full NTP complexity, focusing only on querying time from one remote server and synchronizing the local clock to it. The daemon runs with minimal privileges, and has been hooked up with networkd to only operate when network connectivity is available. The daemon saves the current clock to disk every time a new NTP sync has been acquired, and uses this to possibly correct the system clock early at bootup, in order to accommodate for systems that lack an RTC such as the Raspberry Pi and embedded devices, and make sure that time monotonically progresses on these systems, even if it is not always correct. To make use of this daemon a new system user and group "systemd-timesync" needs to be created on installation of systemd.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The default configuration is set during compilation, so configuration is only needed when it is necessary to deviate from those defaults. Initially, the main configuration file in /etc/systemd/ contains commented out entries showing the defaults as a guide to the administrator. Local overrides can be created by editing this file or by creating drop-ins, as described below. Using drop-ins for local configuration is recommended over modifications to the main configuration file.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>In addition to the "main" configuration file, drop-in configuration snippets are read from <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/lib/systemd/*.conf.d/</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/local/lib/systemd/*.conf.d/</xhtml:span>, and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/systemd/*.conf.d/</xhtml:span>. Those drop-ins have higher precedence and override the main configuration file. Files in the *.conf.d/ configuration subdirectories are sorted by their filename in lexicographic order, regardless of in which of the subdirectories they reside. When multiple files specify the same option, for options which accept just a single value, the entry in the file sorted last takes precedence, and for options which accept a list of values, entries are collected as they occur in the sorted files.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>When packages need to customize the configuration, they can install drop-ins under /usr/. Files in /etc/ are reserved for the local administrator, who may use this logic to override the configuration files installed by vendor packages. Drop-ins have to be used to override package drop-ins, since the main configuration file has lower precedence. It is recommended to prefix all filenames in those subdirectories with a two-digit number and a dash, to simplify the ordering of the files.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>To disable a configuration file supplied by the vendor, the recommended way is to place a symlink to /dev/null in the configuration directory in /etc/, with the same filename as the vendor configuration file.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>The recommendations in this section only apply if <xhtml:span class="inline_block">timesyncd</xhtml:span> is in use on the system</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-timesyncd</xhtml:span> service specifically implements only SNTP.
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>This minimalistic service will set the system clock for large offsets or slowly adjust it for smaller deltas</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>More complex use cases are not covered by <xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-timesyncd</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:strong>If <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chrony</xhtml:span> is used, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-timesyncd</xhtml:span> should be stopped and masked, and this section skipped</xhtml:strong></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:strong>One, and only one, time synchronization method should be in use on the system</xhtml:strong></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

Rule.title: Ensure systemd-timesyncd configured with authorized timeserver
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">NTP=</xhtml:span></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>A space-separated list of NTP server host names or IP addresses. During runtime this list is combined with any per-interface NTP servers acquired from systemd-networkd.service(8). systemd-timesyncd will contact all configured system or per-interface servers in turn, until one responds. When the empty string is assigned, the list of NTP servers is reset, and all prior assignments will have no effect. This setting defaults to an empty list.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">FallbackNTP=</xhtml:span></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>A space-separated list of NTP server host names or IP addresses to be used as the fallback NTP servers. Any per-interface NTP servers obtained from systemd-networkd.service(8) take precedence over this setting, as do any servers set via NTP= above. This setting is hence only relevant if no other NTP server information is known. When the empty string is assigned, the list of NTP servers is reset, and all prior assignments will have no effect. If this option is not given, a compiled-in list of NTP servers is used.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

safeguard.title: Standardize Time Synchronization
Utilize Three Synchronized Time Sources

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Time synchronization is important to support time sensitive security mechanisms and to ensure log files have consistent time records across the enterprise to aid in forensic investigations</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Set <xhtml:span class="inline_block">NTP</xhtml:span> and/or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">FallbackNPT</xhtml:span> parameters to local site approved authoritative time server(s) in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/systemd/timesyncd.conf</xhtml:span> or a file in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/systemd/timesyncd.conf.d/</xhtml:span> ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">[Time]</xhtml:span> section:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example file:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">[Time]<br />NTP=time.nist.gov # Uses the generic name for NIST's time servers  <br />FallbackNTP=time-a-g.nist.gov time-b-g.nist.gov time-c-g.nist.gov # Space separated list of NIST time servers
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example script to create systemd drop-in configuration file:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>

Group.title: Configure chrony
Group.description:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">chrony</xhtml:span> is a daemon which implements the Network Time Protocol (NTP) and is designed to synchronize system clocks across a variety of systems and use a source that is highly accurate.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">chrony</xhtml:span> can be configured to be a client and/or a server.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>More information on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chrony</xhtml:span> can be found at: <xhtml:a href="http://chrony.tuxfamily.org/">http://chrony.tuxfamily.org/</xhtml:a>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>If <xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-timesyncd</xhtml:span> is being used, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chrony</xhtml:span> should be removed and this section skipped</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Only one time synchronization method should be in use on the system</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

Rule.title: Ensure chrony is configured with authorized timeserver
Rule.description:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>
<xhtml:p>server</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>The server directive specifies an NTP server which can be used as a time source. The client-server relationship is strictly hierarchical: a client might synchronize its system time to that of the server, but the server’s system time will never be influenced by that of a client.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>This directive can be used multiple times to specify multiple servers.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The directive is immediately followed by either the name of the server, or its IP address.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>
<xhtml:p>pool</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>The syntax of this directive is similar to that for the server directive, except that it is used to specify a pool of NTP servers rather than a single NTP server. The pool name is expected to resolve to multiple addresses which might change over time.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>This directive can be used multiple times to specify multiple pools.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>All options valid in the server directive can be used in this directive too.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

safeguard.title: Standardize Time Synchronization
Utilize Three Synchronized Time Sources

metadata.notes:
<xhtml:p>If pool and/or server directive(s) are set in a sources file in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/chrony/sources.d</xhtml:span>, the line:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">sourcedir /etc/chrony/sources.d
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>must be present in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/chrony/chrony.conf</xhtml:span></xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Time synchronization is important to support time sensitive security mechanisms and to ensure log files have consistent time records across the enterprise to aid in forensic investigations</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/chrony/chrony.conf</xhtml:span> or a file ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.sources</xhtml:span> in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/chrony/sources.d/</xhtml:span> and add or edit server or pool lines as appropriate according to local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Chrony</xhtml:span> configuration and add or edit the server and/or pool lines returned by the Audit Procedure as appropriate according to local site policy</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"><[server|pool]> <[remote-server|remote-pool]>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example script to add a drop-in configuration for the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pool</xhtml:span> directive:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   [ ! -d "/etc/chrony/sources.d/" ] && mkdir /etc/chrony/sources.d/<br />   printf '%s\n' "" "#The maxsources option is unique to the pool directive" \<br />   "pool time.nist.gov iburst maxsources 4" >> /etc/chrony/sources.d/60-sources.sources<br />   chronyc reload sources &>/dev/null<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example script to add a drop-in configuration for the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">server</xhtml:span> directive:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   [ ! -d "/etc/chrony/sources.d/" ] && mkdir /etc/chrony/sources.d/<br />   printf '%s\n' "" "server time-a-g.nist.gov iburst" "server 132.163.97.3 iburst" \<br />   "server time-d-b.nist.gov iburst" >> /etc/chrony/sources.d/60-sources.sources<br />   chronyc reload sources &>/dev/null<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to reload the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chronyd</xhtml:span> config:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl reload-or-restart chronyd
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chrony</xhtml:span> is in use on the system, run the following script to ensure <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chrony</xhtml:span> is configured with an authorized timeserver:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_output=() a_output2=() a_config_files=("/etc/chrony/chrony.conf") <br />   l_include='(confdir|sourcedir)' l_parameter_name='(server|pool)' l_parameter_value='.+'<br />   while IFS= read -r l_conf_loc; do<br />      l_dir="" l_ext=""<br />      if [ -d "$l_conf_loc" ]; then<br />         l_dir="$l_conf_loc" l_ext="*"<br />      elif  grep -Psq '\/\*\.([^#/\n\r]+)?\h*$' <<< "$l_conf_loc" || [ -f "$(readlink -f "$l_conf_loc")" ]; then<br />         l_dir="$(dirname "$l_conf_loc")" l_ext="$(basename "$l_conf_loc")"<br />      fi<br />      if [[ -n "$l_dir" && -n "$l_ext" ]]; then<br />         while IFS= read -r -d $'\0' l_file_name; do<br />            [ -f "$(readlink -f "$l_file_name")" ] && a_config_files+=("$(readlink -f "$l_file_name")")<br />         done < <(find -L "$l_dir" -type f -name "$l_ext" -print0 2>/dev/null)<br />      fi<br />   done < <(awk '$1~/^\s*'"$l_include"'$/{print $2}' "${a_config_files[*]}" 2>/dev/null)<br />   for l_file in "${a_config_files[@]}"; do<br />      l_parameter_line="$(grep -Psi '^\h*'"$l_parameter_name"'(\h+|\h*:\h*)'"$l_parameter_value"'\b' "$l_file")"<br />      [ -n "$l_parameter_line" ] && a_output+=("  - Parameter: \"$(tr -d '()' <<< ${l_parameter_name//|/ or })\"" \<br />      "    Exists in the file: \"$l_file\" as:" "$l_parameter_line")<br />   done<br />   [ "${#a_output[@]}" -le "0" ] && a_output2+=("  - Parameter: \"$(tr -d '()' <<< ${l_parameter_name//|/ or })\"" \<br />   "    Does not exist in the chrony configuration")<br />   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}" ""<br />   else<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" " - Reason(s) for audit failure:" "${a_output2[@]}"<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure crontab is restricted to authorized users
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">crontab</xhtml:span> is the program used to install, deinstall, or list the tables used to drive the cron daemon. Each user can have their own crontab, and though these are files in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/var/spool/cron/crontabs</xhtml:span>, they are not intended to be edited directly.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>If the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.allow</xhtml:span> file exists, then you must be listed (one user per line) therein in order to be allowed to use this command. If the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.allow</xhtml:span> file does not exist but the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.deny</xhtml:span> file does exist, then you must not be listed in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.deny</xhtml:span> file in order to use this command.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>If neither of these files exists, then depending on site-dependent configuration parameters, only the super user will be allowed to use this command, or all users will be able to use this command.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>If both files exist then <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.allow</xhtml:span> takes precedence. Which means that <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.deny</xhtml:span> is not considered and your user must be listed in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.allow</xhtml:span> in order to be able to use the crontab.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Regardless of the existence of any of these files, the root administrative user is always allowed to setup a crontab.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The files <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.allow</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.deny</xhtml:span>, if they exist, must be either world-readable, or readable by group <xhtml:span class="inline_block">crontab</xhtml:span>. If they are not, then cron will deny access to all users until the permissions are fixed.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>There is one file for each user's crontab under the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/var/spool/cron/crontabs</xhtml:span> directory. Users are not allowed to edit the files under that directory directly to ensure that only users allowed by the system to run periodic tasks can add them, and only syntactically correct crontabs will be written there. This is enforced by having the directory writable only by the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">crontab</xhtml:span> group and configuring crontab command with the setgid bid set for that specific group.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Even though a given user is not listed in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cron.allow</xhtml:span>, cron jobs can still be run as that user</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The files <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.allow</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.deny</xhtml:span>, if they exist, only controls administrative access to the crontab command for scheduling and modifying cron jobs</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Protect Information through  Access Control Lists

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>On many systems, only the system administrator is authorized to schedule <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cron</xhtml:span> jobs. Using the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cron.allow</xhtml:span> file to control who can run <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cron</xhtml:span> jobs enforces this policy. It is easier to manage an allow list than a deny list. In a deny list, you could potentially add a user ID to the system and forget to add it to the deny files.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> cron is installed on the system:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following script to:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Create <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.allow</xhtml:span> if it doesn't exist</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Change owner to user <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Change group owner to group <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span> <xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong> group <xhtml:span class="inline_block">crontab</xhtml:span> if it exists</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Change mode to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">640</xhtml:span> or more restrictive</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   [ ! -e "/etc/cron.deny" ] && touch /etc/cron.allow<br />   chmod u-x,g-wx,o-rwx /etc/cron.allow<br />   if grep -Pq -- '^\h*crontab\:' /etc/group; then<br />      chown root:crontab /etc/cron.allow<br />   else<br />      chown root:root /etc/cron.allow<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.deny</xhtml:span> exists, run the following script to:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Change owner to user <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Change group owner to group <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span> <xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong> group <xhtml:span class="inline_block">crontab</xhtml:span> if it exists</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Change mode to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">640</xhtml:span> or more restrictive</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   if [ -e "/etc/cron.deny" ]; then<br />      chmod u-x,g-wx,o-rwx /etc/cron.deny<br />      if grep -Pq -- '^\h*crontab\:' /etc/group; then<br />         chown root:crontab /etc/cron.deny<br />      else<br />         chown root:root /etc/cron.deny<br />      fi<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> On systems where cron is configured to use the group <xhtml:span class="inline_block">crontab</xhtml:span>, if the group <xhtml:span class="inline_block">crontab</xhtml:span> is not set as the owner of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cron.allow</xhtml:span>, then cron will deny access to all users and you will see an error similar to:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">You (<USERNAME>) are not allowed to use this program (crontab)<br />See crontab(1) for more information
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> cron is installed on the system:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/cron.allow</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>

Group.title: Configure at
Group.description:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">at</xhtml:span> is a command-line utility used to schedule a job for later execution</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> if <xhtml:span class="inline_block">at</xhtml:span> is not installed on the system, this section can be skipped</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure at is restricted to authorized users
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">at</xhtml:span> allows fairly complex time specifications, extending the POSIX.2 standard. It accepts times of the form HH:MM to run a job at a specific time of day. (If that time is already past, the next day is assumed.) You may also specify midnight, noon, or teatime (4pm) and you can have a time-of-day suffixed with AM or PM for running in the morning or the evening. You can also say what day the job will be run, by giving a date in the form month-name day with an optional year, or giving a date of the form MMDD[CC]YY, MM/DD/[CC]YY,  DD.MM.[CC]YY or [CC]YY-MM-DD. The specification of a date must follow the specification of the time of day. You can also give times like now + count time-units, where the time-units can be minutes, hours, days, or weeks and you can tell at to run the job today by suffixing the time with today and to run the job tomorrow by suffixing the time with tomorrow.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/at.allow</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/at.deny</xhtml:span> files determine which user can submit commands for later execution via at or batch. The format of the files is a list of usernames, one on each line. Whitespace is not permitted. If the file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/at.allow</xhtml:span> exists, only usernames mentioned in it are allowed to use at. If <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/at.allow</xhtml:span> does not exist, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/at.deny</xhtml:span> is checked, every username not mentioned in it is then allowed to use at. An empty <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/at.deny</xhtml:span> means that every user may use at. If neither file exists, only the superuser is allowed to use at.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Protect Information through  Access Control Lists

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>On many systems, only the system administrator is authorized to schedule <xhtml:span class="inline_block">at</xhtml:span> jobs. Using the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">at.allow</xhtml:span> file to control who can run <xhtml:span class="inline_block">at</xhtml:span> jobs enforces this policy. It is easier to manage an allow list than a deny list. In a deny list, you could potentially add a user ID to the system and forget to add it to the deny files.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> at is installed on the system:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following script to:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/at.allow</xhtml:span>:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Create the file if it doesn't exist</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Change owner or user <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>If group <xhtml:span class="inline_block">daemon</xhtml:span> exists, change to group <xhtml:span class="inline_block">daemon</xhtml:span>, else change group to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Change mode to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">640</xhtml:span> or more restrictive</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/at.deny</xhtml:span> exists:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Change owner or user <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>If group <xhtml:span class="inline_block">daemon</xhtml:span> exists, change to group <xhtml:span class="inline_block">daemon</xhtml:span>, else change group to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Change mode to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">640</xhtml:span> or more restrictive</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   grep -Pq -- '^daemon\b' /etc/group && l_group="daemon" || l_group="root"<br />   [ ! -e "/etc/at.allow" ] && touch /etc/at.allow<br />   chown root:"$l_group" /etc/at.allow<br />   chmod u-x,g-wx,o-rwx /etc/at.allow<br />   [ -e "/etc/at.deny" ] && chown root:"$l_group" /etc/at.deny<br />   [ -e "/etc/at.deny" ] && chmod u-x,g-wx,o-rwx /etc/at.deny<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> at is installed on the system:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/at.allow</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Exists</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Is mode <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0640</xhtml:span> or more restrictive</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Is owned by the user <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Is group owned by the group <xhtml:span class="inline_block">daemon</xhtml:span> or group <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># stat -Lc 'Access: (%a/%A) Owner: (%U) Group: (%G)' /etc/at.allow<br /><br />Access: (640/-rw-r-----) Owner: (root) Group: (daemon)<br />-OR-<br />Access: (640/-rw-r-----) Owner: (root) Group: (root)
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Verify mode is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">640</xhtml:span> or more restrictive, owner is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span>, and group is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">daemon</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify <xhtml:span class="inline_block">at.deny</xhtml:span> doesn't exist, <xhtml:strong>-OR-</xhtml:strong> is:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Mode <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0640</xhtml:span> or more restrictive</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Owned by the user <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Group owned by the group <xhtml:span class="inline_block">daemon</xhtml:span> or group <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># [ -e "/etc/at.deny" ] && stat -Lc 'Access: (%a/%A) Owner: (%U) Group: (%G)' /etc/at.deny<br /><br />Access: (640/-rw-r-----) Owner: (root) Group: (daemon)<br />-OR-<br />Access: (640/-rw-r-----) Owner: (root) Group: (root)<br />-OR-<br />Nothing is returned
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>If a value is returned, verify mode is 640 or more restrictive, owner is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span>, and group is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">daemon</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span></xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Group.title: Network
Group.description: <xhtml:p>This section provides guidance on for securing the network configuration of the system</xhtml:p>

Group.title: Configure Network Devices
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>To reduce the attack surface of a system, unused devices should be disabled.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> This should not be considered a comprehensive list, you may wish to consider additions to those listed here for your environment.</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure IPv6 status is identified
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6) is the most recent version of Internet Protocol (IP). It's designed to supply IP addressing and additional security to support the predicted growth of connected devices. IPv6 is based on 128-bit addressing and can support 340 undecillion, which is 340,282,366,920,938,463,463,374,607,431,768,211,456 unique addresses.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Features of IPv6</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Hierarchical addressing and routing infrastructure</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Statefull and Stateless configuration</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Support for quality of service (QoS)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>An ideal protocol for neighboring node interaction</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

safeguard.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software
Ensure Only Approved Ports, Protocols and Services Are Running

metadata.notes: <xhtml:p>Having more addresses has grown in importance with the expansion of smart devices and connectivity. IPv6 provides more than enough globally unique IP addresses for every networked device currently on the planet, helping ensure providers can keep pace with the expected proliferation of IP-based devices.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>IETF RFC 4038 recommends that applications are built with an assumption of dual stack. It is recommended that IPv6 be enabled and configured in accordance with Benchmark recommendations.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> dual stack and IPv6 are not used in your environment, IPv6 may be disabled to reduce the attack surface of the system, and recommendations pertaining to IPv6 can be skipped.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> It is recommended that IPv6 be enabled and configured unless this is against local site policy</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Enable or disable IPv6 in accordance with system requirements and local site policy</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>IETF RFC 4038 recommends that applications are built with an assumption of dual stack.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>When enabled, IPv6 will require additional configuration to reduce risk to the system.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to identify if IPv6 is enabled on the system:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   l_output=""<br />   ! grep -Pqs -- '^\h*0\b' /sys/module/ipv6/parameters/disable && l_output="- IPv6 is not enabled"<br />   if sysctl net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6 | grep -Pqs -- "^\h*net\.ipv6\.conf\.all\.disable_ipv6\h*=\h*1\b" && \<br />      sysctl net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6 | grep -Pqs -- "^\h*net\.ipv6\.conf\.default\.disable_ipv6\h*=\h*1\b"; then<br />      l_output="- IPv6 is not enabled"<br />   fi<br />   [ -z "$l_output" ] && l_output="- IPv6 is enabled"<br />   echo -e "\n$l_output\n"<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure wireless interfaces are disabled
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>Wireless networking is used when wired networks are unavailable.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software
Disable Wireless Access on Devices if Not Required
Limit Wireless Access on Client Devices

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>-IF-</xhtml:strong> wireless is not to be used, wireless devices can be disabled to reduce the potential attack surface.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to disable any wireless interfaces:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   module_fix()<br />   {<br />      if ! modprobe -n -v "$l_mname" | grep -P -- '^\h*install \/bin\/(true|false)'; then<br />         echo -e " - setting module: \"$l_mname\" to be un-loadable"<br />         echo -e "install $l_mname /bin/false" >> /etc/modprobe.d/"$l_mname".conf<br />      fi<br />      if lsmod | grep "$l_mname" > /dev/null 2>&1; then<br />         echo -e " - unloading module \"$l_mname\""<br />         modprobe -r "$l_mname"<br />      fi<br />      if ! grep -Pq -- "^\h*blacklist\h+$l_mname\b" /etc/modprobe.d/*; then<br />         echo -e " - deny listing \"$l_mname\""<br />         echo -e "blacklist $l_mname" >> /etc/modprobe.d/"$l_mname".conf<br />      fi<br />   }<br />   if [ -n "$(find /sys/class/net/*/ -type d -name wireless)" ]; then<br />      l_dname=$(for driverdir in $(find /sys/class/net/*/ -type d -name wireless | xargs -0 dirname); do basename "$(readlink -f "$driverdir"/device/driver/module)";done | sort -u)<br />      for l_mname in $l_dname; do<br />         module_fix<br />      done<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Many if not all laptop workstations and some desktop workstations will connect via wireless requiring these interfaces be enabled.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to verify no wireless interfaces are active on the system:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   l_output="" l_output2=""<br />   module_chk()<br />   {<br />      # Check how module will be loaded<br />      l_loadable="$(modprobe -n -v "$l_mname")"<br />      if grep -Pq -- '^\h*install /bin/(true|false)' <<< "$l_loadable"; then<br />         l_output="$l_output
 - module: "$l_mname" is not loadable: "$l_loadable""<br />      else<br />         l_output2="$l_output2
 - module: "$l_mname" is loadable: "$l_loadable""<br />      fi<br />      # Check is the module currently loaded<br />      if ! lsmod | grep "$l_mname" > /dev/null 2>&1; then<br />         l_output="$l_output
 - module: "$l_mname" is not loaded"<br />      else<br />         l_output2="$l_output2
 - module: "$l_mname" is loaded"<br />      fi<br />      # Check if the module is deny listed<br />      if modprobe --showconfig | grep -Pq -- "^\h*blacklist\h+$l_mname "; then<br />         l_output="$l_output
 - module: "$l_mname" is deny listed in: "$(grep -Pl -- "^\h*blacklist\h+$l_mname " /etc/modprobe.d/*)""<br />      else<br />         l_output2="$l_output2
 - module: "$l_mname" is not deny listed"<br />      fi<br />   }<br />   if [ -n "$(find /sys/class/net/*/ -type d -name wireless)" ]; then<br />      l_dname=$(for driverdir in $(find /sys/class/net/*/ -type d -name wireless | xargs -0 dirname); do basename "$(readlink -f "$driverdir"/device/driver/module)";done | sort -u)<br />      for l_mname in $l_dname; do<br />         module_chk<br />      done<br />   fi<br />   # Report results. If no failures output in l_output2, we pass<br />   if [ -z "$l_output2" ]; then<br />      echo -e "
- Audit Result:
  ** PASS **"<br />      if [ -z "$l_output" ]; then<br />         echo -e "
 - System has no wireless NICs installed"<br />      else<br />         echo -e "
$l_output
"<br />      fi<br />   else<br />      echo -e "
- Audit Result:
  ** FAIL **
 - Reason(s) for audit failure:
$l_output2
"<br />      [ -n "$l_output" ] && echo -e "
- Correctly set:
$l_output
"<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure bluetooth services are not in use
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology standard that is used for exchanging data between devices over short distances. It employs UHF radio waves in the ISM bands, from 2.402 GHz to 2.48 GHz. It is mainly used as an alternative to wire connections.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software
Ensure Only Approved Ports, Protocols and Services Are Running

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>An attacker may be able to find a way to access or corrupt your data. One example of this type of activity is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">bluesnarfing</xhtml:span>, which refers to attackers using a Bluetooth connection to steal information off of your Bluetooth device. Also, viruses or other malicious code can take advantage of Bluetooth technology to infect other devices. If you are infected, your data may be corrupted, compromised, stolen, or lost.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following commands to stop <xhtml:span class="inline_block">bluetooth.service</xhtml:span>, and remove the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">bluez</xhtml:span> package:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl stop bluetooth.service<br /># apt purge bluez
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">bluez</xhtml:span> package is required as a dependency:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following commands to stop and mask <xhtml:span class="inline_block">bluetooth.service</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl stop bluetooth.service<br /># systemctl mask bluetooth.service
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> A reboot may be required</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Many personal electronic devices (PEDs) use Bluetooth technology. For example, you may be able to operate your computer with a wireless keyboard. Disabling Bluetooth will prevent these devices from connecting to the system.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>There may be packages that are dependent on the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">bluez</xhtml:span> package.  If the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">bluez</xhtml:span> package is removed, these dependent packages will be removed as well. Before removing the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">bluez</xhtml:span> package, review any dependent packages to determine if they are required on the system.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>-IF-</xhtml:strong> a dependent package is required: stop and mask <xhtml:span class="inline_block">bluetooth.service</xhtml:span> leaving the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">bluez</xhtml:span> package installed.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">bluez</xhtml:span> package is not installed:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># dpkg-query -s bluez &>/dev/null && echo "bluez is installed" 
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">bluez</xhtml:span> package is required as a dependency:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify <xhtml:span class="inline_block">bluetooth.service</xhtml:span> is not enabled:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl is-enabled bluetooth.service 2>/dev/null | grep 'enabled'
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify <xhtml:span class="inline_block">bluetooth.service</xhtml:span> is not active:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl is-active bluetooth.service 2>/dev/null | grep '^active'
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> If the package is required for a dependency</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Ensure the dependent package is approved by local site policy</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Ensure stopping and masking the service and/or socket meets local site policy</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Group.title: Configure Network Kernel Modules
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>The Linux kernel modules support several network protocols that are not commonly used. If these protocols are not needed, it is recommended that they be disabled in the kernel.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> This should not be considered a comprehensive list of uncommon network protocols, you may wish to consider additions to those listed here for your environment.</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure dccp kernel module is not available
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The Datagram Congestion Control Protocol (DCCP) is a transport layer protocol that supports streaming media and telephony. DCCP provides a way to gain access to congestion control, without having to do it at the application layer, but does not provide in-sequence delivery.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software
Ensure Only Approved Ports, Protocols and Services Are Running

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> the protocol is not required, it is recommended that the drivers not be installed to reduce the potential attack surface.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to unload and disable the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">dccp</xhtml:span> module:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">dccp</xhtml:span> kernel module is available in ANY installed kernel:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Create a file ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">install dccp /bin/false</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/modprobe.d/</xhtml:span> directory</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Create a file ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">blacklist dccp</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/modprobe.d/</xhtml:span> directory</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Run <xhtml:span class="inline_block">modprobe -r dccp 2>/dev/null; rmmod dccp 2>/dev/null</xhtml:span> to remove <xhtml:span class="inline_block">dccp</xhtml:span> from the kernel</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">dccp</xhtml:span> kernel module is not available on the system, or pre-compiled into the kernel, no remediation is necessary</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_output2=() a_output3=() l_dl="" l_mod_name="dccp" l_mod_type="net"<br />   l_mod_path="$(readlink -f /lib/modules/**/kernel/$l_mod_type | sort -u)"<br />   f_module_fix()<br />   {<br />      l_dl="y" a_showconfig=()<br />      while IFS= read -r l_showconfig; do<br />         a_showconfig+=("$l_showconfig")<br />      done < <(modprobe --showconfig | grep -P -- '\b(install|blacklist)\h+'"${l_mod_chk_name//-/_}"'\b')<br />      if  lsmod | grep "$l_mod_chk_name" &> /dev/null; then<br />         a_output2+=(" - unloading kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\"")<br />         modprobe -r "$l_mod_chk_name" 2>/dev/null; rmmod "$l_mod_name" 2>/dev/null<br />      fi<br />      if ! grep -Pq -- '\binstall\h+'"${l_mod_chk_name//-/_}"'\h+(\/usr)?\/bin\/(true|false)\b' <<< "${a_showconfig[*]}"; then<br />         a_output2+=(" - setting kernel  module: \"$l_mod_name\" to \"$(readlink -f /bin/false)\"")<br />         printf '%s\n' "install $l_mod_chk_name $(readlink -f /bin/false)" >> /etc/modprobe.d/"$l_mod_name".conf<br />      fi<br />      if ! grep -Pq -- '\bblacklist\h+'"${l_mod_chk_name//-/_}"'\b' <<< "${a_showconfig[*]}"; then<br />         a_output2+=(" - denylisting kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\"")<br />         printf '%s\n' "blacklist $l_mod_chk_name" >> /etc/modprobe.d/"$l_mod_name".conf<br />      fi<br />   }<br />   for l_mod_base_directory in $l_mod_path; do # Check if the module exists on the system<br />      if [ -d "$l_mod_base_directory/${l_mod_name/-/\/}" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$l_mod_base_directory/${l_mod_name/-/\/}")" ]; then<br />         a_output3+=("  - \"$l_mod_base_directory\"")<br />         l_mod_chk_name="$l_mod_name"<br />         [[ "$l_mod_name" =~ overlay ]] && l_mod_chk_name="${l_mod_name::-2}"        <br />         [ "$l_dl" != "y" ] && f_module_fix<br />      else<br />         printf '%s\n' " - kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\" doesn't exist in \"$l_mod_base_directory\""<br />      fi<br />   done<br />   [ "${#a_output3[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "" " -- INFO --" " - module: \"$l_mod_name\" exists in:" "${a_output3[@]}"<br />   [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "" "${a_output2[@]}" || printf '%s\n' "" " - No changes needed"<br />   printf '%s\n' "" " - remediation of kernel module: \"$l_mod_name\" complete" ""<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to verify:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">dccp</xhtml:span> kernel module is available in ANY installed kernel, verify:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>

Group.title: Configure Network Kernel Parameters
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>The following network parameters are intended for use on both host only and router systems. A system acts as a router if it has at least two interfaces and is configured to perform routing functions.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>sysctl settings are defined through files in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/local/lib</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/lib/</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/lib/</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/run/</xhtml:span>, and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Files are typically placed in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sysctl.d</xhtml:span> directory within the parent directory</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The paths where sysctl preload files usually exist
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/run/sysctl.d/*.conf</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.d/*.conf</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/local/lib/sysctl.d/*.conf</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/lib/sysctl.d/*.conf</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/lib/sysctl.d/*.conf</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.conf</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Files must have the "<xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span>" extension</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Vendors settings usually live in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/lib/</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/local/lib/</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>To override a whole file, create a new file with the same name in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.d/</xhtml:span> and put new settings there.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>To override only specific settings, add a file with a lexically later name in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.d/</xhtml:span> and put new settings there.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The command <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-sysctl --cat-config</xhtml:span> produces output containing The system's loaded kernel parameters and the files they're configured in:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Entries listed latter in the file take precedence over the same settings listed earlier in the file</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Files containing kernel parameters that are over-ridden by other files with the same name will not be listed</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>On systems running UncomplicatedFirewall, the kernel parameters may be set or over-written. This will not be visible in the output of the command</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>On systems with Uncomplicated Firewall, additional settings may be configured in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf</xhtml:span>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>The settings in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf</xhtml:span> will override settings other settings and <xhtml:strong>will not</xhtml:strong> be visible in the output of the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-sysctl --cat-config</xhtml:span> command</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>This behavior can be changed by updating the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">IPT_SYSCTL</xhtml:span> parameter in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/default/ufw</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>The system's loaded kernel parameters and the files they're configured in can be viewed by running the following command:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># /usr/lib/systemd/systemd-sysctl --cat-config
</xhtml:code>

Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">net.ipv4.ip_forward</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding</xhtml:span> flags are used to tell the system whether it can forward packets or not.</xhtml:p>

<xhtml:ul>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Setting <xhtml:span class="inline_block">net.ipv4.ip_forward</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding</xhtml:span> to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> ensures that a system with multiple interfaces (for example, a hard proxy), will never be able to forward packets, and therefore, never serve as a router.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: CM-1, CM-2, CM-6, CM-7, IA-5

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Set the following parameter in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.conf</xhtml:span> or a file in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.d/</xhtml:span> ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">net.ipv4.ip_forward = 0</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># printf '%s\n' "net.ipv4.ip_forward = 0" >> /etc/sysctl.d/60-netipv4_sysctl.conf
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following script to set the active kernel parameters:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=0<br />   sysctl -w net.ipv4.route.flush=1<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> IPv6 is enabled on the system:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Set the following parameter in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.conf</xhtml:span> or a file in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sysctl.d/</xhtml:span> ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding = 0</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># printf '%s\n' "net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding = 0" >> /etc/sysctl.d/60-netipv6_sysctl.conf
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following script to set the active kernel parameters:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash <br /><br />{<br />   sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=0<br />   sysctl -w net.ipv6.route.flush=1<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> If these settings appear in a canonically later file, or later in the same file, these settings will be overwritten</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>IP forwarding is required on systems configured to act as a router. If these parameters are disabled, the system will not be able to perform as a router.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Many Cloud Service Provider (CSP) hosted systems require IP forwarding to be enabled. If the system is running on a CSP platform, this requirement should be reviewed before disabling IP forwarding.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to verify the following kernel parameters are set in the running configuration and correctly loaded from a kernel parameter configuration file:</xhtml:p>

<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>

The parameters being checked may be set correctly in a file. If that file is superseded, the parameter is overridden by an incorrect setting later in that file, or in a canonically later file, that "correct" setting will be ignored both by the script and by the system during a normal kernel parameter load sequence.</xhtml:li>

then<br />         a_output+=(" - \"$l_parameter_name\" is correctly set to \"$l_running_parameter_value\""<br />         "    in the running configuration")<br />      else<br />         a_output2+=(" - \"$l_parameter_name\" is incorrectly set to \"$l_running_parameter_value\"" \<br />         "    in the running configuration" \<br />         "    and should have a value of: \"$l_value_out\"")<br />      fi<br />      unset A_out; declare -A A_out # Check durable setting (files)<br />      while read -r l_out; do<br />         if [ -n "$l_out" ]; then<br />            if [[ $l_out =~ ^\s*# ]]; then<br />               l_file="${l_out//# /}"<br />            else<br />               l_kpar="$(awk -F= '{print $1}' <<< "$l_out" | xargs)"<br />               [ "$l_kpar" = "$l_parameter_name" ] && A_out+=(["$l_kpar"]="$l_file")<br />            fi<br />         fi<br />      done < <("$l_systemdsysctl" --cat-config | grep -Po '^\h*([^#\n\r]+|#\h*\/[^#\n\r\h]+\.conf\b)')<br />      if [ -n "$l_ufwscf" ]; then # Account for systems with UFW (Not covered by systemd-sysctl --cat-config)<br />         l_kpar="$(grep -Po "^\h*$l_parameter_name\b" "$l_ufwscf" | xargs)"<br />         l_kpar="${l_kpar//\//.}"<br />         [ "$l_kpar" = "$l_parameter_name" ] && A_out+=(["$l_kpar"]="$l_ufwscf")<br />      fi<br />      if (( ${#A_out[@]} > 0 )); then<br />               a_output+=(" - \"$l_parameter_name\" is correctly set to \"$l_file_parameter_value\"" \<br />               "    in \"$(printf '%s' "${A_out[@]}")\"")<br />            else<br />               a_output2+=(" - \"$l_parameter_name\" is incorrectly set to \"$l_file_parameter_value\""<br />               "    in \"$(printf '%s' "${A_out[@]}")\"" \<br />               "    and should have a value of: \"$l_value_out\"")<br />            fi<br />         done < <(grep -Po -- "^\h*$l_parameter_name\h*=\h*\H+" "${A_out[@]}")<br />      else<br />         a_output2+=(" - \"$l_parameter_name\" is not set in an included file" \<br />         "    ** Note: \"$l_parameter_name\" May be set in a file that's ignored by load procedure **")<br />      fi<br />   }<br />   l_systemdsysctl="$(readlink -f /lib/systemd/systemd-sysctl)"<br />   while IFS="=" read -r l_parameter_name l_parameter_value;
