Group.title: Configure SSH Server
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>Secure Shell (SSH) is a secure, encrypted replacement for common login services such as <xhtml:span class="inline_block">telnet</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ftp</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rlogin</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsh</xhtml:span>, and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rcp</xhtml:span>. It is strongly recommended that sites abandon older clear-text login protocols and use SSH to prevent session hijacking and sniffing of sensitive data off the network.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The recommendations in this section only apply if the SSH daemon is installed on the system, <xhtml:strong>if remote access is not required the SSH daemon can be removed and this section skipped</xhtml:strong>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">sshd_config</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>The openSSH daemon configuration directives, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Include</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Match</xhtml:span>, may cause the audits in this section's recommendations to report incorrectly. It is recommended that these options only be used if they're needed and fully understood. If these options are configured in accordance with local site policy, they should be accounted for when following the recommendations in this section.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The default <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Include</xhtml:span> location is the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d</xhtml:span> directory. This default has been accounted for in this section. If a file has an additional <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Include</xhtml:span> that isn't this default location, the files should be reviewed to verify that the recommended setting is not being over-ridden.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The audits of the running configuration in this section are run in the context of the root user, the local host name, and the local host's IP address. If a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Match</xhtml:span> block exists that matches one of these criteria, the output of the audit will be from the match block. The respective matched criteria should be replaced with a non-matching substitution.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">Include</xhtml:span>:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Include the specified configuration file(s).</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Multiple pathnames may be specified and each pathname may contain glob(7) wildcards that will be expanded and processed in lexical order.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Files without absolute paths are assumed to be in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>An Include directive may appear inside a Match block to perform conditional inclusion.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">Match</xhtml:span>:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Introduces a conditional block. If all of the criteria on the Match line are satisfied, the keywords on the following lines override those set in the global section of the config file, until either another Match line or the end of the file. If a keyword appears in multiple Match blocks that are satisfied, only the first instance of the keyword is applied.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The arguments to Match are one or more criteria-pattern pairs or the single token All which matches all criteria. The available criteria are User, Group, Host, LocalAddress, LocalPort, and Address.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The match patterns may consist of single entries or comma-separated lists and may use the wildcard and negation operators described in the PATTERNS section of ssh_config(5).</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The patterns in an Address criteria may additionally contain addresses to match in CIDR address/masklen format, such as <xhtml:span class="inline_block">192.0.2.0/24</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">2001:db8::/32</xhtml:span>.  Note that the mask length provided must be consistent with the address - it is an error to specify a mask length that is too long for the address or one with bits set in this host portion of the address. For example, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">192.0.2.0/33</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">192.0.2.0/8</xhtml:span>, respectively.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Only a subset of keywords may be used on the lines following a Match keyword. Available keywords are available in the ssh_config man page.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Once all configuration changes have been made to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config</xhtml:span> or any included configuration files, the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sshd</xhtml:span> configuration must be reloaded</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>Command to re-load the SSH daemon configuration:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl reload-or-restart sshd
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">sshd</xhtml:span> command:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">-T</xhtml:span> - Extended test mode.  Check the validity of the configuration file, output the effective configuration to stdout and then exit. Optionally, Match rules may be applied by specifying the connection parameters using one or more <xhtml:span class="inline_block">-C</xhtml:span> options.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">-C</xhtml:span> - connection_spec. Specify the connection parameters to use for the -T extended test mode. If provided, any Match directives in the configuration file that would apply are applied before the configuration is written to standard output. The connection parameters are supplied as keyword=value pairs and may be supplied in any order, either with multiple <xhtml:span class="inline_block">-C</xhtml:span> options or as a comma-separated list. The keywords are <xhtml:span class="inline_block">addr</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">user</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">host</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">laddr</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">lport</xhtml:span>, and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rdomain</xhtml:span> and correspond to source address, user, resolved source host name, local address, local port number and routing domain respectively.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

Rule.title: Ensure permissions on /etc/ssh/sshd_config are configured
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config</xhtml:span>, and files ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d</xhtml:span> directory, contain configuration specifications for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sshd</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Protect Information through  Access Control Lists

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>configuration specifications for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sshd</xhtml:span> need to be protected from unauthorized changes by non-privileged users.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to set ownership and permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config</xhtml:span> and files ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d</xhtml:span> directory:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   chmod u-x,og-rwx /etc/ssh/sshd_config<br />   chown root:root /etc/ssh/sshd_config<br />   while IFS= read -r -d $'\0' l_file; do<br />      if [ -e "$l_file" ]; then<br />         chmod u-x,og-rwx "$l_file"<br />         chown root:root "$l_file"<br />      fi<br />   done < <(find /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> other locations are listed in an <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Include</xhtml:span> statement, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">*.conf</xhtml:span> files in these locations access should also be modified.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script and verify <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config</xhtml:span> and files ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d</xhtml:span> directory are:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Mode <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0600</xhtml:span> or more restrictive</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Owned by the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span> user</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Group owned by the group <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_output=(); a_output2=()<br />   perm_mask='0177' && maxperm="$( printf '%o' $(( 0777 & ~$perm_mask)) )"<br />   f_sshd_files_chk()<br />   {<br />      while IFS=: read -r l_mode l_user l_group; do<br />         a_out2=()<br />         [ $(( $l_mode & $perm_mask )) -gt 0 ] && a_out2+=("    Is mode: \"$l_mode\"" \<br />         "    should be mode: \"$maxperm\" or more restrictive")<br />         [ "$l_user" != "root" ] && a_out2+=("    Is owned by \"$l_user\" should be owned by \"root\"")<br />         [ "$l_group" != "root" ] && a_out2+=("    Is group owned by \"$l_user\" should be group owned by \"root\"")<br />         if [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt "0" ]; then<br />            a_output2+=("  - File: \"$l_file\":" "${a_out2[@]}")<br />         else<br />            a_output+=("  - File: \"$l_file\":" "    Correct: mode ($l_mode), owner ($l_user)" \<br />            "    and group owner ($l_group) configured")<br />         fi<br />      done < <(stat -Lc '%#a:%U:%G' "$l_file")      <br />   }<br />   [ -e "/etc/ssh/sshd_config" ] && l_file="/etc/ssh/sshd_config" && f_sshd_files_chk<br />   while IFS= read -r -d $'\0' l_file; do<br />      [ -e "$l_file" ] && f_sshd_files_chk<br />   done < <(find /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d -type f -name '*.conf' \( -perm /077 -o ! -user root -o ! -group root \) -print0 2>/dev/null)<br />   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}" ""<br />   else<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" " - Reason(s) for audit failure:" "${a_output2[@]}"<br />      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "" "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}" ""<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> other locations are listed in an <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Include</xhtml:span> statement, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">*.conf</xhtml:span> files in these locations should also be checked.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure permissions on SSH private host key files are configured
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>An SSH private key is one of two files used in SSH public key authentication.  In this authentication method, the possession of the private key is proof of identity. Only a private key that corresponds to a public key will be able to authenticate successfully. The private keys need to be stored and handled carefully, and no copies of the private key should be distributed.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Protect Information through  Access Control Lists

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>If an unauthorized user obtains the private SSH host key file, the host could be impersonated</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to set mode, ownership, and group on the private SSH host key files:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_output=(); a_output2=(); l_ssh_group_name="$(awk -F: '($1 ~ /^(ssh_keys|_?ssh)$/) {print $1}' /etc/group)"<br />   f_file_access_fix()<br />   {<br />      while IFS=: read -r l_file_mode l_file_owner l_file_group; do<br />         a_out2=()<br />         [ "$l_file_group" = "$l_ssh_group_name" ] && l_pmask="0137" || l_pmask="0177"<br />         l_maxperm="$( printf '%o' $(( 0777 & ~$l_pmask )) )"<br />         if [ $(( $l_file_mode & $l_pmask )) -gt 0 ]; then<br />            a_out2+=("    Mode: \"$l_file_mode\" should be mode: \"$l_maxperm\" or more restrictive" \<br />            "    updating to mode: \:$l_maxperm\"")<br />            if [ "l_file_group" = "$l_ssh_group_name" ]; then<br />               chmod u-x,g-wx,o-rwx "$l_file"<br />            else<br />               chmod u-x,go-rwx "$l_file"<br />            fi<br />         fi<br />         if [ "$l_file_owner" != "root" ]; then<br />            a_out2+=("    Owned by: \"$l_file_owner\" should be owned by \"root\"" \<br />            "    Changing ownership to \"root\"")<br />            chown root "$l_file"<br />         fi<br />         if [[ ! "$l_file_group" =~ ($l_ssh_group_name|root) ]]; then<br />            [ -n "$l_ssh_group_name" ] && l_new_group="$l_ssh_group_name" || l_new_group="root"<br />            a_out2+=("    Owned by group \"$l_file_group\" should be group owned by: \"$l_ssh_group_name\" or \"root\"" \<br />            "    Changing group ownership to \"$l_new_group\"")<br />            chgrp "$l_new_group" "$l_file"<br />         fi<br />         if [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt "0" ]; then<br />            a_output2+=("  - File: \"$l_file\"" "${a_out2[@]}")<br />         else<br />            a_output+=("  - File: \"$l_file\"" \<br />            "Correct: mode: \"$l_file_mode\", owner: \"$l_file_owner\", and group owner: \"$l_file_group\" configured")<br />         fi<br />      done < <(stat -Lc '%#a:%U:%G' "$l_file")<br />   }<br />   while IFS= read -r -d $'\0' l_file; do <br />      if ssh-keygen -lf &>/dev/null "$l_file"; then <br />         file "$l_file" | grep -Piq -- '\bopenssh\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?private\h+key\b' && f_file_access_fix<br />      fi<br />   done < <(find -L /etc/ssh -xdev -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)<br />   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le "0" ]; then<br />      printf '%s\n' "" " - No access changes required" ""<br />   else<br />      printf '%s\n' "" " - Remediation results:" "${a_output2[@]}" ""<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to verify SSH private host key files are owned by the root user and either:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>owned by the group root and mode <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0600</xhtml:span> or more restrictive</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>owned by the group designated to own openSSH private keys and mode <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0640</xhtml:span> or more restrictive</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_output=(); a_output2=()<br />   l_ssh_group_name="$(awk -F: '($1 ~ /^(ssh_keys|_?ssh)$/) {print $1}' /etc/group)"<br />   f_file_chk()<br />   {<br />      while IFS=: read -r l_file_mode l_file_owner l_file_group; do<br />         a_out2=()<br />         [ "$l_file_group" = "$l_ssh_group_name" ] && l_pmask="0137" || l_pmask="0177"<br />         l_maxperm="$( printf '%o' $(( 0777 & ~$l_pmask )) )"<br />         if [ $(( $l_file_mode & $l_pmask )) -gt 0 ]; then<br />            a_out2+=("    Mode: \"$l_file_mode\" should be mode: \"$l_maxperm\" or more restrictive")<br />         fi<br />         if [ "$l_file_owner" != "root" ]; then<br />            a_out2+=("    Owned by: \"$l_file_owner\" should be owned by \"root\"")<br />         fi<br />         if [[ ! "$l_file_group" =~ ($l_ssh_group_name|root) ]]; then<br />            a_out2+=("    Owned by group \"$l_file_group\" should be group owned by: \"$l_ssh_group_name\" or \"root\"")<br />         fi<br />         if [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt "0" ]; then<br />            a_output2+=("  - File: \"$l_file\"${a_out2[@]}")<br />         else<br />            a_output+=("  - File: \"$l_file\"" \<br />            "    Correct: mode: \"$l_file_mode\", owner: \"$l_file_owner\" and group owner: \"$l_file_group\" configured")<br />         fi<br />      done < <(stat -Lc '%#a:%U:%G' "$l_file")<br />   }<br />   while IFS= read -r -d $'\0' l_file; do <br />      if ssh-keygen -lf &>/dev/null "$l_file"; then <br />         file "$l_file" | grep -Piq -- '\bopenssh\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?private\h+key\b' && f_file_chk<br />      fi<br />   done < <(find -L /etc/ssh -xdev -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)<br />   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}" ""<br />   else<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" " - Reason(s) for audit failure:" "${a_output2[@]}"<br />      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "" "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}" ""<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure permissions on SSH public host key files are configured
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>An SSH public key is one of two files used in SSH public key authentication. In this authentication method, a public key is a key that can be used for verifying digital signatures generated using a corresponding private key. Only a public key that corresponds to a private key will be able to authenticate successfully.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>If a public host key file is modified by an unauthorized user, the SSH service may be compromised.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to set mode, ownership, and group on the public SSH host key files:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_output=(); a_output2=()<br />   l_pmask="0133"; l_maxperm="$( printf '%o' $(( 0777 & ~$l_pmask )) )"<br />   f_file_access_fix()<br />   {<br />      while IFS=: read -r l_file_mode l_file_owner l_file_group; do<br />         a_out2=()<br />         [ $(( $l_file_mode & $l_pmask )) -gt 0 ] && \<br />            a_out2+=("    Mode: \"$l_file_mode\" should be mode: \"$l_maxperm\" or more restrictive" \<br />            "    updating to mode: \"$l_maxperm\"") && chmod u-x,go-wx "$l_file"<br />         [ "$l_file_owner" != "root" ] && \<br />            a_out2+=("    Owned by: \"$l_file_owner\" should be owned by \"root\"" \<br />            "    Changing ownership to \"root\"") && chown root "$l_file"<br />         [ "$l_file_group" != "root" ] && \<br />            a_out2+=("    Owned by group \"$l_file_group\" should be group owned by: \"root\"" \<br />            "    Changing group ownership to \"root\"") && chgrp root "$l_file"<br />         if [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt "0" ]; then<br />            a_output2+=("  - File: \"$l_file\"" "${a_out2[@]}")<br />         else<br />            a_output+=("  - File: \"$l_file\"" \<br />            "    Correct: mode: \"$l_file_mode\", owner: \"$l_file_owner\", and group owner: \"$l_file_group\" configured")<br />         fi<br />      done < <(stat -Lc '%#a:%U:%G' "$l_file")<br />   }<br />   while IFS= read -r -d $'\0' l_file; do <br />      if ssh-keygen -lf &>/dev/null "$l_file"; then <br />         file "$l_file" | grep -Piq -- '\bopenssh\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?public\h+key\b' && f_file_access_fix<br />      fi<br />   done < <(find -L /etc/ssh -xdev -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)<br />   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le "0" ]; then<br />      printf '%s\n' "" " - No access changes required" ""<br />   else<br />      printf '%s\n' " - Remediation results:" "${a_output2[@]}" ""<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

<xhtml:p>Run the following script to verify SSH public host key files are mode <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0644</xhtml:span> or more restrictive, owned by the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span> user, and owned by the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span> group:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_output=(); a_output2=()<br />   l_pmask="0133"; l_maxperm="$( printf '%o' $(( 0777 & ~$l_pmask )) )"<br />   f_file_chk()<br />   {<br />      while IFS=: read -r l_file_mode l_file_owner l_file_group; do<br />         a_out2=()<br />         if [ $(( $l_file_mode & $l_pmask )) -gt 0 ]; then<br />            a_out2+=("    Mode: \"$l_file_mode\" should be mode: \"$l_maxperm\" or more restrictive")<br />         fi<br />         if [ "$l_file_owner" != "root" ]; then<br />            a_out2+=("    Owned by: \"$l_file_owner\" should be owned by: \"root\"")<br />         fi<br />         if [ "$l_file_group" != "root" ]; then<br />            a_out2+=("    Owned by group \"$l_file_group\" should be group owned by group: \"root\"")<br />         fi<br />         if [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt "0" ]; then<br />            a_output2+=("  - File: \"$l_file\"" "${a_out2[@]}")<br />         else<br />            a_output+=("  - File: \"$l_file\"" \<br />            "    Correct: mode: \"$l_file_mode\", owner: \"$l_file_owner\" and group owner: \"$l_file_group\" configured")<br />         fi<br />      done < <(stat -Lc '%#a:%U:%G' "$l_file")<br />   }<br />   while IFS= read -r -d $'\0' l_file; do <br />      if ssh-keygen -lf &>/dev/null "$l_file"; then <br />         file "$l_file" | grep -Piq -- '\bopenssh\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?public\h+key\b' && f_file_chk<br />      fi<br />   done < <(find -L /etc/ssh -xdev -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)<br />   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then<br />      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -le 0 ] && a_output+=("  - No openSSH public keys found")<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}" ""<br />   else<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" " - Reason(s) for audit failure:" "${a_output2[@]}"<br />      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "" "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}" ""<br />   fi<br />}

Rule.title: Ensure sshd access is configured
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>There are several options available to limit which users and group can access the system via SSH. It is recommended that at least one of the following options be leveraged:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">AllowUsers</xhtml:span>:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">AllowUsers</xhtml:span> variable gives the system administrator the option of allowing specific users to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ssh</xhtml:span> into the system. The list consists of space separated user names. Numeric user IDs are not recognized with this variable. If a system administrator wants to restrict user access further by only allowing the allowed users to log in from a particular host, the entry can be specified in the form of user@host.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">AllowGroups</xhtml:span>:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">AllowGroups</xhtml:span> variable gives the system administrator the option of allowing specific groups of users to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ssh</xhtml:span> into the system. The list consists of space separated group names. Numeric group IDs are not recognized with this variable.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">DenyUsers</xhtml:span>:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">DenyUsers</xhtml:span> variable gives the system administrator the option of denying specific users to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ssh</xhtml:span> into the system. The list consists of space separated user names. Numeric user IDs are not recognized with this variable. If a system administrator wants to restrict user access further by specifically denying a user's access from a particular host, the entry can be specified in the form of user@host.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">DenyGroups</xhtml:span>:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">DenyGroups</xhtml:span> variable gives the system administrator the option of denying specific groups of users to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ssh</xhtml:span> into the system. The list consists of space separated group names. Numeric group IDs are not recognized with this variable.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Ensure the Use of Dedicated Administrative Accounts

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Restricting which users can remotely access the system via SSH will help ensure that only authorized users access the system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config</xhtml:span> file to set one or more of the parameters above any <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Include</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Match</xhtml:span> set statements as follows:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">AllowUsers <userlist><br /> - AND/OR -<br />AllowGroups <grouplist>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>First occurrence of a option takes precedence, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Match</xhtml:span> set statements withstanding. If <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Include</xhtml:span> locations are enabled, used, and order of precedence is understood in your environment, the entry may be created in a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> file in a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Include</xhtml:span> directory.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:strong>Be advised</xhtml:strong> that these options are "ANDed" together. If both <xhtml:span class="inline_block">AllowUsers</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">AllowGroups</xhtml:span> are set, connections will be limited to the list of users that are also a member of an allowed group. It is recommended that only one be set for clarity and ease of administration.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>It is easier to manage an allow list than a deny list. In a deny list, you could potentially add a user or group and forget to add it to the deny list.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command and verify the output:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># sshd -T | grep -Pi -- '^\h*(allow|deny)(users|groups)\h+\H+'
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Verify that the output matches at least one of the following lines:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">allowusers <userlist><br />-OR-<br />allowgroups <grouplist><br />-OR-<br />denyusers <userlist><br />-OR-<br />denygroups <grouplist>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Review the list(s) to ensure included users and/or groups follow local site policy</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Match</xhtml:span> set statements are used in your environment, specify the connection parameters to use for the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">-T</xhtml:span> extended test mode and run the audit to verify the setting is not incorrectly configured in a match block</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example additional audit needed for a match block for the user <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sshuser</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># sshd -T -C user=sshuser | grep -Pi -- '^\h*(allow|deny)(users|groups)\h+\H+'
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> If provided, any Match directives in the configuration file that would apply are applied before the configuration is written to standard output. The connection parameters are supplied as keyword=value pairs and may be supplied in any order, either with multiple <xhtml:span class="inline_block">-C</xhtml:span> options or as a comma-separated list. The keywords are <xhtml:span class="inline_block">addr</xhtml:span> (source address), <xhtml:span class="inline_block">user</xhtml:span> (user), <xhtml:span class="inline_block">host</xhtml:span> (resolved source host name), <xhtml:span class="inline_block">laddr</xhtml:span> (local address), <xhtml:span class="inline_block">lport</xhtml:span> (local port number), and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rdomain</xhtml:span> (routing domain).</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure sshd Banner is configured
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Banner</xhtml:span> parameter specifies a file whose contents must be sent to the remote user before authentication is permitted. By default, no banner is displayed.</xhtml:p>
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Banners are used to warn connecting users of the particular site's policy regarding connection. Presenting a warning message prior to the normal user login may assist the prosecution of trespassers on the computer system.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: CM-1, CM-2, CM-6, CM-7, IA-5

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config</xhtml:span> file to set the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Banner</xhtml:span> parameter above any <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Include</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Match</xhtml:span> entries as follows:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">Banner /etc/issue.net
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> First occurrence of a option takes precedence, Match set statements withstanding. If Include locations are enabled, used, and order of precedence is understood in your environment, the entry may be created in a file in Include location.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Edit the file being called by the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Banner</xhtml:span> argument with the appropriate contents according to your site policy, remove any instances of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">\m</xhtml:span> , <xhtml:span class="inline_block">\r</xhtml:span> , <xhtml:span class="inline_block">\s</xhtml:span> , <xhtml:span class="inline_block">\v</xhtml:span> or references to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">OS platform</xhtml:span></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># printf '%s\n' "Authorized users only. All activity may be monitored and reported." > "$(sshd -T | awk '$1 == "banner" {print $2}')"
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Banner</xhtml:span> is set:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># sshd -T | grep -Pi -- '^banner\h+\/\H+'
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">banner /etc/issue.net
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Match</xhtml:span> set statements are used in your environment, specify the connection parameters to use for the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">-T</xhtml:span> extended test mode and run the audit to verify the setting is not incorrectly configured in a match block</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example additional audit needed for a match block for the user <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sshuser</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># sshd -T -C user=sshuser | grep -Pi -- '^banner\h+\/\H+'
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> If provided, any Match directives in the configuration file that would apply are applied before the configuration is written to standard output. The connection parameters are supplied as keyword=value pairs and may be supplied in any order, either with multiple <xhtml:span class="inline_block">-C</xhtml:span> options or as a comma-separated list. The keywords are <xhtml:span class="inline_block">addr</xhtml:span> (source address), <xhtml:span class="inline_block">user</xhtml:span> (user), <xhtml:span class="inline_block">host</xhtml:span> (resolved source host name), <xhtml:span class="inline_block">laddr</xhtml:span> (local address), <xhtml:span class="inline_block">lport</xhtml:span> (local port number), and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rdomain</xhtml:span> (routing domain).</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command and verify that the contents or the file being called by the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Banner</xhtml:span> argument match site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># [ -e "$(sshd -T | awk '$1 == "banner" {print $2}')" ] && cat "$(sshd -T | awk '$1 == "banner" {print $2}')"
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command and verify no results are returned:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Psi -- "(\\\v|\\\r|\\\m|\\\s|\b$(grep '^ID=' /etc/os-release | cut -d= -f2 | sed -e 's/"//g')\b)" "$(sshd -T | awk '$1 == "banner" {print $2}')"
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure sshd Ciphers are configured
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>This variable limits the ciphers that SSH can use during communication.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Notes:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Some organizations may have stricter requirements for approved ciphers.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Ensure that ciphers used are in compliance with site policy.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The only "strong" ciphers currently FIPS 140 compliant are:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:a href="mailto:aes256-gcm@openssh.com">aes256-gcm@openssh.com</xhtml:a></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:a href="mailto:aes128-gcm@openssh.com">aes128-gcm@openssh.com</xhtml:a></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>aes256-ctr</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>aes192-ctr</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>aes128-ctr</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

safeguard.title: Encrypt Sensitive Data in Transit
Encrypt All Sensitive Information in Transit

Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>Weak ciphers  that are used for authentication to the cryptographic module cannot be relied upon to provide confidentiality or integrity, and system data may be compromised.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>The Triple DES ciphers, as used in SSH, have a birthday bound of approximately four billion blocks, which makes it easier for remote attackers to obtain clear text data via a birthday attack against a long-duration encrypted session, aka a "Sweet32" attack.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Error handling in the SSH protocol; Client and Server, when using a block cipher algorithm in Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode, makes it easier for remote attackers to recover certain plain text data from an arbitrary block of cipher text in an SSH session via unknown vectors.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit the /etc/ssh/sshd_config file and add/modify the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Ciphers</xhtml:span> line to contain a comma separated list of the site unapproved (weak) Ciphers preceded with a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">-</xhtml:span> above any <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Include</xhtml:span> entries:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">Ciphers -3des-cbc,aes128-cbc,aes192-cbc,aes256-cbc,chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">CVE-2023-48795</xhtml:span> has been addressed, and it meets local site policy, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com</xhtml:span> may be removed from the list of excluded ciphers.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> First occurrence of an option takes precedence. If Include locations are enabled, used, and order of precedence is understood in your environment, the entry may be created in a file in Include location.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify none of the "weak" ciphers are being used:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># sshd -T | grep -Pi -- '^ciphers\h+\"?([^#\n\r]+,)?((3des|blowfish|cast128|aes(128|192|256))-cbc|arcfour(128|256)?|rijndael-cbc@lysator\.liu\.se|chacha20-poly1305@openssh\.com)\b'
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> a line is returned, review the list of ciphers. If the line includes <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com</xhtml:span>, review <xhtml:span class="inline_block">CVE-2023-48795</xhtml:span> and verify the system has been patched. No ciphers in the list below should be returned as they're considered "weak":</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">3des-cbc<br />aes128-cbc<br />aes192-cbc<br />aes256-cbc
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure sshd ClientAliveInterval and ClientAliveCountMax are configured
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> To clarify, the two settings described below are only meant for idle connections from a protocol perspective and are not meant to check if the user is active or not. An idle user does not mean an idle connection. SSH does not and never had, intentionally, the capability to drop idle users. In SSH versions before <xhtml:span class="inline_block">8.2p1</xhtml:span> there was a bug that caused these values to behave in such a manner that they were abused to disconnect idle users. This bug has been resolved in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">8.2p1</xhtml:span> and thus it can no longer be abused disconnect idle users.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The two options <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ClientAliveInterval</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ClientAliveCountMax</xhtml:span> control the timeout of SSH sessions. Taken directly from <xhtml:span class="inline_block">man 5 sshd_config</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">ClientAliveInterval</xhtml:span> Sets a timeout interval in seconds after which if no data has been received from the client, sshd(8) will send a message through the encrypted channel to request a response from the client. The default is 0, indicating that these messages will not be sent to the client.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">ClientAliveCountMax</xhtml:span> Sets the number of client alive messages which may be sent without sshd(8) receiving any messages back from the client. If this threshold is reached while client alive messages are being sent, sshd will disconnect the client, terminating the session.  It is important to note that the use of client alive messages is very different from TCPKeepAlive. The client alive messages are sent through the encrypted channel and therefore will not be spoofable. The TCP keepalive option en‐abled by TCPKeepAlive is spoofable. The client alive mechanism is valuable when the client or server depend on knowing when a connection has become unresponsive.
The default value is 3. If ClientAliveInterval is set to 15, and ClientAliveCountMax is left at the default, unresponsive SSH clients will be disconnected after approximately 45 seconds. Setting a zero ClientAliveCountMax disables connection termination.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

metadata.notes:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:a href="https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1873547">https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1873547</xhtml:a></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:a href="https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_8_9/serverloop.c#L137">https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_8_9/serverloop.c#L137</xhtml:a></xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>In order to prevent resource exhaustion, appropriate values should be set for both <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ClientAliveInterval</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ClientAliveCountMax</xhtml:span>. Specifically, looking at the source code, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ClientAliveCountMax</xhtml:span> must be greater than zero in order to utilize the ability of SSH to drop idle connections. If connections are allowed to stay open indefinitely, this can potentially be used as a DDOS attack or simple resource exhaustion could occur over unreliable networks.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The example set here is a 45 second timeout. Consult your site policy for network timeouts and apply as appropriate.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: CM-1, CM-2, CM-6, CM-7, IA-5

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config</xhtml:span> file to set the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ClientAliveInterval</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ClientAliveCountMax</xhtml:span> parameters above any <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Include</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Match</xhtml:span> entries according to site policy.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">ClientAliveInterval 15<br />ClientAliveCountMax 3
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> First occurrence of a option takes precedence, Match set statements withstanding. If Include locations are enabled, used, and order of precedence is understood in your environment, the entry may be created in a file in Include location.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command and verify <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ClientAliveInterval</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ClientAliveCountMax</xhtml:span> are greater than zero:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># sshd -T | grep -Pi -- '(clientaliveinterval|clientalivecountmax)'
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example Output:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">clientaliveinterval 15<br />clientalivecountmax 3
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Match</xhtml:span> set statements are used in your environment, specify the connection parameters to use for the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">-T</xhtml:span> extended test mode and run the audit to verify the setting is not incorrectly configured in a match block</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example additional audit needed for a match block for the user <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sshuser</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># sshd -T -C user=sshuser | grep -Pi -- '(clientaliveinterval|clientalivecountmax)'
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> If provided, any Match directives in the configuration file that would apply are applied before the configuration is written to standard output. The connection parameters are supplied as keyword=value pairs and may be supplied in any order, either with multiple <xhtml:span class="inline_block">-C</xhtml:span> options or as a comma-separated list. The keywords are <xhtml:span class="inline_block">addr</xhtml:span> (source address), <xhtml:span class="inline_block">user</xhtml:span> (user), <xhtml:span class="inline_block">host</xhtml:span> (resolved source host name), <xhtml:span class="inline_block">laddr</xhtml:span> (local address), <xhtml:span class="inline_block">lport</xhtml:span> (local port number), and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rdomain</xhtml:span> (routing domain).</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure sshd DisableForwarding is enabled
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">DisableForwarding</xhtml:span> parameter disables all forwarding features, including X11, ssh-agent(1), TCP and StreamLocal. This option overrides all other forwarding-related options and may simplify restricted configurations.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>X11Forwarding provides the ability to tunnel X11 traffic through the connection to enable remote graphic connections.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>ssh-agent is a program to hold private keys used for public key authentication. Through use of environment variables the agent can be located and automatically used for authentication when logging in to other machines using ssh.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>SSH port forwarding is a mechanism in SSH for tunneling application ports from the client to the server, or servers to clients. It can be used for adding encryption to legacy applications, going through firewalls, and some system administrators and IT professionals use it for opening backdoors into the internal network from their home machines.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

safeguard.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software
Ensure Only Approved Ports, Protocols and Services Are Running

Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>Disable X11 forwarding unless there is an operational requirement to use X11 applications directly. There is a small risk that the remote X11 servers of users who are logged in via SSH with X11 forwarding could be compromised by other users on the X11 server. Note that even if X11 forwarding is disabled, users can always install their own forwarders.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>anyone with root privilege on the the intermediate server can make free use of ssh-agent to authenticate them to other servers</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Leaving port forwarding enabled can expose the organization to security risks and backdoors. SSH connections are protected with strong encryption. This makes their contents invisible to most deployed network monitoring and traffic filtering solutions. This invisibility carries considerable risk potential if it is used for malicious purposes such as data exfiltration. Cybercriminals or malware could exploit SSH to hide their unauthorized communications, or to exfiltrate stolen data from the target network.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/ssh/sshd_config</xhtml:span> file to set the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">DisableForwarding</xhtml:span> parameter to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">yes</xhtml:span> above any <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Include</xhtml:span> entry as follows:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">DisableForwarding yes
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> First occurrence of a option takes precedence. If Include locations are enabled, used, and order of precedence is understood in your environment, the entry may be created in a file in Include location.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>SSH tunnels are widely used in many corporate environments. In some environments the applications themselves may have very limited native support for security. By utilizing tunneling, compliance with SOX, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, and other standards can be achieved without having to modify the applications.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify <xhtml:span class="inline_block">DisableForwarding</xhtml:span> is set to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">yes</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># sshd -T | grep -i disableforwarding<br /><br />disableforwarding yes
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Group.title: Configure privilege escalation
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>There are various tools which allows a permitted user to execute a command as the superuser or another user, as specified by the security policy.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>sudo</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:a href="https://www.sudo.ws/">sudo documentation</xhtml:a></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The invoking user's real (not effective) user ID is used to determine the user name with which to query the security policy.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo</xhtml:span> supports a plug-in architecture for security policies and input/output logging.  Third parties can develop and distribute their own policy and I/O logging plug-ins to work seamlessly with the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo</xhtml:span> front end.   The default security policy is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudoers</xhtml:span>, which is configured via the file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers</xhtml:span> and any entries in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers.d</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>pkexec</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:a href="https://www.freedesktop.org/software/polkit/docs/0.105/pkexec.1.html">pkexec documentation</xhtml:a></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">pkexec</xhtml:span> allows an authorized user to execute <xhtml:em>PROGRAM</xhtml:em> as another user. If <xhtml:em>username</xhtml:em> is not specified, then the program will be executed as the administrative super user, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo</xhtml:span> supports a plug-in architecture for security policies and input/output logging.  Third parties can develop and distribute their own policy and I/O logging plug-ins to work seamlessly with the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo</xhtml:span> front end. The default security policy is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudoers</xhtml:span>, which is configured via the file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers</xhtml:span> and any entries in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers.d</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The security policy determines what privileges, if any, a user has to run <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo</xhtml:span>. The policy may require that users authenticate themselves with a password or another authentication mechanism. If authentication is required, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo</xhtml:span> will exit if the user's password is not entered within a configurable time limit. This limit is policy-specific.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>First determine is LDAP functionality is required. If so, then install <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo-ldap</xhtml:span>, else install <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># apt install sudo
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Attackers can run a malicious program using <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo</xhtml:span> which would fork a background process that remains even when the main program has finished executing.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit the file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers</xhtml:span> with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">visudo</xhtml:span> or a file in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers.d/</xhtml:span> with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">visudo -f <PATH TO FILE></xhtml:span> and add the following line:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">Defaults use_pty
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Edit the file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers</xhtml:span> with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">visudo</xhtml:span> and any files in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers.d/</xhtml:span> with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">visudo -f <PATH TO FILE></xhtml:span> and remove any occurrence of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">!use_pty</xhtml:span></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>sudo will read each file in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers.d</xhtml:span>, skipping file names that end in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">~</xhtml:span> or contain a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.</xhtml:span> character to avoid causing problems with package manager or editor temporary/backup files.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Files are parsed in sorted lexical order. That is, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers.d/01_first</xhtml:span> will be parsed before <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers.d/10_second</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Be aware that because the sorting is lexical, not numeric, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers.d/1_whoops</xhtml:span> would be loaded after <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers.d/10_second</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Using a consistent number of leading zeroes in the file names can be used to avoid such problems.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>WARNING:</xhtml:strong> Editing the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo</xhtml:span> configuration incorrectly can cause <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo</xhtml:span> to stop functioning. Always use <xhtml:span class="inline_block">visudo</xhtml:span> to modify <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo</xhtml:span> configuration files.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Verify the output matches:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">/etc/sudoers:Defaults use_pty
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the follow command to to verify <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Defaults !use_pty</xhtml:span> is not set:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -rPi -- '^\h*Defaults\h+([^#\n\r]+,\h*)?!use_pty\b' /etc/sudoers*

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Setting a timeout value reduces the window of opportunity for unauthorized privileged access to another user.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>If the currently configured timeout is larger than 15 minutes, edit the file listed in the audit section with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">visudo -f <PATH TO FILE></xhtml:span> and modify the entry <xhtml:span class="inline_block">timestamp_timeout=</xhtml:span> to 15 minutes or less as per your site policy. The value is in minutes. This particular entry may appear on it's own, or on the same line as <xhtml:span class="inline_block">env_reset</xhtml:span>. See the following two examples:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">Defaults    env_reset, timestamp_timeout=15
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">Defaults    timestamp_timeout=15<br />Defaults    env_reset
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Ensure that the caching timeout is no more than 15 minutes.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Example:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -roP "timestamp_timeout=\K[0-9]*" /etc/sudoers*
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>If there is no <xhtml:span class="inline_block">timestamp_timeout</xhtml:span> configured in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers*</xhtml:span> then the default is 15 minutes. This default can be checked with:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># sudo -V | grep "Authentication timestamp timeout:"
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>NOTE:</xhtml:strong> A value of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">-1</xhtml:span> means that the timeout is disabled. Depending on the configuration of the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">timestamp_type</xhtml:span>, this could mean for all terminals / processes of that user and not just that one single terminal session.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

artifact_expression.artifact_title: Ensure no file named /etc/sudoers exists and matches pattern (?i)^\h*defaults\h+(?:[^#\n\r]+\h*,\h*)?timestamp_timeout=(-1|1[6-9]|[2-9][0-9]|[1-9][0-9][0-9]+)\b(\h*,\h*.*)?$
Ensure no file(s) named ^.+\.conf$ in /etc/sudoers.d/ exists and matches pattern (?i)^\h*defaults\h+(?:[^#\n\r]+\h*,\h*)?timestamp_timeout=(-1|1[6-9]|[2-9][0-9]|[1-9][0-9][0-9]+)\b(\h*,\h*.*)?$

Rule.title: Ensure access to the su command is restricted
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">su</xhtml:span> command allows a user to run a command or shell as another user. The program has been superseded by <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo</xhtml:span>, which allows for more granular control over privileged access. Normally, the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">su</xhtml:span> command can be executed by any user. By uncommenting the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_wheel.so</xhtml:span> statement in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/su</xhtml:span>, the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">su</xhtml:span> command will only allow users in a specific groups to execute <xhtml:span class="inline_block">su</xhtml:span>. This group should be empty to reinforce the use of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo</xhtml:span> for privileged access.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Protect Information through  Access Control Lists

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Restricting the use of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">su</xhtml:span> , and using <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo</xhtml:span> in its place, provides system administrators better control of the escalation of user privileges to execute privileged commands. The sudo utility also provides a better logging and audit mechanism, as it can log each command executed via <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo</xhtml:span> , whereas <xhtml:span class="inline_block">su</xhtml:span> can only record that a user executed the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">su</xhtml:span> program.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Create an empty group that will be specified for use of the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">su</xhtml:span> command.  The group should be named according to site policy.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Example:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># groupadd sugroup
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Add the following line to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/su</xhtml:span> file, specifying the empty group:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">auth required pam_wheel.so use_uid group=sugroup
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pi '^\h*auth\h+(?:required|requisite)\h+pam_wheel\.so\h+(?:[^#\n\r]+\h+)?((?!\2)(use_uid\b|group=\H+\b))\h+(?:[^#\n\r]+\h+)?((?!\1)(use_uid\b|group=\H+\b))(\h+.*)?$' /etc/pam.d/su
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Verify the output matches:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">auth required pam_wheel.so use_uid group=<group_name>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command and verify that the group specified in <xhtml:span class="inline_block"><group_name></xhtml:span> contains no users:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep <group_name> /etc/group
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Verify the output does not contain any users in the relevant group:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"><group_name>:x:<GID>:
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

artifact_expression.artifact_title: Ensure at least one file named /etc/pam.d/su exists and matches pattern (?i)^\h*auth\h+(?:required|requisite)\h+pam_wheel\.so\h+(?:[^#\n\r]+\h+)?((?!\2)(use_uid\b|group=\H+\b))\h+(?:[^#\n\r]+\h+)?((?!\1)(use_uid\b|group=\H+\b))(\h+.*)?$

Group.title: Configure pam-auth-update profiles
Group.description:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam-auth-update</xhtml:span> is a utility that permits configuring the central authentication policy for the system using pre-defined profiles as supplied by PAM  module  packages.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Profiles - Shipped in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/share/pam-configs/</xhtml:span> directory specify the modules, with options, to enable; the preferred ordering with respect to other profiles; and whether a profile should be enabled by default. Packages providing PAM modules register their profiles at install time by calling pam-auth-update --package.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Selection of profiles is done using the standard <xhtml:span class="inline_block">debconf</xhtml:span> interface. The profile selection question will be asked at <xhtml:span class="inline_block">medium</xhtml:span> priority when packages are added or removed, so no user interaction is required by default. Users may invoke <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam-auth-update</xhtml:span> directly to change their authentication configuration.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam-auth-update</xhtml:span> script makes every effort to respect local changes to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/common-*.</xhtml:span> Local modifications to the list of module options will be preserved, and additions of modules within the managed portion of the stack will cause pam-auth-update to treat the config files as locally modified and not make further changes to the config files unless given the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">--force</xhtml:span> option.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>If the user specifies that <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam-auth-update</xhtml:span> should override local configuration changes, the locally-modified files will be saved in /etc/pam.d/ with a suffix of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.pam-old</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure pam_unix module is enabled
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_unix</xhtml:span> is the standard Unix authentication module. It uses standard calls from the system's libraries to retrieve and set account information as well as authentication. Usually this is obtained from the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> and if shadow is enabled, the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span> file as well.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The account component performs the task of establishing the status of the user's account and password based on the following shadow elements: <xhtml:span class="inline_block">expire</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">last_change</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">max_change</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">min_change</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">warn_change</xhtml:span>. In the case of the latter, it may offer advice to the user on changing their password or, through the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PAM_AUTHTOKEN_REQD</xhtml:span> return, delay giving service to the user until they have established a new password. The entries listed above are documented in the shadow(5) manual page. Should the user's record not contain one or more of these entries, the corresponding shadow check is not performed.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The authentication component performs the task of checking the users credentials (password). The default action of this module is to not permit the user access to a service if their official password is blank.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Protect Information through  Access Control Lists

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>The system should only provide access after performing authentication of a user.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to enable the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_unix</xhtml:span> module:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update --enable unix
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> If a site specific custom profile is being used in your environment to configure PAM that includes the configuration for the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_faillock</xhtml:span> module, enable that module instead</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:

<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -P -- '\bpam_unix\.so\b' /etc/pam.d/common-{account,session,auth,password}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Output should be simular to:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">/etc/pam.d/common-account:account   [success=1 new_authtok_reqd=done default=ignore]   pam_unix.so<br />/etc/pam.d/common-session:session   required   pam_unix.so<br />/etc/pam.d/common-auth:auth   [success=2 default=ignore]   pam_unix.so try_first_pass<br />/etc/pam.d/common-password:password   [success=1 default=ignore]   pam_unix.so obscure use_authtok try_first_pass yescrypt
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure pam_faillock module is enabled
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_faillock.so</xhtml:span> module maintains a list of failed authentication attempts per user during a specified interval and locks the account in case there were more than the configured number of consecutive failed authentications (this is defined by the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">deny</xhtml:span> parameter in the faillock configuration). It stores the failure records into per-user files in the tally directory.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Establish an Access Revoking Process
Establish Process for Revoking Access

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Locking out user IDs after n unsuccessful consecutive login attempts mitigates brute force password attacks against your systems.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Create two pam-auth-update profiles in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/share/pam-configs/</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:li>Create the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">faillock</xhtml:span> profile in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/share/pam-configs/</xhtml:span> with the following lines:</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">Name: Enable pam_faillock to deny access<br />Default: yes<br />Priority: 0<br />Auth-Type: Primary<br />Auth:<br />        [default=die]                   pam_faillock.so authfail
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example Script:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   arr=('Name: Enable pam_faillock to deny access' 'Default: yes' 'Priority: 0' 'Auth-Type: Primary' 'Auth:' '        [default=die]                   pam_faillock.so authfail') <br />   printf '%s\n' "${arr[@]}" > /usr/share/pam-configs/faillock<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:ol start="2">
<xhtml:li>Create the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">faillock_notify</xhtml:span> profile in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/share/pam-configs/</xhtml:span> with the following lines:</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">Name: Notify of failed login attempts and reset count upon success<br />Default: yes<br />Priority: 1024<br />Auth-Type: Primary<br />Auth:<br />        requisite                       pam_faillock.so preauth<br />Account-Type: Primary<br />Account:<br />        required                        pam_faillock.so
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example Script:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   arr=('Name: Notify of failed login attempts and reset count upon success' 'Default: yes' 'Priority: 1024' 'Auth-Type: Primary' 'Auth:' '        requisite                       pam_faillock.so preauth' 'Account-Type: Primary' 'Account:' '        required                        pam_faillock.so') <br />   printf '%s\n' "${arr[@]}" > /usr/share/pam-configs/faillock_notify<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to update the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">common-auth</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">common-account</xhtml:span> PAM files with the new profiles:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update --enable <profile_filename>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update --enable faillock<br /># pam-auth-update --enable faillock_notify
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>The name used for the file must be used in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam-auth-update --enable</xhtml:span> command</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Name:</xhtml:span> line should be easily recognizable and understood</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Priority:</xhtml:span> Line is important as it effects the order of the lines in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/</xhtml:span> files</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>If a site specific custom profile is being used in your environment to configure PAM that includes the configuration for the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_faillock</xhtml:span> module, enable that module instead</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following commands to verify that <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_faillock</xhtml:span> is enabled:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -P -- '\bpam_faillock\.so\b' /etc/pam.d/common-{auth,account}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Output should be similar to:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">/etc/pam.d/common-auth:auth     requisite                       pam_faillock.so preauth<br />/etc/pam.d/common-auth:auth     [default=die]                   pam_faillock.so authfail<br />/etc/pam.d/common-account:account       required                        pam_faillock.so
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Ensure at least one file named /etc/pam.d/common-auth exists and matches pattern (?i)^\h*auth\h+([^#\n\r]+)\h+pam_faillock\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?authfail\b

Rule.title: Ensure pam_pwquality module is enabled
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwquality.so</xhtml:span> module performs password quality checking. This module can be plugged into the password stack of a given service to provide strength-checking for passwords. The code was originally based on pam_cracklib module and the module is backwards compatible with its options.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The action of this module is to prompt the user for a password and check its strength against a system dictionary and a set of rules for identifying poor choices.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The first action is to prompt for a single password, check its strength and then, if it is considered strong, prompt for the password a second time (to verify that it was typed correctly on the first occasion). All being well, the password is passed on to subsequent modules to be installed as the new authentication token.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Use Unique Passwords
Use Unique Passwords

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Use of a unique, complex passwords helps to increase the time and resources required to compromise the password.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to verify the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwquality.so</xhtml:span> line exists in a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam-auth-update</xhtml:span> profile:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -P -- '\bpam_pwquality\.so\b' /usr/share/pam-configs/*
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Output should be similar to:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">/usr/share/pam-configs/pwquality:       requisite                       pam_pwquality.so retry=3<br />/usr/share/pam-configs/pwquality:       requisite                       pam_pwquality.so retry=3
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> similar output is returned:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to update <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/common-password</xhtml:span> with the returned profile:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update --enable {PROFILE_NAME}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update pwquality
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> similar output is <xhtml:strong>NOT</xhtml:strong> returned:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Create a pam-auth-update profile in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/share/pam-configs/</xhtml:span> with the following lines:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">Name: Pwquality password strength checking<br />Default: yes<br />Priority: 1024<br />Conflicts: cracklib<br />Password-Type: Primary<br />Password:<br />        requisite                       pam_pwquality.so retry=3
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   arr=('Name: Pwquality password strength checking' 'Default: yes' 'Priority: 1024' 'Conflicts: cracklib' 'Password-Type: Primary' 'Password:' '        requisite                       pam_pwquality.so retry=3')<br />   printf '%s\n' "${arr[@]}" > /usr/share/pam-configs/pwquality<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to update <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/common-password</xhtml:span> with the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pwquality</xhtml:span> profile:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update --enable pwquality
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>The name used for the file must be used in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam-auth-update --enable</xhtml:span> command</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Name:</xhtml:span> line should be easily recognizable and understood</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Priority:</xhtml:span> Line is important as it effects the order of the lines in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/</xhtml:span> files</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>If a site specific custom profile is being used in your environment to configure PAM that includes the configuration for the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwquality</xhtml:span> module, enable that module instead</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify that pam_pwhistory is enabled:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -P -- '\bpam_pwquality\.so\b' /etc/pam.d/common-password
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Output should be similar to:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">password   requisite   pam_pwquality.so retry=3
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure pam_pwhistory module is enabled
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwhistory.so</xhtml:span> module saves the last passwords for each user in order to force password change history and keep the user from alternating between the same password too frequently.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>This module does not work together with kerberos. In general, it does not make much sense to use this module in conjunction with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">NIS</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">LDAP</xhtml:span>, since the old passwords are stored on the local machine and are not available on another machine for password history checking.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Use Unique Passwords
Use Unique Passwords

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Use of a unique, complex passwords helps to increase the time and resources required to compromise the password.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to verify the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwquality.so</xhtml:span> line exists in a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam-auth-update</xhtml:span> profile:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -P -- '\bpam_pwhistory\.so\b' /usr/share/pam-configs/*
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Output should be similar to:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">/usr/share/pam-configs/pwhistory:   requisite   pam_pwhistory.so remember=24 enforce_for_root try_first_pass use_authtok
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> similar output is returned:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to update <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/common-password</xhtml:span> with the returned profile:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update --enable {PROFILE_NAME}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update pwhistory
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> similar output is <xhtml:strong>NOT</xhtml:strong> returned:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Create a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pwhistory</xhtml:span> profile in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/share/pam-configs/</xhtml:span> with the following lines:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">Name: pwhistory password history checking<br />Default: yes<br />Priority: 1024<br />Password-Type: Primary<br />Password: requisite pam_pwhistory.so remember=24 enforce_for_root try_first_pass use_authtok
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example Script:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   arr=('Name: pwhistory password history checking' 'Default: yes' 'Priority: 1024' 'Password-Type: Primary' 'Password:' '        requisite                       pam_pwhistory.so remember=24 enforce_for_root try_first_pass use_authtok')<br />   printf '%s\n' "${arr[@]}" > /usr/share/pam-configs/pwhistory<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to update <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/common-password</xhtml:span> with the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pwhistory</xhtml:span> profile:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update --enable pwhistory
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>The name used for the file must be used in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam-auth-update --enable</xhtml:span> command</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Name:</xhtml:span> line should be easily recognizable and understood</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Priority:</xhtml:span> Line is important as it effects the order of the lines in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/</xhtml:span> files</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>If a site specific custom profile is being used in your environment to configure PAM that includes the configuration for the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwhistory</xhtml:span> module, enable that module instead</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify that pam_pwhistory is enabled:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -P -- '\bpam_pwhistory\.so\b' /etc/pam.d/common-password
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Output should be similar to:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">password   requisite   pam_pwhistory.so remember=24 enforce_for_root try_first_pass use_authtok
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
