Group.title: Configure PAM Arguments
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) uses arguments to pass information to a pluggable module during authentication for a particular module type. These arguments allow the PAM configuration files for particular programs to use a common PAM module but in different ways.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Invalid arguments are ignored and do not otherwise affect the success or failure of the PAM module. When an invalid argument is passed, an error is usually written to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/var/log/messages</xhtml:span> file. However, since the reporting method is controlled by the PAM module, the module must be written correctly to log the error to this file.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> If custom PAM files are being used, for this section's remediation, the corresponding files in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/</xhtml:span> would need to be edited directly, and the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam-auth-update --enable <EDITED_PROFILE_NAME></xhtml:span> command skipped</xhtml:p>

Group.title: Configure pam_faillock module
Group.description:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_faillock.so</xhtml:span> provides a way to configure the default settings for locking the user after multiple failed authentication attempts.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Options:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block"><dir=/path/to/tally-directory></xhtml:span> - The directory where the user files with the failure records are kept. The default is /var/run/faillock. Note: These files will disappear after reboot on systems configured with directory /var/run/faillock mounted on virtual memory.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">audit</xhtml:span> - Will log the user name into the system log if the user is not found.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">silent</xhtml:span> - Don't print informative messages to the user. Please note that when this option is not used there will be difference in the authentication behavior for users which exist on the system and non-existing users.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">no_log_info</xhtml:span> - Don't log informative messages via syslog(3).</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">local_users_only</xhtml:span> - Only track failed user authentications attempts for local users in /etc/passwd and ignore centralized (AD, IdM, LDAP, etc.) users. The faillock(8) command will also no longer track user failed authentication attempts. Enabling this option will prevent a double-lockout scenario where a user is locked out locally and in the centralized mechanism.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">nodelay</xhtml:span> - Don't enforce a delay after authentication failures.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">deny=<n></xhtml:span> - Deny access if the number of consecutive authentication failures for this user during the recent interval exceeds <xhtml:em></xhtml:em>. The default is 3.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">fail_interval=n</xhtml:span> - The length of the interval during which the consecutive authentication failures must happen for the user account lock out is n seconds. The default is 900 (15 minutes).</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">unlock_time=n</xhtml:span> - The access will be re-enabled after n seconds after the lock out. The value 0 has the same meaning as value never - the access will not be re-enabled without resetting the faillock entries by the faillock(8) command. The default is 600 (10 minutes). Note that the default directory that pam_faillock uses is usually cleared on system boot so the access will be also re-enabled after system reboot. If that is undesirable a different tally directory must be set with the dir option. Also note that it is usually undesirable to permanently lock out users as they can become easily a target of denial of service attack unless the usernames are random and kept secret to potential attackers.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">even_deny_root</xhtml:span> - Root account can become locked as well as regular accounts.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">root_unlock_time=n</xhtml:span> - This option implies even_deny_root option. Allow access after n seconds to root account after the account is locked. In case the option is not specified the value is the same as of the unlock_time option.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">admin_group=name</xhtml:span> - If a group name is specified with this option, members of the group will be handled by this module the same as the root account (the options even_deny_root and root_unlock_time will apply to them. By default the option is not set.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

Rule.title: Ensure password failed attempts lockout is configured
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">deny=<n></xhtml:span> option will deny access if the number of consecutive authentication failures for this user during the recent interval exceeds <xhtml:em></xhtml:em>.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Establish an Access Revoking Process
Establish Process for Revoking Access

metadata.notes: <xhtml:p>If a user has been locked out because they have reached the maximum consecutive failure count defined by <xhtml:span class="inline_block">deny=</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_faillock.so</xhtml:span> module, the user can be unlocked by issuing the command <xhtml:span class="inline_block">faillock --user &amp;lt;USERNAME&amp;amp;gt; --reset</xhtml:span>. This command sets the failed count to 0, effectively unlocking the user.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Locking out user IDs after <xhtml:em>n</xhtml:em> unsuccessful consecutive login attempts mitigates brute force password attacks against your systems.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Create or edit the following line in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/faillock.conf</xhtml:span> setting the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">deny</xhtml:span> option to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">5</xhtml:span> or less:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">deny = 5
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pl -- '\bpam_faillock\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?deny\b' /usr/share/pam-configs/*
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Edit any returned files and remove the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">deny=<N></xhtml:span> arguments from the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_faillock.so</xhtml:span> line(s):</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify that Number of failed logon attempts before the account is locked is no greater than <xhtml:span class="inline_block">5</xhtml:span> and meets local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pi -- '^\h*deny\h*=\h*[1-5]\b' /etc/security/faillock.conf<br /><br />deny = 5
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify that the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">deny</xhtml:span> argument has not been set, or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">5</xhtml:span> or less and meets local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pi -- '^\h*auth\h+(requisite|required|sufficient)\h+pam_faillock\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?deny\h*=\h*(0|[6-9]|[1-9][0-9]+)\b' /etc/pam.d/common-auth
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

artifact_expression.artifact_title: Ensure at least one file named /etc/security/faillock.conf exists and matches pattern (?i)^\h*deny\h*=\h*[1-5]\b
Ensure no file named /etc/pam.d/common-auth exists and matches pattern (?i)^\h*auth\h+(requisite|required|sufficient)\h+pam_faillock\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?deny\h*=\h*(0|[6-9]|[1-9][0-9]+)\b

Rule.title: Ensure password unlock time is configured
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">unlock_time=<n></xhtml:span> - The access will be re-enabled after <xhtml:em></xhtml:em> seconds after the lock out. The value <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> has the same meaning as value never - the access will not be re-enabled without resetting the faillock entries by the faillock(8) command.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>The default directory that pam_faillock uses is usually cleared on system boot so the access will be also re-enabled after system reboot. If that is undesirable a different tally directory must be set with the dir option.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>It is usually undesirable to permanently lock out users as they can become easily a target of denial of service attack unless the usernames are random and kept secret to potential attackers.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The maximum configurable value for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">unlock_time</xhtml:span> is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">604800</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

safeguard.title: Establish an Access Revoking Process
Establish Process for Revoking Access

metadata.notes: <xhtml:p>If a user has been locked out because they have reached the maximum consecutive failure count defined by <xhtml:span class="inline_block">deny=</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_faillock.so</xhtml:span> module, the user can be unlocked by issuing the command <xhtml:span class="inline_block">faillock --user &amp;lt;USERNAME&amp;amp;gt; --reset</xhtml:span>. This command sets the failed count to 0, effectively unlocking the user.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Locking out user IDs after <xhtml:em>n</xhtml:em> unsuccessful consecutive login attempts mitigates brute force password attacks against your systems.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Set password unlock time to conform to site policy. <xhtml:span class="inline_block">unlock_time</xhtml:span> should be <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> (never), or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">900</xhtml:span> seconds or greater.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/faillock.conf</xhtml:span> and update or add the following line:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">unlock_time = 900
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command: remove the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">unlock_time</xhtml:span> argument from the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_faillock.so</xhtml:span> module in the PAM files:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pl -- '\bpam_faillock\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?unlock_time\b' /usr/share/pam-configs/*
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Edit any returned files and remove the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">unlock_time=<N></xhtml:span> argument from the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_faillock.so</xhtml:span> line(s):</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Use of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">unlock_time=0</xhtml:span> may allow an attacker to cause denial of service to legitimate users. This will also require a systems administrator with elevated privileges to unlock the account.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify that the time in seconds before the account is unlocked is either <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> (never) or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">900</xhtml:span> (15 minutes) or more and meets local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pi -- '^\h*unlock_time\h*=\h*(0|9[0-9][0-9]|[1-9][0-9]{3,})\b' /etc/security/faillock.conf<br /><br />unlock_time = 900
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify that the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">unlock_time</xhtml:span> argument has not been set, or is either <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> (never) or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">900</xhtml:span> (15 minutes) or more and meets local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pi -- '^\h*auth\h+(requisite|required|sufficient)\h+pam_faillock\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?unlock_time\h*=\h*([1-9]|[1-9][0-9]|[1-8][0-9][0-9])\b' /etc/pam.d/common-auth
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Ensure no file named /etc/pam.d/common-auth exists and matches pattern (?i)^\h*auth\h+(requisite|required|sufficient)\h+pam_faillock\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?unlock_time\h*=\h*([1-9]|[1-9][0-9]|[1-8][0-9][0-9])\b

Rule.title: Ensure password failed attempts lockout includes root account
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">even_deny_root</xhtml:span> - Root account can become locked as well as regular accounts</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">root_unlock_time=n</xhtml:span> - This option implies even_deny_root option. Allow access after n seconds to root account after the account is locked. In case the option is not specified the value is the same as of the unlock_time option.</xhtml:p>

metadata.notes: <xhtml:p>If a user has been locked out because they have reached the maximum consecutive failure count defined by <xhtml:span class="inline_block">deny=</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_faillock.so</xhtml:span> module, the user can be unlocked by issuing the command <xhtml:span class="inline_block">faillock --user &amp;lt;USERNAME&amp;amp;gt; --reset</xhtml:span>. This command sets the failed count to 0, effectively unlocking the user.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Locking out user IDs after n unsuccessful consecutive login attempts mitigates brute force password attacks against your systems.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/faillock.conf</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Remove or update any line containing <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root_unlock_time</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong> set it to a value of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">60</xhtml:span> or more</xhtml:li>

</xhtml:ul>

</xhtml:code>

</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Edit any returned files and remove the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">even_deny_root</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root_unlock_time</xhtml:span> arguments from the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_faillock.so</xhtml:span> line(s):</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Use of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">unlock_time=0</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root_unlock_time=0</xhtml:span> may allow an attacker to cause denial of service to legitimate users.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

</xhtml:code>

</xhtml:code>

</xhtml:code>

Verify <xhtml:strong>-IF-</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root_unlock_time</xhtml:span> is set, it is set to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">60</xhtml:span> (One minute) or more:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pi -- '^\h*auth\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)pam_faillock\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?root_unlock_time\h*=\h*([1-9]|[1-5][0-9])\b' /etc/pam.d/common-auth
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Group.title: Configure pam_pwquality module
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwquality.so</xhtml:span> module checks the strength of passwords. It performs checks such as making sure a password is not a dictionary word, it is a certain length, contains a mix of characters (e.g. alphabet, numeric, other) and more.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>These checks are configurable by either:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>use of the module arguments</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>modifying the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf</xhtml:span> configuration file</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>creating a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> file in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/</xhtml:span> directory.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> The module arguments override the settings in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf</xhtml:span> configuration file. Settings in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf</xhtml:span> configuration file override settings in a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> file in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/</xhtml:span> directory.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The possible options in the file are:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">difok</xhtml:span> - Number of characters in the new password that must not be present in the old password. (default 1). The special value of 0 disables all checks of similarity of the new password with the old password except the new password being exactly the same as the old one.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">minlen</xhtml:span> - Minimum acceptable size for the new password (plus one if credits are not disabled which is the default). (See pam_pwquality(8).) Cannot be set to lower value than 6. (default 8)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">dcredit</xhtml:span> - The maximum credit for having digits in the new password. If less than 0 it is the minimum number of digits in the new password. (default 0)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">ucredit</xhtml:span> - The maximum credit for having uppercase characters in the new password.  If less than 0 it is the minimum number of uppercase characters in the new password. (default 0)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">lcredit</xhtml:span> - The maximum credit for having lowercase characters in the new password.  If less than 0 it is the minimum number of lowercase characters in the new password. (default 0)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">ocredit</xhtml:span> - The maximum credit for having other characters in the new password.  If less than 0 it is the minimum number of other characters in the new password. (default 0)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">minclass</xhtml:span> - The minimum number of required classes of characters for the new password (digits, uppercase, lowercase, others). (default 0)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">maxrepeat</xhtml:span> - The maximum number of allowed same consecutive characters in the new password.  The check is disabled if the value is 0. (default 0)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">maxsequence</xhtml:span> - The maximum length of monotonic character sequences in the new password.  Examples of such sequence are '12345' or 'fedcb'. Note that most such passwords will not pass the simplicity check unless the sequence is only a minor part of the password. The check is disabled if the value is 0. (default 0)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">maxclassrepeat</xhtml:span> - The maximum number of allowed consecutive characters of the same class in the new password. The check is disabled if the value is 0. (default 0)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">gecoscheck</xhtml:span> - If nonzero, check whether the words longer than 3 characters from the GECOS field of the user's passwd(5) entry are contained in the new password. The check is disabled if the value is 0. (default 0)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">dictcheck</xhtml:span> - If nonzero, check whether the password (with possible modifications) matches a word in a dictionary. Currently the dictionary check is performed
using the cracklib library. (default 1)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">usercheck=<N></xhtml:span> - If nonzero, check whether the password (with possible modifications) contains the user name in some form. It is not performed for user names
shorter than 3 characters. (default 1)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">usersubstr=<N></xhtml:span> - If greater than 3 (due to the minimum length in usercheck), check whether the password contains a substring of at least N length in some form.
(default 0)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">enforcing=<N></xhtml:span> - If nonzero, reject the password if it fails the checks, otherwise only print the warning. This setting applies only to the pam_pwquality module
and possibly other applications that explicitly change their behavior based on it. It does not affect pwmake(1) and pwscore(1). (default 1)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">badwords</xhtml:span> - Space separated list of words that must not be contained in the password. These are additional words to the cracklib dictionary check. This setting can be also used by applications to emulate the gecos check for user accounts that are not created yet.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">dictpath</xhtml:span> - Path to the cracklib dictionaries. Default is to use the cracklib default.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">retry=<N></xhtml:span> - Prompt user at most N times before returning with error. The default is 1.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">enforce_for_root</xhtml:span> - The module will return error on failed check even if the user changing the password is root. This option is off by default which means that just the message about the failed check is printed but root can change the password anyway. Note that root is not asked for an old password so the checks that compare the old and new password are not performed.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">local_users_only</xhtml:span> - The module will not test the password quality for users that are not present in the /etc/passwd file. The module still asks for the password so the following modules in the stack can use the use_authtok option. This option is off by default.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

Rule.title: Ensure password number of changed characters is configured
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pwquality</xhtml:span> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">difok</xhtml:span> option sets the number of characters in a password that must not be present in the old password.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Use Unique Passwords
Use Unique Passwords

Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>Use of a complex password helps to increase the time and resources required to compromise the password. Password complexity, or strength, is a measure of the effectiveness of a password in resisting attempts at guessing and brute-force attacks.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Password complexity is one factor of several that determines how long it takes to crack a password. The more complex the password, the greater the number of possible combinations that need to be tested before the password is compromised.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Create or modify a file ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/</xhtml:span> directory or the file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf</xhtml:span> and add or modify the following line to set <xhtml:span class="inline_block">difok</xhtml:span> to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">2</xhtml:span> or more. Ensure setting conforms to local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   sed -ri 's/^\s*difok\s*=/# &/' /etc/security/pwquality.conf<br />   [ ! -d /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/ ] && mkdir /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/<br />   printf '\n%s' "difok = 2" > /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/50-pwdifok.conf<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pl -- '\bpam_pwquality\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?difok\b' /usr/share/pam-configs/*
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Edit any returned files and remove the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">difok</xhtml:span> argument from the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwquality.so</xhtml:span> line(s):</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify that the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">difok</xhtml:span> option is set to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">2</xhtml:span> or more and follows local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Psi -- '^\h*difok\h*=\h*([2-9]|[1-9][0-9]+)\b' /etc/security/pwquality.conf /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/*.conf
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example output:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/50-pwdifok.conf:difok = 2
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Verify returned value(s) are <xhtml:span class="inline_block">2</xhtml:span> or more and meet local site policy</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify that <xhtml:span class="inline_block">difok</xhtml:span> is not set, is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">2</xhtml:span> or more, and conforms to local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Psi -- '^\h*password\h+(requisite|required|sufficient)\h+pam_pwquality\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?difok\h*=\h*([0-1])\b' /etc/pam.d/common-password
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>settings should be configured in only <xhtml:strong>one</xhtml:strong> location for clarity</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Settings observe an order of precedence:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>module arguments override the settings in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf</xhtml:span> configuration file</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>settings in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf</xhtml:span> configuration file override settings in a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> file in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/</xhtml:span> directory</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>settings in a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> file in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/</xhtml:span> directory are read in canonical order, with last read file containing the setting taking precedence</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>It is recommended that settings be configured in a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> file in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/</xhtml:span> directory for clarity, convenience, and durability.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure minimum password length is configured
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>The minimum password length setting determines the lowers number of characters that make up a password for a user account. There are many different theories about how to determine the best password length for an organization, but perhaps "passphrase" is a better term than "password".</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">minlen</xhtml:span> option sets the minimum acceptable size for the new password (plus one if credits are not disabled which is the default). Cannot be set to lower value than 6.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Use Unique Passwords
Use Unique Passwords

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Strong passwords help protect systems from password attacks. Types of password attacks include dictionary attacks, which attempt to use common words and phrases, and brute force attacks, which try every possible combination of characters. Also attackers may try to obtain the account database so they can use tools to discover the accounts and passwords.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Create or modify a file ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/</xhtml:span> directory or the file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf</xhtml:span> and add or modify the following line to set password length of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">14</xhtml:span> or more characters. Ensure that password length conforms to local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   sed -ri 's/^\s*minlen\s*=/# &/' /etc/security/pwquality.conf<br />   [ ! -d /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/ ] && mkdir /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/<br />   printf '\n%s' "minlen = 14" > /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/50-pwlength.conf<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pl -- '\bpam_pwquality\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?minlen\b' /usr/share/pam-configs/*
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Edit any returned files and remove the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">minlen</xhtml:span> argument from the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwquality.so</xhtml:span> line(s):</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>In general, it is true that longer passwords are better (harder to crack), but it is also true that forced password length requirements can cause user behavior that is predictable and undesirable. For example, requiring users to have a minimum 16-character password may cause them to choose repeating patterns like fourfourfourfour or passwordpassword that meet the requirement but aren’t hard to guess. Additionally, length requirements increase the chances that users will adopt other insecure practices, like writing them down, re-using them or storing them unencrypted in their documents.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Having a reasonable minimum length with no maximum character limit increases the resulting
average password length used (and therefore the strength).6</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example output:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>

</xhtml:code>

</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned</xhtml:p>

<xhtml:li>settings in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf</xhtml:span> configuration file override settings in a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> file in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/</xhtml:span> directory</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>settings in a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> file in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/</xhtml:span> directory are read in canonical order, with last read file containing the setting taking precedence</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

</xhtml:ul>

Rule.title: Ensure password complexity is configured
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>Password complexity can be set through:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">minclass</xhtml:span> - The minimum number of classes of characters required in a new password. (digits, uppercase, lowercase, others). e.g. <xhtml:span class="inline_block">minclass = 4</xhtml:span> requires digits, uppercase, lower case, and special characters.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">dcredit</xhtml:span> - The maximum credit for having digits in the new password. If less than <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> it is the minimum number of digits in the new password. e.g. <xhtml:span class="inline_block">dcredit = -1</xhtml:span> requires at least one digit</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">ucredit</xhtml:span> - The maximum credit for having uppercase characters in the new password. If less than <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> it is the minimum number of uppercase characters in the new password. e.g. <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ucredit = -1</xhtml:span> requires at least one uppercase character</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">ocredit</xhtml:span> - The maximum credit for having other characters in the new password. If less than <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> it is the minimum number of other characters in the new password. e.g. <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ocredit = -1</xhtml:span> requires at least one special character</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">lcredit</xhtml:span> - The maximum credit for having lowercase characters in the new password.  If less than <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> it is the minimum number of lowercase characters in the new password. e.g. <xhtml:span class="inline_block">lcredit = -1</xhtml:span> requires at least one lowercase character</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

safeguard.title: Use Unique Passwords
Use Unique Passwords

Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>Strong passwords protect systems from being hacked through brute force methods.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Requiring at least one non-alphabetic character increases the search space beyond pure dictionary words, which makes the resulting password harder to crack.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Forcing users to choose an excessively complex password, e.g. some combination of upper-case, lower-case, numbers, and special characters, has a negative impact. It places an extra burden on users and many will use predictable patterns (for example, a capital letter in the first position, followed by lowercase letters, then one or two numbers, and a “special character” at the end). Attackers know this, so dictionary attacks will often contain these common patterns and use the most common substitutions like, $ for s, @ for a, 1 for l, 0 for o.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pl -- '\bpam_pwquality\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?(minclass|[dulo]credit)\b' /usr/share/pam-configs/*
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Edit any returned files and remove the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">minclass</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">dcredit</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ucredit</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">lcredit</xhtml:span>, and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ocredit</xhtml:span> arguments from the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwquality.so</xhtml:span> line(s)</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Create or modify a file ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/</xhtml:span> directory or the file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf</xhtml:span> and add or modify the following line(s) to set complexity according to local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">minclass = _N_</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">dcredit = _N_</xhtml:span> # Value should be either <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> or a number proceeded by a minus (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">-</xhtml:span>) symbol</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">ucredit = -1</xhtml:span> # Value should be either <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> or a number proceeded by a minus (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">-</xhtml:span>) symbol</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">ocredit = -1</xhtml:span> # Value should be either <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> or a number proceeded by a minus (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">-</xhtml:span>) symbol</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">lcredit = -1</xhtml:span> # Value should be either <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> or a number proceeded by a minus (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">-</xhtml:span>) symbol</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example 1 - Set <xhtml:span class="inline_block">minclass = 3</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   sed -ri 's/^\s*minclass\s*=/# &/' /etc/security/pwquality.conf<br />   sed -ri 's/^\s*[dulo]credit\s*=/# &/' /etc/security/pwquality.conf<br />   [ ! -d /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/ ] && mkdir /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/<br />   printf '\n%s' "minclass = 3" > /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/50-pwcomplexity.conf<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example 2 - set <xhtml:span class="inline_block">dcredit = -1</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ucredit = -1</xhtml:span>, and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">lcredit = -1</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   sed -ri 's/^\s*minclass\s*=/# &/' /etc/security/pwquality.conf<br />   sed -ri 's/^\s*[dulo]credit\s*=/# &/' /etc/security/pwquality.conf<br />   [ ! -d /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/ ] && mkdir /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/<br />   printf '%s\n' "dcredit = -1" "ucredit = -1" "lcredit = -1" > /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/50-pwcomplexity.conf<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Passwords that are too complex in nature make it harder for users to remember, leading to bad practices. In addition, composition requirements provide no defense against common attack types such as social engineering or insecure storage of passwords</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:

<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">dcredit</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ucredit</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">lcredit</xhtml:span>, and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ocredit</xhtml:span> are not set to a value greater than <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Complexity conforms to local site policy:</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Psi -- '^\h*(minclass|[dulo]credit)\b' /etc/security/pwquality.conf /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/*.conf

<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example output:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>

</xhtml:ul>

<xhtml:li>It is recommended that settings be configured in a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> file in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/</xhtml:span> directory for clarity, convenience, and durability.</xhtml:li>

Rule.title: Ensure password same consecutive characters is configured
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pwquality</xhtml:span> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">maxrepeat</xhtml:span> option sets the maximum number of allowed same consecutive characters in a new password.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Use Unique Passwords
Use Unique Passwords

Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>Use of a complex password helps to increase the time and resources required to compromise the password. Password complexity, or strength, is a measure of the effectiveness of a password in resisting attempts at guessing and brute-force attacks.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Password complexity is one factor of several that determines how long it takes to crack a password. The more complex the password, the greater the number of possible combinations that need to be tested before the password is compromised.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Create or modify a file ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/</xhtml:span> directory or the file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf</xhtml:span> and add or modify the following line to set <xhtml:span class="inline_block">maxrepeat</xhtml:span> to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">3</xhtml:span> or less and not <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span>. Ensure setting conforms to local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   sed -ri 's/^\s*maxrepeat\s*=/# &/' /etc/security/pwquality.conf<br />   [ ! -d /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/ ] && mkdir /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/<br />   printf '\n%s' "maxrepeat = 3" > /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/50-pwrepeat.conf<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pl -- '\bpam_pwquality\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?maxrepeat\b' /usr/share/pam-configs/*
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Edit any returned files and remove the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">maxrepeat</xhtml:span> argument from the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwquality.so</xhtml:span> line(s):</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify that the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">maxrepeat</xhtml:span> option is set to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">3</xhtml:span> or less, not <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span>, and follows local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Psi -- '^\h*maxrepeat\h*=\h*[1-3]\b' /etc/security/pwquality.conf /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/*.conf
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example output:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/50-pwrepeat.conf:maxrepeat = 3
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Verify returned value(s) are <xhtml:span class="inline_block">3</xhtml:span> or less, not <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span>, and meet local site policy</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify that <xhtml:span class="inline_block">maxrepeat</xhtml:span> is not set, is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">3</xhtml:span> or less, not <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span>, and conforms to local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Psi -- '^\h*password\h+(requisite|required|sufficient)\h+pam_pwquality\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?maxrepeat\h*=\h*(0|[4-9]|[1-9][0-9]+)\b' /etc/pam.d/common-password
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>settings should be configured in only <xhtml:strong>one</xhtml:strong> location for clarity</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Settings observe an order of precedence:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>module arguments override the settings in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf</xhtml:span> configuration file</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>settings in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf</xhtml:span> configuration file override settings in a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> file in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/</xhtml:span> directory</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>settings in a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> file in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/</xhtml:span> directory are read in canonical order, with last read file containing the setting taking precedence</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>It is recommended that settings be configured in a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> file in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/</xhtml:span> directory for clarity, convenience, and durability.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pwquality</xhtml:span> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">maxsequence</xhtml:span> option sets the maximum length of monotonic character sequences in the new password. <xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> Most such passwords will not pass the simplicity check unless the sequence is only a minor part of the password.</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure password quality checking is enforced
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwquality</xhtml:span> module can be configured to either reject a password if it fails the checks, or only print a warning.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>This is configured by setting the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">enforcing=<N></xhtml:span> argument. If nonzero, a password will be rejected if it fails the checks, otherwise only a warning message will be provided.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>This setting applies only to the pam_pwquality module and possibly other applications that explicitly change their behavior based on it. It does not affect pwmake(1) and pwscore(1).</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Use Unique Passwords
Use Unique Passwords

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Strong passwords help protect systems from password attacks. Types of password attacks include dictionary attacks, which attempt to use common words and phrases, and brute force attacks, which try every possible combination of characters. Also attackers may try to obtain the account database so they can use tools to discover the accounts and passwords.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pl -- '\bpam_pwquality\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?enforcing=0\b' /usr/share/pam-configs/*
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Edit any returned files and remove the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">enforcing=0</xhtml:span> argument from the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwquality.so</xhtml:span> line(s)</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf</xhtml:span> and all files ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/</xhtml:span> directory and remove or comment out any line containing the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">enforcing = 0</xhtml:span> argument:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># sed -ri 's/^\s*enforcing\s*=\s*0/# &/' /etc/security/pwquality.conf /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/*.conf
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify that <xhtml:span class="inline_block">enforcing=0</xhtml:span> has not been set in a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pwquality</xhtml:span> configuration file:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -PHsi -- '^\h*enforcing\h*=\h*0\b' /etc/security/pwquality.conf /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/*.conf
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify that the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">enforcing=0</xhtml:span> argument has not been set on the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwquality</xhtml:span> module:</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure password quality is enforced for the root user
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>If the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pwquality</xhtml:span> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">enforce_for_root</xhtml:span> option is enabled, the module will return error on failed check even if the user changing the password is root.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>This option is off by default which means that just the message about the failed check is printed but root can change the password anyway.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> The root is not asked for an old password so the checks that compare the old and new password are not performed.</xhtml:p>

Group.title: Configure pam_pwhistory module
Group.description:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwhistory</xhtml:span> - PAM module to remember last passwords</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_history.so</xhtml:span> module - This module saves the last passwords for each user in order to force password change history and keep the user from alternating between the same password too frequently.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>This module does not work together with kerberos. In general, it does not make much sense to use this module in conjunction with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">NIS</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">LDAP</xhtml:span>, since the old passwords are stored on the local machine and are not available on another machine for password history checking.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Options:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">debug</xhtml:span> - Turns on debugging via syslog(3).</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">use_authtok</xhtml:span> - When password changing enforce the module to use the new password provided by a previously stacked password module (this is used in the example of the stacking of the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_passwdqc module</xhtml:span> documented below).</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">enforce_for_root</xhtml:span> - If this option is set, the check is enforced for root, too.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">remember=<N></xhtml:span> - The last <xhtml:em><N></xhtml:em> passwords for each user are saved. The default is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">10</xhtml:span>. Value of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> makes the module to keep the existing contents of the opasswd file unchanged.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">retry=<N></xhtml:span> - Prompt user at most <xhtml:em><N></xhtml:em> times before returning with error. The default is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">1</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">authtok_type=<STRING></xhtml:span> - See pam_get_authtok(3) for more details.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Examples:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">An example password section would be:<br /><br />    #%PAM-1.0<br />    password     required       pam_pwhistory.so<br />    password     required       pam_unix.so        use_authtok<br /><br />In combination with pam_passwdqc:<br /><br />    #%PAM-1.0<br />    password     required       pam_passwdqc.so    config=/etc/passwdqc.conf<br />    password     required       pam_pwhistory.so   use_authtok<br />    password     required       pam_unix.so        use_authtok
</xhtml:code>

Rule.title: Ensure password history remember is configured
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/opasswd</xhtml:span> file stores the users' old passwords and can be checked to ensure that users are not recycling recent passwords. The number of passwords remembered is set via the remember argument value in set for the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwhistory</xhtml:span> module.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>remember=<N> - <xhtml:span class="inline_block"><N></xhtml:span> is the number of old passwords to remember</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

safeguard.title: Use Unique Passwords
Use Unique Passwords

Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>Requiring users not to reuse their passwords make it less likely that an attacker will be able to guess the password or use a compromised password.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> These change only apply to accounts configured on the local system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># awk '/Password-Type:/{ f = 1;next } /-Type:/{ f = 0 } f {if (/pam_pwhistory\.so/) print FILENAME}' /usr/share/pam-configs/*
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Edit any returned files and edit or add the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">remember=</xhtml:span> argument, with a value of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">24</xhtml:span> or more, that meets local site policy to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwhistory</xhtml:span> line in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Password</xhtml:span> section:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example File:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">Name: pwhistory password history checking<br />Default: yes<br />Priority: 1024<br />Password-Type: Primary<br />Password:<br />   requisite   pam_pwhistory.so remember=24 enforce_for_root try_first_pass use_authtok # <- **ensure line includes remember=<N>**
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to update the files in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/</xhtml:span> directory:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update --enable <MODIFIED_PROFILE_NAME>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update --enable pwhistory
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command and verify:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pwhistory</xhtml:span> line in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/common-password</xhtml:span> includes <xhtml:span class="inline_block">remember=<N></xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The value of <N> is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">24</xhtml:span> or more</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The value meets local site policy</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Psi -- '^\h*password\h+[^#\n\r]+\h+pam_pwhistory\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?remember=\d+\b' /etc/pam.d/common-password
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Output should be similar to:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">password   requisite   pam_pwhistory.so remember=24 enforce_for_root try_first_pass use_authtok
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Group.title: Configure pam_unix module
Group.description: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_unix.so</xhtml:span> module is the standard Unix authentication module. It uses standard calls from the system's libraries to retrieve and set account information as well as authentication. Usually this is obtained from the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> and the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span> file as well if shadow is enabled.</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure pam_unix does not include nullok
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">nullok</xhtml:span> argument overrides the default action of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_unix.so</xhtml:span> to not permit the user access to a service if their official password is blank.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Use Unique Passwords
Use Unique Passwords

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Using a strong password is essential to helping protect personal and sensitive information from unauthorized access</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -PH -- '^\h*([^#\n\r]+\h+)?pam_unix\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?nullok\b' /usr/share/pam-configs/*
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Edit any files returned and remove the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">nullok</xhtml:span> argument for the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_unix</xhtml:span> lines</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example File:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">Name: Unix authentication<br />Default: yes<br />Priority: 256<br />Auth-Type: Primary<br />Auth:<br />        [success=end default=ignore]    pam_unix.so try_first_pass # <- **ensure line does not include nullok nullok**<br />Auth-Initial:<br />        [success=end default=ignore]    pam_unix.so # <- **ensure line does not include nullok nullok**<br />Account-Type: Primary<br />Account:<br />        [success=end new_authtok_reqd=done default=ignore]      pam_unix.so<br />Account-Initial:<br />        [success=end new_authtok_reqd=done default=ignore]      pam_unix.so<br />Session-Type: Additional<br />Session:<br />        required        pam_unix.so<br />Session-Initial:<br />        required        pam_unix.so<br />Password-Type: Primary<br />Password:<br />        [success=end default=ignore]    pam_unix.so obscure use_authtok try_first_pass yescrypt<br />Password-Initial:<br />        [success=end default=ignore]    pam_unix.so obscure yescrypt
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to update the files in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/</xhtml:span> directory:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update --enable <EDITED_PROFILE_NAME>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update --enable unix
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> If custom files are being used, the corresponding files in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/</xhtml:span> would need to be edited directly, and the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam-auth-update --enable <EDITED_PROFILE_NAME></xhtml:span> command skipped</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -PH -- '^\h*^\h*[^#\n\r]+\h+pam_unix\.so\b' /etc/pam.d/common-{password,auth,account,session,session-noninteractive} | grep -Pv -- '\bnullok\b'
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Output should be similar to:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">/etc/pam.d/common-password:password   [success=1 default=ignore]   pam_unix.so obscure use_authtok try_first_pass yescrypt<br />/etc/pam.d/common-auth:auth   [success=2 default=ignore]   pam_unix.so try_first_pass<br />/etc/pam.d/common-account:account   [success=1 new_authtok_reqd=done default=ignore]   pam_unix.so<br />/etc/pam.d/common-session:session   required   pam_unix.so<br />/etc/pam.d/common-session-noninteractive:session   required   pam_unix.so
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure pam_unix does not include remember
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">remember=n</xhtml:span> argument saves the last n passwords for each user in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/opasswd</xhtml:span> in order to force password change history and keep the user from alternating between the same password too frequently. The MD5 password hash algorithm is used for storing the old passwords. Instead of this option the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwhistory</xhtml:span> module should be used. The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_pwhistory</xhtml:span> module saves the last n passwords for each user in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/opasswd</xhtml:span> using the password hash algorithm set on the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_unix</xhtml:span> module. This allows for the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">yescrypt</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sha512</xhtml:span> hash algorithm to be used.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Use Unique Passwords
Use Unique Passwords

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">remember=n</xhtml:span> argument should be removed to ensure a strong password hashing algorithm is being used. A stronger hash provides additional protection to the system by increasing the level of effort needed for an attacker to successfully determine local user's old passwords stored in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/opasswd</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>

</xhtml:code>

<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update --enable <EDITED_PROFILE_NAME>
</xhtml:code>

<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update --enable unix
</xhtml:code>

</xhtml:code>

Rule.title: Ensure pam_unix includes a strong password hashing algorithm
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>A cryptographic hash function converts an arbitrary-length input into a fixed length output. Password hashing performs a one-way transformation of a password, turning the password into another string, called the hashed password.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_unix</xhtml:span> module can be configured to use one of the following hashing algorithms for user's passwords:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">md5</xhtml:span> - When a user changes their password next, encrypt it with the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">MD5</xhtml:span> algorithm.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">bigcrypt</xhtml:span> - When a user changes their password next, encrypt it with the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">DEC C2</xhtml:span> algorithm.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">sha256</xhtml:span> - When a user changes their password next, encrypt it with the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">SHA256</xhtml:span> algorithm. The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">SHA256</xhtml:span> algorithm must be supported by the crypt(3) function.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">sha512</xhtml:span> - When a user changes their password next, encrypt it with the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">SHA512</xhtml:span> algorithm. The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">SHA512</xhtml:span> algorithm must be supported by the crypt(3) function.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">blowfish</xhtml:span> - When a user changes their password next, encrypt it with the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">blowfish</xhtml:span> algorithm. The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">blowfish</xhtml:span> algorithm must be supported by the crypt(3) function.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">gost_yescrypt</xhtml:span> - When a user changes their password next, encrypt it with the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">gost-yescrypt</xhtml:span> algorithm. The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">gost-yescrypt</xhtml:span> algorithm must be supported by the crypt(3) function.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">yescrypt</xhtml:span> - When a user changes their password next, encrypt it with the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">yescrypt</xhtml:span> algorithm. The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">yescrypt</xhtml:span> algorithm must be supported by the crypt(3) function.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

safeguard.title: Encrypt Sensitive Data at Rest
Encrypt or Hash all Authentication Credentials

metadata.notes:
<xhtml:p>The following command may be used to expire all non-system user ID's immediately and force them to change their passwords on next login. Any system accounts that need to be expired should be carefully done separately by the system administrator to prevent any potential problems.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># awk -F: '( $3&amp;amp;lt;'"$(awk '/^\s*UID_MIN/{print $2}' /etc/login.defs)"' &amp;amp;&amp;amp; $1 != "nfsnobody" ) { print $1 }' /etc/passwd | xargs -n 1 chage -d 0
</xhtml:code>

Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">SHA-512</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">yescrypt</xhtml:span> algorithms provide a stronger hash than other algorithms used by Linux for password hash generation. A stronger hash provides additional protection to the system by increasing the level of effort needed for an attacker to successfully determine local user passwords.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> These changes only apply to the local system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># awk '/Password-Type:/{ f = 1;next } /-Type:/{ f = 0 } f {if (/pam_unix\.so/) print FILENAME}' /usr/share/pam-configs/*
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Edit any returned files and edit or add a strong hashing algorithm, either sha512 or yescrypt, that meets local site policy to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_unix</xhtml:span> lines in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Password</xhtml:span> section:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example File:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">Name: Unix authentication<br />Default: yes<br />Priority: 256<br />Auth-Type: Primary # <- Start of "Auth" section<br />Auth:<br />        [success=end default=ignore]    pam_unix.so try_first_pass<br />Auth-Initial:<br />        [success=end default=ignore]    pam_unix.so<br />Account-Type: Primary # <- Start of "Account" section<br />Account:<br />        [success=end new_authtok_reqd=done default=ignore]      pam_unix.so<br />Account-Initial:<br />        [success=end new_authtok_reqd=done default=ignore]      pam_unix.so<br />Session-Type: Additional  # <- Start of "Session" section<br />Session:<br />        required        pam_unix.so<br />Session-Initial:<br />        required        pam_unix.so<br />Password-Type: Primary # <- Start of "Password" section<br />Password:<br />        [success=end default=ignore]    pam_unix.so obscure use_authtok try_first_pass yescrypt # <- **ensure hashing algorithm is either sha512 or yescrypt**<br />Password-Initial:<br />        [success=end default=ignore]    pam_unix.so obscure yescrypt # <- **ensure hashing algorithm is either sha512 or yescrypt**
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to update the files in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/</xhtml:span> directory:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update --enable <MODIFIED_PROFILE_NAME>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update --enable unix
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify that a strong password hashing algorithm is set on the pam_unix.so module:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -PH -- '^\h*password\h+([^#\n\r]+)\h+pam_unix\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?(sha512|yescrypt)\b' /etc/pam.d/common-password
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Output should be similar to:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">/etc/pam.d/common-password:password   [success=1 default=ignore]   pam_unix.so obscure use_authtok try_first_pass yescrypt
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Verify that the line(s) include either <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sha512</xhtml:span> <xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">yescrypt</xhtml:span></xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure pam_unix includes use_authtok
Rule.description: <xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">use_authtok</xhtml:span> - When password changing enforce the module to set the new password to the one provided by a previously stacked password module</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Encrypt Sensitive Data at Rest
Encrypt or Hash all Authentication Credentials

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">use_authtok</xhtml:span> allows multiple pam modules to confirm a new password before it is accepted.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># awk '/Password-Type:/{ f = 1;next } /-Type:/{ f = 0 } f {if (/pam_unix\.so/) print FILENAME}' /usr/share/pam-configs/*
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Edit any returned files add <xhtml:span class="inline_block">use_authtok</xhtml:span> to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_unix</xhtml:span> line in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Password</xhtml:span> section under <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Password:</xhtml:span> subsection:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> The if the file's <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Password</xhtml:span> section includes a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Password-Initial:</xhtml:span> subsection, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">use_authtok</xhtml:span> should not be added to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_unix</xhtml:span> line in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Password-Initial:</xhtml:span> subsection</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example File:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">Name: Unix authentication<br />Default: yes<br />Priority: 256<br />Auth-Type: Primary # <- Start of "Auth" section<br />Auth:<br />        [success=end default=ignore]    pam_unix.so try_first_pass<br />Auth-Initial:<br />        [success=end default=ignore]    pam_unix.so<br />Account-Type: Primary # <- Start of "Account" section<br />Account:<br />        [success=end new_authtok_reqd=done default=ignore]      pam_unix.so<br />Account-Initial:<br />        [success=end new_authtok_reqd=done default=ignore]      pam_unix.so<br />Session-Type: Additional  # <- Start of "Session" section<br />Session:<br />        required        pam_unix.so<br />Session-Initial:<br />        required        pam_unix.so<br />Password-Type: Primary # <- Start of "Password" section<br />Password:<br />        [success=end default=ignore]    pam_unix.so obscure use_authtok try_first_pass yescrypt # <- **ensure line includes use_authtok**<br />Password-Initial:<br />        [success=end default=ignore]    pam_unix.so obscure yescrypt # <- **Password-Initial: subsection does not include use_authtok
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to update the files in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/</xhtml:span> directory:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update --enable <MODIFIED_PROFILE_NAME>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pam-auth-update --enable unix
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify that <xhtml:span class="inline_block">use_authtok</xhtml:span> is set on the pam_unix.so module lines in the password stack:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -PH -- '^\h*password\h+([^#\n\r]+)\h+pam_unix\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?use_authtok\b' /etc/pam.d/common-password
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Output should be similar to:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">/etc/pam.d/common-password:password   [success=1 default=ignore]   pam_unix.so obscure use_authtok try_first_pass yescrypt
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Verify that the line(s) include <xhtml:span class="inline_block">use_authtok</xhtml:span></xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
