Group.title: User Accounts and Environment
Group.description: <xhtml:p>This section provides guidance on setting up secure defaults for system and user accounts and their environment.</xhtml:p>

Group.title: Configure shadow password suite parameters
Group.description: <xhtml:p>While a majority of the password control parameters have been moved to PAM, some parameters are still available through the shadow password suite. Any changes made to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/login.defs </xhtml:span>will only be applied if the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">usermod </xhtml:span>command is used. If user IDs are added a different way, use the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chage </xhtml:span>command to effect changes to individual user IDs.</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure password expiration is configured
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_MAX_DAYS</xhtml:span> parameter in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/login.defs</xhtml:span> allows an administrator to force passwords to expire once they reach a defined age.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_MAX_DAYS</xhtml:span> <xhtml:em><N></xhtml:em> - The maximum number of days a password may be used. If the password is older than this, a password change will be forced. If not specified, -1 will be assumed (which disables the restriction).</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Use Unique Passwords
Use Unique Passwords

metadata.notes: <xhtml:p>A value of -1 will disable password expiration.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>The window of opportunity for an attacker to leverage compromised credentials or successfully compromise credentials via an online brute force attack is limited by the age of the password. Therefore, reducing the maximum age of a password also reduces an attacker's window of opportunity.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>We recommend a yearly password change. This is primarily because for all their good intentions users will share credentials across accounts. Therefore, even if a breach is publicly identified, the user may not see this notification, or forget they have an account on that site. This could leave a shared credential vulnerable indefinitely. Having an organizational policy of a 1-year (annual) password expiration is a reasonable compromise to mitigate this with minimal user burden.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: CM-1, CM-2, CM-6, CM-7, IA-5

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Set the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_MAX_DAYS</xhtml:span> parameter to conform to site policy in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/login.defs</xhtml:span> :</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">PASS_MAX_DAYS 365
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Modify user parameters for all users with a password set to match:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># chage --maxdays 365 <user>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/login.defs</xhtml:span> and set <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_MAX_DAYS</xhtml:span> to a value greater than <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> that follows local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">PASS_MAX_DAYS 365
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to modify user parameters for all users with a password set to a maximum age no greater than <xhtml:span class="inline_block">365</xhtml:span> or less than <xhtml:span class="inline_block">1</xhtml:span> that follows local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># chage --maxdays <N> <user>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># awk -F: '($2~/^\$.+\$/) {if($5 > 365 || $5 < 1)system ("chage --maxdays 365 " $1)}' /etc/shadow
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Warning:</xhtml:strong> If a password has been set at system install or kickstart, the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">last change date</xhtml:span> field is not set, In this case, setting <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_MAX_DAYS</xhtml:span> will immediately expire the password. One possible solution is to populate the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">last change date</xhtml:span> field through a command like: <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chage -d "$(date +%Y-%m-%d)" root</xhtml:span></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The password expiration must be greater than the minimum days between password changes or users will be unable to change their password.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Excessive password expiration requirements do more harm than good, because these requirements make users select predictable passwords, composed of sequential words and numbers that are closely related to each other. In these cases, the next password can be predicted based on the previous one (incrementing a number used in the password for
example). Also, password expiration requirements offer no containment benefits because attackers will often use credentials as soon as they compromise them. Instead, immediate password changes should be based on key events including, but not limited to:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Indication of compromise</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Change of user roles</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>When a user leaves the organization.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>Not only does changing passwords every few weeks or months frustrate the user, but it’s also been suggested that it does more harm than good, because it could lead to bad practices by the user such as adding a character to the end of their existing password.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command and verify <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_MAX_DAYS</xhtml:span> is set to 365 days or less and conforms to local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pi -- '^\h*PASS_MAX_DAYS\h+\d+\b' /etc/login.defs
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example output:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">PASS_MAX_DAYS 365
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify all <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span> passwords <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_MAX_DAYS</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>is greater than <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> days</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>is less than or equal to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">365</xhtml:span> days</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>conforms to local site policy</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># awk -F: '($2~/^\$.+\$/) {if($5 > 365 || $5 < 1)print "User: " $1 " PASS_MAX_DAYS: " $5}' /etc/shadow
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

artifact_expression.artifact_title: Ensure at least one file named /etc/login.defs exists and matches pattern (?i)^\h*PASS_MAX_DAYS\h+(36[0-5]|3[0-5][0-9]|[1-2][0-9][0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|[1-9])\b
Script Check Engine Check "nix_shadow_field_chk.sh" passing "pass_max_days:>:365" as "XCCDF_VALUE_REGEX"
Script Check Engine Check "nix_shadow_field_chk.sh" passing "pass_max_days:<:1" as "XCCDF_VALUE_REGEX"

Rule.title: Ensure minimum password days is configured
Rule.description: <xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_MIN_DAYS</xhtml:span> <<xhtml:em>N</xhtml:em>> - The minimum number of days allowed between password changes. Any password changes attempted sooner than this will be rejected. If not specified, 0 will be assumed (which disables the restriction).</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Use Unique Passwords
Use Unique Passwords

Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>Users may have favorite passwords that they like to use because they are easy to remember and they believe that their password choice is secure from compromise. Unfortunately, passwords are compromised and if an attacker is targeting a specific individual user account, with foreknowledge of data about that user, reuse of old, potentially compromised passwords, may cause a security breach.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>By restricting the frequency of password changes, an administrator can prevent users from repeatedly changing their password in an attempt to circumvent password reuse controls</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/login.defs</xhtml:span> and set <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_MIN_DAYS</xhtml:span> to a value greater than <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> that follows local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">PASS_MIN_DAYS 1
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to modify user parameters for all users with a password set to a minimum days greater than zero that follows local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># chage --mindays <N> <user>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># awk -F: '($2~/^\$.+\$/) {if($4 < 1)system ("chage --mindays 1 " $1)}' /etc/shadow
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>If a users password is set by other personnel as a procedure in dealing with a lost or expired password, the user should be forced to update this "set" password with their own password. e.g. force "change at next logon".</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>If it is not possible to have a user set their own password immediately, and this recommendation or local site procedure may cause a user to continue using a third party generated password, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_MIN_DAYS</xhtml:span> for the effected user should be temporally changed to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span>, to allow a user to change their password immediately.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>For applications where the user is not using the password at console, the ability to "change at next logon" may be limited. This may cause a user to continue to use a password created by other personnel.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify that <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_MIN_DAYS</xhtml:span> is set to a value greater than <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span>and follows local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pi -- '^\h*PASS_MIN_DAYS\h+\d+\b' /etc/login.defs
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example output:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">PASS_MIN_DAYS   1
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify all passwords have a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_MIN_DAYS</xhtml:span> greater than <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># awk -F: '($2~/^\$.+\$/) {if($4 < 1)print "User: " $1 " PASS_MIN_DAYS: " $4}' /etc/shadow
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

artifact_expression.artifact_title: Ensure at least one file named /etc/login.defs exists and matches pattern (?i)^\h*PASS_MIN_DAYS\h+[1-9][0-9]*\b
Script Check Engine Check "nix_shadow_field_chk.sh" passing "pass_min_days:<:1" as "XCCDF_VALUE_REGEX"

Rule.title: Ensure password expiration warning days is configured
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_WARN_AGE</xhtml:span> parameter in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/login.defs</xhtml:span>  allows an administrator to notify users that their password will expire in a defined number of days.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_WARN_AGE</xhtml:span> <xhtml:em><N></xhtml:em> - The number of days warning given before a password expires. A zero means warning is given only upon the day of expiration, a negative value means no warning is given. If not specified, no warning will be provided.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Establish and Maintain a Secure Configuration Process
Use Unique Passwords

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Providing an advance warning that a password will be expiring gives users time to think of a secure password. Users caught unaware may choose a simple password or write it down where it may be discovered.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/login.defs</xhtml:span> and set <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_WARN_AGE</xhtml:span> to a value of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">7</xhtml:span> or more that follows local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">PASS_WARN_AGE 7
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to modify user parameters for all users with a password set to a minimum warning to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">7</xhtml:span> or more days that follows local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># chage --warndays <N> <user>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># awk -F: '($2~/^\$.+\$/) {if($6 < 7)system ("chage --warndays 7 " $1)}' /etc/shadow
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command and verify <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_WARN_AGE</xhtml:span> is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">7</xhtml:span> or more and follows local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pi -- '^\h*PASS_WARN_AGE\h+\d+\b' /etc/login.defs
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example output:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">PASS_WARN_AGE 7
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify all passwords have a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_WARN_AGE</xhtml:span> of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">7</xhtml:span> or more:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># awk -F: '($2~/^\$.+\$/) {if($6 < 7)print "User: " $1 " PASS_WARN_AGE: " $6}' /etc/shadow
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

artifact_expression.artifact_title: Ensure at least one file named /etc/login.defs exists and matches pattern (?i)^\h*PASS_WARN_AGE\h+([7-9]|[1-9][0-9]+)\b
Script Check Engine Check "nix_shadow_field_chk.sh" passing "pass_warn_age:<:7" as "XCCDF_VALUE_REGEX"

Rule.title: Ensure strong password hashing algorithm is configured
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>A cryptographic hash function converts an arbitrary-length input into a fixed length output. Password hashing performs a one-way transformation of a password, turning the password into another string, called the hashed password.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">ENCRYPT_METHOD</xhtml:span> (string) - This defines the system default encryption algorithm for encrypting passwords (if no algorithm are specified on the command line). It can take one of these values:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">MD5</xhtml:span> - MD5-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">SHA256</xhtml:span> - SHA256-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">SHA512</xhtml:span> - SHA512-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">BCRYPT</xhtml:span> - BCRYPT-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">YESCRYPT</xhtml:span> - YESCRYPT-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">DES</xhtml:span> - DES-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password (default)</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>This parameter overrides the deprecated <xhtml:span class="inline_block">MD5_CRYPT_ENAB</xhtml:span> variable.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>This parameter will only affect the generation of group passwords.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The generation of user passwords is done by PAM and subject to the PAM configuration.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>It is recommended to set this variable consistently with the PAM configuration.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

safeguard.title: Encrypt Sensitive Data at Rest
Encrypt or Hash all Authentication Credentials

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">SHA-512</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">yescrypt</xhtml:span> algorithms provide a stronger hash than other algorithms used by Linux for password hash generation. A stronger hash provides additional protection to the system by increasing the level of effort needed for an attacker to successfully determine local group passwords.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/login.defs</xhtml:span> and set the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ENCRYPT_METHOD</xhtml:span> to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">SHA512</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">YESCRYPT</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">ENCRYPT_METHOD <HASHING_ALGORITHM>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">ENCRYPT_METHOD YESCRYPT
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>This only effects local groups' passwords created after updating the file to use <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sha512</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">yescrypt</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>If it is determined that the password algorithm being used is not <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sha512</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">yescrypt</xhtml:span>, once it is changed, it is recommended that all group passwords be updated to use the stronger hashing algorithm.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>It is recommended that the chosen hashing algorithm is consistent across <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/login.defs</xhtml:span> and the PAM configuration</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify the hashing algorithm is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sha512</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">yescrypt</xhtml:span> in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/login.defs</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pi -- '^\h*ENCRYPT_METHOD\h+(SHA512|yescrypt)\b' /etc/login.defs
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example output:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">ENCRYPT_METHOD SHA512<br /> - OR -<br />ENCRYPT_METHOD  YESCRYPT
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

artifact_expression.artifact_title: Ensure at least one file named /etc/login.defs exists and matches pattern (?i)^\h*ENCRYPT_METHOD\h+(SHA512|YESCRYPT)\b

Rule.title: Ensure inactive password lock is configured
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>User accounts that have been inactive for over a given period of time can be automatically disabled.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">INACTIVE</xhtml:span> - Defines the number of days after the password exceeded its maximum age where the user is expected to replace this password.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The value is stored in the shadow password file. An input of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span> will disable an expired password with no delay. An input of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">-1</xhtml:span> will blank the respective field in the shadow password file.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Use Unique Passwords
Use Unique Passwords

metadata.notes: <xhtml:p>A value of -1 would disable this setting.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Inactive accounts pose a threat to system security since the users are not logging in to notice failed login attempts or other anomalies.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to set the default password inactivity period to 45 days or less that meets local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># useradd -D -f <N>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># useradd -D -f 45
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to modify user parameters for all users with a password set to a inactive age of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">45</xhtml:span> days or less that follows local site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># chage --inactive <N> <user>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># awk -F: '($2~/^\$.+\$/) {if($7 > 45 || $7 < 0)system ("chage --inactive 45 " $1)}' /etc/shadow
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command and verify <xhtml:span class="inline_block">INACTIVE</xhtml:span> conforms to site policy (no more than 45 days):</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># useradd -D | grep INACTIVE<br /><br />INACTIVE=45
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Verify all users with a password have Password inactive no more than 45 days after password expires</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Verify all users with a password have Password inactive no more than 45 days after password expires: Run the following command and Review list of users and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">INACTIVE</xhtml:span> to verify that all users <xhtml:span class="inline_block">INACTIVE</xhtml:span> conforms to site policy (no more than 45 days):</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># awk -F: '($2~/^\$.+\$/) {if($7 > 45 || $7 < 0)print "User: " $1 " INACTIVE: " $7}' /etc/shadow
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure root path integrity
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span> user can execute any command on the system and could be fooled into executing programs unintentionally if the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PATH</xhtml:span> is not set correctly.</xhtml:p>
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Including the current working directory (.) or other writable directory in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span>'s executable path makes it likely that an attacker can gain superuser access by forcing an administrator operating as <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span> to execute a Trojan horse program.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: CM-1, CM-2, CM-6, CM-7, IA-5

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Correct or justify any:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Locations that are not directories</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Empty directories (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">::</xhtml:span>)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Trailing (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">:</xhtml:span>)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Current working directory (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">.</xhtml:span>)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Non <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span> owned directories</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Directories that less restrictive than mode <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0755</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to verify root's path does not include:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Locations that are not directories</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>An empty directory (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">::</xhtml:span>)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>A trailing (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">:</xhtml:span>)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Current working directory (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">.</xhtml:span>)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Non <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span> owned directories</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Directories that less restrictive than mode <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0755</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   l_output2=""<br />   l_pmask="0022"<br />   l_maxperm="$( printf '%o' $(( 0777 & ~$l_pmask )) )"<br />   l_root_path="$(sudo -Hiu root env | grep '^PATH' | cut -d= -f2)"<br />   unset a_path_loc && IFS=":" read -ra a_path_loc <<< "$l_root_path"<br />   grep -q "::" <<< "$l_root_path" && l_output2="$l_output2
 - root's path contains a empty directory (::)"<br />   grep -Pq ":\h*$" <<< "$l_root_path" && l_output2="$l_output2
 - root's path contains a trailing (:)"<br />   grep -Pq '(\h+|:)\.(:|\h*$)' <<< "$l_root_path" && l_output2="$l_output2
 - root's path contains current working directory (.)"<br />   while read -r l_path; do<br />      if [ -d "$l_path" ]; then<br />         while read -r l_fmode l_fown; do<br />            [ "$l_fown" != "root" ] && l_output2="$l_output2
 - Directory: "$l_path" is owned by: "$l_fown" should be owned by "root""<br />            [ $(( $l_fmode & $l_pmask )) -gt 0 ] && l_output2="$l_output2
 - Directory: "$l_path" is mode: "$l_fmode" and should be mode: "$l_maxperm" or more restrictive"<br />         done <<< "$(stat -Lc '%#a %U' "$l_path")"<br />      else<br />         l_output2="$l_output2
 - "$l_path" is not a directory"<br />      fi<br />   done <<< "$(printf "%s
" "${a_path_loc[@]}")"<br />   if [ -z "$l_output2" ]; then<br />      echo -e "
- Audit Result:
  *** PASS ***
 - Root's path is correctly configured
"<br />   else<br />      echo -e "
- Audit Result:
  ** FAIL **
 - * Reasons for audit failure * :
$l_output2
"<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure root user umask is configured
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>The user file-creation mode mask (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span>) is used to determine the file permission for newly created directories and files. In Linux, the default permissions for any newly created directory is 0777 (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">rwxrwxrwx</xhtml:span>), and for any newly created file it is 0666 (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">rw-rw-rw-</xhtml:span>). The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> modifies the default Linux permissions by restricting (masking) these permissions. The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> is not simply subtracted, but is processed bitwise. Bits set in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> are cleared in the resulting file mode.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> can be set with either <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Octal</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Symbolic</xhtml:span> values:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">Octal</xhtml:span> (Numeric) Value - Represented by either three or four digits. ie <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask 0027</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask 027</xhtml:span>.  If a four digit umask is used, the first digit is ignored. The remaining three digits effect the resulting permissions for user, group, and world/other respectively.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">Symbolic</xhtml:span> Value - Represented by a comma separated list for User <xhtml:span class="inline_block">u</xhtml:span>, group <xhtml:span class="inline_block">g</xhtml:span>, and world/other <xhtml:span class="inline_block">o</xhtml:span>.  The permissions listed are not masked by <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span>. ie a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> set by <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask u=rwx,g=rx,o=</xhtml:span> is the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Symbolic</xhtml:span> equivalent of the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Octal</xhtml:span> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask 027</xhtml:span>.  This <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> would set a newly created directory with file mode <xhtml:span class="inline_block">drwxr-x---</xhtml:span> and a newly created file with file mode <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rw-r-----</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>root user Shell Configuration Files:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/root/.bash_profile</xhtml:span> - Is executed to configure the root users' shell before the initial command prompt. <xhtml:strong>Is only read by login shells.</xhtml:strong></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/root/.bashrc</xhtml:span> - Is executed for interactive shells. <xhtml:strong>only read by a shell that's both interactive and non-login</xhtml:strong></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> is set by order of precedence. If <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> is set in multiple locations, this order of precedence will determine the system's default <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Order of precedence:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/root/.bash_profile</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/root/.bashrc</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The system default umask</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Protect Information through  Access Control Lists

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Setting a secure value for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> ensures that users make a conscious choice about their file permissions. A permissive <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> value could result in directories or files with excessive permissions that can be read and/or written to by unauthorized users.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/root/.bash_profile</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/root/.bashrc</xhtml:span> and remove, comment out, or update any line with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> to be <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0027</xhtml:span> or more restrictive.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following to verify the root user <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> is set to enforce a newly created directories' permissions to be <xhtml:span class="inline_block">750 (drwxr-x---)</xhtml:span>, and a newly created file's permissions be <xhtml:span class="inline_block">640 (rw-r-----)</xhtml:span>, or more restrictive:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Psi -- '^\h*umask\h+(([0-7][0-7][01][0-7]\b|[0-7][0-7][0-7][0-6]\b)|([0-7][01][0-7]\b|[0-7][0-7][0-6]\b)|(u=[rwx]{1,3},)?(((g=[rx]?[rx]?w[rx]?[rx]?\b)(,o=[rwx]{1,3})?)|((g=[wrx]{1,3},)?o=[wrx]{1,3}\b)))' /root/.bash_profile /root/.bashrc
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure system accounts do not have a valid login shell
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>There are a number of accounts provided with most distributions that are used to manage applications and are not intended to provide an interactive shell. Furthermore, a user may add special accounts that are not intended to provide an interactive shell.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Protect Information through  Access Control Lists

metadata.notes: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sync</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">shutdown</xhtml:span>, and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">halt</xhtml:span> users are exempted from requiring a non-login shell.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>It is important to make sure that accounts that are not being used by regular users are prevented from being used to provide an interactive shell. By default, most distributions set the password field for these accounts to an invalid string, but it is also recommended that the shell field in the password file be set to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">nologin</xhtml:span> shell. This prevents the account from potentially being used to run any commands.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: AC-2(5), AC-3, AC-11, MP-2

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to set the shell for any service accounts returned by the audit to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">nologin</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># usermod -s $(command -v nologin) <user>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example script:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   l_valid_shells="^($( awk -F\/ '$NF != "nologin" {print}' /etc/shells | sed -rn '/^\//{s,/,\\\\/,g;p}' | paste -s -d '|' - ))$"<br />   awk -v pat="$l_valid_shells" -F: '($1!~/^(root|halt|sync|shutdown|nfsnobody)$/ && ($3<'"$(awk '/^\s*UID_MIN/{print $2}' /etc/login.defs)"' || $3 == 65534) && $(NF) ~ pat) {system ("usermod -s '"$(command -v nologin)"' " $1)}' /etc/passwd<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify system accounts, except for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">halt</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sync</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">shutdown</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">nfsnobody</xhtml:span>, do not have a valid login shell:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   l_valid_shells="^($(awk -F\/ '$NF != "nologin" {print}' /etc/shells | sed -rn '/^\//{s,/,\\\\/,g;p}' | paste -s -d '|' - ))$"<br />   awk -v pat="$l_valid_shells" -F: '($1!~/^(root|halt|sync|shutdown|nfsnobody)$/ && ($3<'"$(awk '/^\s*UID_MIN/{print $2}' /etc/login.defs)"' || $3 == 65534) && $(NF) ~ pat) {print "Service account: \"" $1 "\" has a valid shell: " $7}' /etc/passwd<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Protect Information through  Access Control Lists

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>It is important to make sure that accounts that are not being used by regular users are prevented from being used to provide an interactive shell. By default, most distributions set the password field for these accounts to an invalid string, but it is also recommended that the shell field in the password file be set to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">nologin</xhtml:span> shell. This prevents the account from potentially being used to run any commands.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: AC-2(5), AC-3, AC-11, MP-2

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to lock any non-root accounts without a valid login shell returned by the audit:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># usermod -L <user>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example script:</xhtml:em>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   l_valid_shells="^($(awk -F\/ '$NF != "nologin" {print}' /etc/shells | sed -rn '/^\//{s,/,\\\\/,g;p}' | paste -s -d '|' - ))$"<br />   while IFS= read -r l_user; do<br />      passwd -S "$l_user" | awk '$2 !~ /^L/ {system ("usermod -L " $1)}'<br />   done < <(awk -v pat="$l_valid_shells" -F: '($1 != "root" && $(NF) !~ pat) {print $1}' /etc/passwd)<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to verify all non-root accounts without a valid login shell are locked.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   l_valid_shells="^($(awk -F\/ '$NF != "nologin" {print}' /etc/shells | sed -rn '/^\//{s,/,\\\\/,g;p}' | paste -s -d '|' - ))$"<br />   while IFS= read -r l_user; do<br />      passwd -S "$l_user" | awk '$2 !~ /^L/ {print "Account: \"" $1 "\" does not have a valid login shell and is not locked"}'<br />   done < <(awk -v pat="$l_valid_shells" -F: '($1 != "root" && $(NF) !~ pat) {print $1}' /etc/passwd)<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

artifact_expression.artifact_title: Script Check Engine Check "nix_account_no_login_shell_locked_chk.sh"

Rule.title: Ensure nologin is not listed in /etc/shells
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shells</xhtml:span> is a text file which contains the full pathnames of valid login shells. This file is consulted by <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chsh</xhtml:span> and available to be queried by other programs.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Be aware that there are programs which consult this file to find out if a user is a normal user; for example, FTP daemons traditionally disallow access to users with shells not included in this file.</xhtml:p>
Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>A user can use <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chsh</xhtml:span> to change their configured shell.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>If a user has a shell configured that isn't in in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shells</xhtml:span>, then the system assumes that they're somehow restricted. In the case of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chsh</xhtml:span> it means that the user cannot change that value.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Other programs might query that list and apply similar restrictions.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>By putting <xhtml:span class="inline_block">nologin</xhtml:span> in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shells</xhtml:span>, any user that has <xhtml:span class="inline_block">nologin</xhtml:span> as its shell is considered a full, unrestricted user. This is not the expected behavior for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">nologin</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: CM-1, CM-2, CM-6, CM-7, IA-5

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shells</xhtml:span> and remove any lines that include <xhtml:span class="inline_block">nologin</xhtml:span></xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify that <xhtml:span class="inline_block">nologin</xhtml:span> is not listed in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shells</xhtml:span> file:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Ps '^\h*([^#\n\r]+)?\/nologin\b' /etc/shells
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

artifact_expression.artifact_title: Ensure no file named /etc/shells exists and matches pattern ^\h*([^#\n\r]+)?\/nologin\b

Rule.title: Ensure default user shell timeout is configured
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">TMOUT</xhtml:span> is an environmental setting that determines the timeout of a shell in seconds.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>TMOUT=<xhtml:em>n</xhtml:em> - Sets the shell timeout to <xhtml:em>n</xhtml:em> seconds.  A setting of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">TMOUT=0</xhtml:span> disables timeout.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>readonly TMOUT- Sets the TMOUT environmental variable as readonly, preventing unwanted modification during run-time.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>export TMOUT - exports the TMOUT variable</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>System Wide Shell Configuration Files:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/profile</xhtml:span> - used to set system wide environmental variables on users shells. The variables are sometimes the same ones that are in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.bash_profile</xhtml:span>, however this file is used to set an initial PATH or PS1 for all shell users of the system. <xhtml:strong>is only executed for interactive <xhtml:em>login</xhtml:em> shells, or shells executed with the --login parameter.</xhtml:strong></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/profile.d</xhtml:span> - <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/profile</xhtml:span> will execute the scripts within <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/profile.d/*.sh</xhtml:span>. It is recommended to place your configuration in a shell script within <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/profile.d</xhtml:span> to set your own system wide environmental variables.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/bashrc</xhtml:span> - System wide version of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.bashrc</xhtml:span>.  In Fedora derived distributions, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/bashrc</xhtml:span> also invokes /etc/profile.d/*.sh if <xhtml:em>non-login</xhtml:em> shell, but redirects output to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/dev/null</xhtml:span> if <xhtml:em>non-interactive.</xhtml:em> <xhtml:strong>Is only executed for <xhtml:em>interactive</xhtml:em> shells or if <xhtml:span class="inline_block">BASH_ENV</xhtml:span> is set to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/bashrc</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:strong></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

safeguard.title: Configure Automatic Session Locking on Enterprise Assets
Lock Workstation Sessions After Inactivity

metadata.notes:
<xhtml:p>The audit and remediation in this recommendation apply to bash and shell. If other shells are supported on the system, it is recommended that their configuration files also are checked.  Other methods of setting a timeout exist for other shells not covered here.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Ensure that the timeout conforms to your local policy.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Setting a timeout value reduces the window of opportunity for unauthorized user access to another user's shell session that has been left unattended. It also ends the inactive session and releases the resources associated with that session.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Review <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/bashrc</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/profile</xhtml:span>, and all files ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">*.sh</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/profile.d/</xhtml:span> directory and remove or edit all <xhtml:span class="inline_block">TMOUT=_n_</xhtml:span> entries to follow local site policy.  <xhtml:span class="inline_block">TMOUT</xhtml:span> should not exceed 900 or be equal to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Configure <xhtml:span class="inline_block">TMOUT</xhtml:span> in <xhtml:strong>one</xhtml:strong> of the following files:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>A file in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/profile.d/</xhtml:span> directory ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.sh</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/profile</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/bashrc</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em><xhtml:span class="inline_block">TMOUT</xhtml:span> configuration examples:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>As multiple lines:</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">TMOUT=900<br />readonly TMOUT<br />export TMOUT
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>As a single line:</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">readonly TMOUT=900 ; export TMOUT
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to verify that <xhtml:span class="inline_block">TMOUT</xhtml:span> is configured to: include a timeout of no more than <xhtml:span class="inline_block">900</xhtml:span> seconds, to be <xhtml:span class="inline_block">readonly</xhtml:span>, to be <xhtml:span class="inline_block">exported</xhtml:span>, and is not being changed to a longer timeout.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   output1="" output2=""<br />   [ -f /etc/bashrc ] && BRC="/etc/bashrc"<br />   for f in "$BRC" /etc/profile /etc/profile.d/*.sh ; do<br />      grep -Pq '^\s*([^#]+\s+)?TMOUT=(900|[1-8][0-9][0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|[1-9]) ' "$f" && grep -Pq '^\s*([^#]+;\s*)?readonly\s+TMOUT(\s+|\s*;|\s*$|=(900|[1-8][0-9][0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|[1-9])) ' "$f" && grep -Pq '^\s*([^#]+;\s*)?export\s+TMOUT(\s+|\s*;|\s*$|=(900|[1-8][0-9][0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|[1-9])) ' "$f" && <br />   output1="$f"<br />   done<br />   grep -Pq '^\s*([^#]+\s+)?TMOUT=(9[0-9][1-9]|9[1-9][0-9]|0+|[1-9]\d{3,}) ' /etc/profile /etc/profile.d/*.sh "$BRC" && output2=$(grep -Ps '^\s*([^#]+\s+)?TMOUT=(9[0-9][1-9]|9[1-9][0-9]|0+|[1-9]\d{3,}) ' /etc/profile /etc/profile.d/*.sh $BRC)<br />   if [ -n "$output1" ] && [ -z "$output2" ]; then<br />      echo -e "
PASSED

TMOUT is configured in: "$output1"
"<br />   else<br />      [ -z "$output1" ] && echo -e "
FAILED

TMOUT is not configured
"<br />      [ -n "$output2" ] && echo -e "
FAILED

TMOUT is incorrectly configured in: "$output2"
"<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

artifact_expression.artifact_title: Script Check Engine Check "tmout_chk.sh"

Rule.title: Ensure default user umask is configured
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>The user file-creation mode mask (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span>) is used to determine the file permission for newly created directories and files. In Linux, the default permissions for any newly created directory is 0777 (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">rwxrwxrwx</xhtml:span>), and for any newly created file it is 0666 (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">rw-rw-rw-</xhtml:span>). The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> modifies the default Linux permissions by restricting (masking) these permissions. The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> is not simply subtracted, but is processed bitwise. Bits set in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> are cleared in the resulting file mode.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> can be set with either <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Octal</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Symbolic</xhtml:span> values:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">Octal</xhtml:span> (Numeric) Value - Represented by either three or four digits. ie <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask 0027</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask 027</xhtml:span>.  If a four digit umask is used, the first digit is ignored. The remaining three digits effect the resulting permissions for user, group, and world/other respectively.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">Symbolic</xhtml:span> Value - Represented by a comma separated list for User <xhtml:span class="inline_block">u</xhtml:span>, group <xhtml:span class="inline_block">g</xhtml:span>, and world/other <xhtml:span class="inline_block">o</xhtml:span>.  The permissions listed are not masked by <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span>. ie a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> set by <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask u=rwx,g=rx,o=</xhtml:span> is the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Symbolic</xhtml:span> equivalent of the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Octal</xhtml:span> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask 027</xhtml:span>.  This <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> would set a newly created directory with file mode <xhtml:span class="inline_block">drwxr-x---</xhtml:span> and a newly created file with file mode <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rw-r-----</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>The default <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> can be set to use the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_umask</xhtml:span> module or in a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">System Wide Shell Configuration File</xhtml:span>. The user creating the directories or files has the discretion of changing the permissions via the chmod command, or choosing a different default <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> by adding the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> command into a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">User Shell Configuration File</xhtml:span>, ( <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.bash_profile</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.bashrc</xhtml:span>), in their home directory.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Setting the default umask:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>pam_umask module:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>will set the umask according to the system default in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/login.defs</xhtml:span> and user settings, solving the problem of different <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> settings with different shells, display managers, remote sessions etc.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask=<mask></xhtml:span> value in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/login.defs</xhtml:span> file is interpreted as Octal</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Setting <xhtml:span class="inline_block">USERGROUPS_ENAB</xhtml:span> to yes in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/login.defs</xhtml:span> (default):
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>will enable setting of the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> group bits to be the same as owner bits. (examples: 022 -> 002, 077 -> 007) for non-root users, if the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">uid</xhtml:span> is the same as <xhtml:span class="inline_block">gid</xhtml:span>, and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">username</xhtml:span> is the same as the <xhtml:span class="inline_block"><primary group name></xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>userdel will remove the user's group if it contains no more members, and useradd will create by default a group with the name of the user</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">System Wide Shell Configuration File</xhtml:span>:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/profile</xhtml:span> - used to set system wide environmental variables on users shells. The variables are sometimes the same ones that are in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.bash_profile</xhtml:span>, however this file is used to set an initial PATH or PS1 for all shell users of the system. <xhtml:strong>is only executed for interactive <xhtml:em>login</xhtml:em> shells, or shells executed with the --login parameter.</xhtml:strong></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/profile.d</xhtml:span> - <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/profile</xhtml:span> will execute the scripts within <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/profile.d/*.sh</xhtml:span>. It is recommended to place your configuration in a shell script within <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/profile.d</xhtml:span> to set your own system wide environmental variables.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/bashrc</xhtml:span> - System wide version of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.bashrc</xhtml:span>.  In Fedora derived distributions, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">etc/bashrc</xhtml:span> also invokes /etc/profile.d/*.sh if <xhtml:em>non-login</xhtml:em> shell, but redirects output to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/dev/null</xhtml:span> if <xhtml:em>non-interactive.</xhtml:em> <xhtml:strong>Is only executed for <xhtml:em>interactive</xhtml:em> shells or if <xhtml:span class="inline_block">BASH_ENV</xhtml:span> is set to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/bashrc</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:strong></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>User Shell Configuration Files:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">~/.bash_profile</xhtml:span> - Is executed to configure your shell before the initial command prompt. <xhtml:strong>Is only read by login shells.</xhtml:strong></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">~/.bashrc</xhtml:span> - Is executed for interactive shells. <xhtml:strong>only read by a shell that's both interactive and non-login</xhtml:strong></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> is set by order of precedence. If <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> is set in multiple locations, this order of precedence will determine the system's default <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Order of precedence:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:li>A file in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/profile.d/</xhtml:span> ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.sh</xhtml:span> - This will override any other system-wide <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> setting</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>In the file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/profile</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>On the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_umask.so</xhtml:span> module in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d/postlogin</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>In the file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/login.defs</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>In the file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/default/login</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Protect Information through  Access Control Lists

metadata.notes:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Other methods of setting a default user umask exist</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>If other methods are in use in your environment they should be audited</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The default user umask can be overridden with a user specific umask</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The user creating the directories or files has the discretion of changing the permissions:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Using the chmod command</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Setting a different default umask by adding the umask command into a User Shell Configuration File, (.bashrc), in their home directory</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Manually changing the umask for the duration of a login session by running the umask command</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Setting a secure default value for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> ensures that users make a conscious choice about their file permissions. A permissive <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> value could result in directories or files with excessive permissions that can be read and/or written to by unauthorized users.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script and perform the instructions in the output to set the default umask to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">027</xhtml:span> or more restrictive:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   l_output="" l_output2="" l_out=""<br />   file_umask_chk()<br />   {<br />      if grep -Psiq -- '^\h*umask\h+(0?[0-7][2-7]7|u(=[rwx]{0,3}),g=([rx]{0,2}),o=)(\h*#.*)?$' "$l_file"; then<br />         l_out="$l_out
 - umask is set correctly in "$l_file""<br />      elif grep -Psiq -- '^\h*umask\h+(([0-7][0-7][01][0-7] |[0-7][0-7][0-7][0-6] )|([0-7][01][0-7] |[0-7][0-7][0-6] )|(u=[rwx]{1,3},)?(((g=[rx]?[rx]?w[rx]?[rx]? )(,o=[rwx]{1,3})?)|((g=[wrx]{1,3},)?o=[wrx]{1,3} )))' "$l_file"; then<br />         l_output2="$l_output2
   - "$l_file""<br />      fi<br />   }<br />   while IFS= read -r -d $'\0' l_file; do<br />      file_umask_chk<br />   done < <(find /etc/profile.d/ -type f -name '*.sh' -print0)<br />   [ -n "$l_out" ] && l_output="$l_out"<br />   l_file="/etc/profile" && file_umask_chk<br />   l_file="/etc/bashrc" && file_umask_chk<br />   l_file="/etc/bash.bashrc" && file_umask_chk<br />   l_file="/etc/pam.d/postlogin"<br />   if grep -Psiq '^\h*session\h+[^#
]+\h+pam_umask\.so\h+([^#
]+\h+)?umask=(([0-7][0-7][01][0-7] |[0-7][0-7][0-7][0-6] )|([0-7][01][0-7] ))' "$l_file"; then<br />      l_output2="$l_output2
   - "$l_file""<br />   fi<br />   l_file="/etc/login.defs" && file_umask_chk<br />   l_file="/etc/default/login" && file_umask_chk<br />   if [ -z "$l_output2" ]; then<br />      echo -e " - No files contain a UMASK that is not restrictive enough
   No UMASK updates required to existing files"<br />   else<br />      echo -e "
 - UMASK is not restrictive enough in the following file(s):$l_output2

- Remediation Procedure:
 - Update these files and comment out the UMASK line
   or update umask to be "0027" or more restrictive"<br />   fi<br />   if [ -n "$l_output" ]; then<br />      echo -e "$l_output"<br />   else<br />      echo -e " - Configure UMASK in a file in the "/etc/profile.d/" directory ending in ".sh"

   Example Command (Hash to represent being run at a root prompt):

# printf '%s\
' "umask 027" > /etc/profile.d/50-systemwide_umask.sh
"<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Notes:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>This method only applies to bash and shell. If other shells are supported on the system, it is recommended that their configuration files also are checked</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>If the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pam_umask.so</xhtml:span> module is going to be used to set <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span>, ensure that it's not being overridden by another setting. Refer to the PAM_UMASK(8) man page for more information</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following to verify the default user <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span> is set to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">027</xhtml:span>(octal) or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">u=rwx,g=rx,o=</xhtml:span> (Symbolic) to enforce newly created directories' permissions to be <xhtml:span class="inline_block">750 (drwxr-x---)</xhtml:span>, and newly created file's permissions be <xhtml:span class="inline_block">640 (rw-r-----)</xhtml:span>, or more restrictive:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{   <br />    l_output="" l_output2=""<br />    file_umask_chk()<br />    {<br />       if grep -Psiq -- '^\h*umask\h+(0?[0-7][2-7]7|u(=[rwx]{0,3}),g=([rx]{0,2}),o=)(\h*#.*)?$' "$l_file"; then<br />          l_output="$l_output

Group.title: Logging and Auditing
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>The items in this section describe how to configure logging, log monitoring, and auditing, using tools included in most distributions.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>It is recommended that <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog </xhtml:span>be used for logging (with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">logwatch </xhtml:span>providing summarization) and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">auditd</xhtml:span> be used for auditing (with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">aureport </xhtml:span>providing summarization) to automatically monitor logs for intrusion attempts and other suspicious system behavior.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>In addition to the local log files created by the steps in this section, it is also recommended that sites collect copies of their system logs on a secure, centralized log server via an encrypted connection. Not only does centralized logging help sites correlate events that may be occurring on multiple systems, but having a second copy of the system log information may be critical after a system compromise where the attacker has modified the local log files on the affected system(s). If a log correlation system is deployed, configure it to process the logs described in this section.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Because it is often necessary to correlate log information from many different systems (particularly after a security incident) it is recommended that the time be synchronized among systems and devices connected to the local network. The standard Internet protocol for time synchronization is the Network Time Protocol (NTP), which is supported by most network-ready devices. Reference <<xhtml:a href="http://chrony.tuxfamily.org/">http://chrony.tuxfamily.org/</xhtml:a>> manual page for more information on configuring chrony.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>It is important that all logs described in this section be monitored on a regular basis and correlated to determine trends. A seemingly innocuous entry in one log could be more significant when compared to an entry in another log.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note on log file permissions:</xhtml:strong> There really isn't a "one size fits all" solution to the permissions on log files. Many sites utilize group permissions so that administrators who are in a defined security group, such as "wheel" do not have to elevate privileges to root in order to read log files. Also, if a third party log aggregation tool is used, it may need to have group permissions to read the log files, which is preferable to having it run setuid to root. Therefore, there are two remediation and audit steps for log file permissions. One is for systems that do not have a secured group method implemented that only permits root to read the log files (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">root:root 600</xhtml:span>). The other is for sites that do have such a setup and are designated as <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root:securegrp 640 </xhtml:span>where <xhtml:span class="inline_block">securegrp</xhtml:span> is the defined security group (in some cases <xhtml:span class="inline_block">wheel</xhtml:span>).</xhtml:p>

Group.title: System Logging
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>Logging services should be configured to prevent information leaks and to aggregate logs on a remote server so that they can be reviewed in the event of a system compromise. A centralized log server provides a single point of entry for further analysis, monitoring and filtering.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Security principals for logging</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Ensure transport layer security is implemented between the client and the log server.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Ensure that logs are rotated as per the environment requirements.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Ensure all locally generated logs have the appropriate permissions.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Ensure all security logs are sent to a remote log server.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Ensure the required events are logged.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>What is covered</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>This section will cover the minimum best practices for the usage of <xhtml:strong>either</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> <xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">journald</xhtml:span>. The recommendations are written such that each is wholly independent of each other and <xhtml:strong>only one is implemented</xhtml:strong>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>If your organization makes use of an enterprise wide logging system completely outside of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">journald</xhtml:span>, then the following recommendations do not directly apply. However, the principals of the recommendations should be followed regardless of what solution is implemented. If the enterprise solution incorporates either of these tools, careful consideration should be given to the following recommendations to determine exactly what applies.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Should your organization make use of both <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">journald</xhtml:span>, take care how the recommendations may or may not apply to you.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>What is not covered</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Enterprise logging systems not utilizing <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">journald</xhtml:span>. As logging is very situational and dependent on the local environment, not everything can be covered here.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Transport layer security should be applied to all remote logging functionality. Both <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">journald</xhtml:span> supports secure transport and should be configured as such.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The log server. There are a multitude of reasons for a centralized log server (and keeping a short period logging on the local system), but the log server is out of scope for these recommendations.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

Group.title: Configure systemd-journald service
Group.description:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-journald</xhtml:span> is a system service that collects and stores logging data. It creates and maintains structured, indexed journals based on logging information that is received from a variety of sources:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Kernel log messages, via kmsg</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Simple system log messages, via the libc syslog call</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Structured system log messages via the native Journal API</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Standard output and standard error of service units</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Audit records, originating from the kernel audit subsystem</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>The daemon will implicitly collect numerous metadata fields for each log messages in a secure and unfakeable way. See systemd.journal-fields man page for more information about the collected metadata.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The journal service stores log data either persistently below <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/var/log/journal</xhtml:span> or in a volatile way below <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/run/log/journal/</xhtml:span>. By default, log data is stored persistently if <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/var/log/journal/</xhtml:span> exists during boot, with an implicit fallback to volatile storage. Use <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Storage=</xhtml:span> in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">journald.conf</xhtml:span> to configure where log data is placed, independently of the existence of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/var/log/journal/</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>On systems where <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/var/log/journal/</xhtml:span> does not exist but where persistent logging is desired, and the default <xhtml:span class="inline_block">journald.conf</xhtml:span> is used, it is sufficient to create the directory and ensure it has the correct access modes and ownership.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-journald.service</xhtml:span> must be configured appropriately for either <xhtml:span class="inline_block">journald</xhtml:span> <xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> to operate effectively.</xhtml:p>

do<br />      l_file="$(tr -d '# ' <<< "$l_file")" a_out=() a_out2=()<br />      l_logfile_perms_line="$(awk '($1~/^(f|d)$/ && $2~/\/\S+/ && $3~/[0-9]{3,}/){print $2 ":" $3 ":" $4 ":" $5}' "$l_file")"<br />      while IFS=: read -r l_logfile l_mode l_user l_group; do<br />         if [ -d "$l_logfile" ]; then<br />            l_perm_mask="0027" l_type="Directory"<br />            grep -Psq '^(\/run|\/var\/lib\/systemd)\b' <<< "$l_logfile" && l_perm_mask="0022"<br />         else<br />            l_perm_mask="0137" l_type="File"<br />         fi<br />         grep -Psq '^(\/run|\/var\/lib\/systemd)\b' <<< "$l_logfile" && l_perm_mask="0022"<br />         f_file_chk<br />      done <<< "$l_logfile_perms_line"<br />      [ "${#a_out[@]}" -gt "0" ] && a_output+=(" - File: \"$l_file\" sets:" "${a_out[@]}")<br />      [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt "0" ] && a_output2+=(" - File: \"$l_file\" sets:" "${a_out2[@]}")<br />   done < <($l_analyze_cmd cat-config "$l_systemd_config_file" | tac | grep -Pio '^\h*#\h*\/[^#\n\r\h]+\.conf\b')<br />   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}" ""<br />   else<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** REVIEW **" \<br />      " -  Review file access to ensure they are set IAW site policy:" "${a_output2[@]}"<br />      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "" "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}" ""<br />   fi   <br />}

Rule.title: Ensure journald log file rotation is configured
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>Journald includes the capability of rotating log files regularly to avoid filling up the system with logs or making the logs unmanageably large. The file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/systemd/journald.conf</xhtml:span> is the configuration file used to specify how logs generated by Journald should be rotated.</xhtml:p>

Activate audit logging
Enable Detailed Logging

metadata.notes: <xhtml:p>See <xhtml:span class="inline_block">man 5 journald.conf</xhtml:span> for detailed information regarding the parameters in use.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>By keeping the log files smaller and more manageable, a system administrator can easily archive these files to another system and spend less time looking through inordinately large log files.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: AU-2, AU-7, AU-12

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/systemd/journald.conf</xhtml:span> or a file ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.conf</xhtml:span> the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/</xhtml:span> directory. Set the following parameters in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">[Journal]</xhtml:span> section to ensure logs are rotated according to site policy. The settings should be carefully understood as there are specific edge cases and prioritization of parameters.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example Configuration</xhtml:em>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">[Journal]<br />SystemMaxUse=1G<br />SystemKeepFree=500M<br />RuntimeMaxUse=200M<br />RuntimeKeepFree=50M<br />MaxFileSec=1month
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example script to create systemd drop-in configuration file:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">{<br />   a_settings=("SystemMaxUse=1G" "SystemKeepFree=500M" "RuntimeMaxUse=200M" "RuntimeKeepFree=50M" "MaxFileSec=1month")<br />   [ ! -d /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/ ] && mkdir /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/<br />   if grep -Psq -- '^\h*\[Journal\]' /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/60-journald.conf; then<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "${a_settings[@]}" >> /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/60-journald.conf<br />   else<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "[Journal]" "${a_settings[@]}" >> /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/60-journald.conf<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>If these settings appear in a canonically later file, or later in the same file, the setting will be overwritten</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Logfile size and configuration to move logfiles to a remote log server should be accounted for when configuring these settings</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>Run to following command to update the parameters in the service:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl reload-or-restart systemd-journald
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure only one logging system is in use
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>Best practices recommend that a single centralized logging system be used for log management, choose a single service either <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> <xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">journald</xhtml:span> to be used as a single centralized logging system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Configuring only one logging service either <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> <xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">journald</xhtml:span> avoids redundancy, optimizes resources, simplifies configuration and management, and ensures consistency.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:li>Determine whether to use <xhtml:span class="inline_block">journald</xhtml:span> <xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> depending on site needs</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Configure <xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-jounald.service</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Configure only <xhtml:strong>ONE</xhtml:strong> either <xhtml:span class="inline_block">journald</xhtml:span> <xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> and complete the recommendations in that subsection</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Return to this recommendation to ensure only one logging system is in use</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ol>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>

Group.title: Configure journald
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>Included in the systemd suite is a journaling service called systemd-journald.service for the collection and storage of logging data. It creates and maintains structured, indexed journals based on logging information that is received from a variety of sources such as:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Classic RFC3164 BSD syslog via the /dev/log socket
STDOUT/STDERR of programs via StandardOutput=journal + StandardError=journal in service files (both of which are default settings)
Kernel log messages via the /dev/kmsg device node
Audit records via the kernel’s audit subsystem
Structured log messages via journald’s native protocol
Any changes made to the systemd-journald configuration will require a re-start of systemd-journald</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> will be used for remote logging on the system this subsection can be skipped</xhtml:p>

Group.title: Configure systemd-journal-remote
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-journal-remote</xhtml:span> package includes <xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-journal-upload</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-journal-upload</xhtml:span> will upload journal entries to the URL specified with --url=. This program reads journal entries from one or more journal files, similarly to journalctl.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-journal-upload</xhtml:span> transfers the raw content of journal file and uses HTTP as a transport protocol.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-journal-upload.service</xhtml:span> is a system service that uses <xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-journal-upload</xhtml:span> to upload journal entries to a server. It uses the configuration in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">journal-upload.conf</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:strong>- IF -</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> is in use this subsection can be skipped.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-journal-remote</xhtml:span> package is part of the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">universe</xhtml:span> component, this may impact support and update frequency which should be considered when assessing organizational risk.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

Group.title: Configure rsyslog
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> software package may be used instead of the default <xhtml:span class="inline_block">journald</xhtml:span> logging mechanism.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Rsyslog has evolved over several decades. For this reason it supports three different configuration formats (“languages”):</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">basic</xhtml:span> - previously known as the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sysklogd</xhtml:span> format, this is the format best used to express basic things, such as where the statement fits on a single line.
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>It stems back to the original syslog.conf format, in use now for several decades.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The most common use case is matching on facility/severity and writing matching messages to a log file.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">advanced</xhtml:span> - previously known as the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">RainerScript</xhtml:span> format, this format was first available in rsyslog v6 and is the current, best and most precise format for non-trivial use cases where more than one line is needed.
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Prior to v7, there was a performance impact when using this format that encouraged use of the basic format for best results. Current versions of rsyslog do not suffer from this (historical) performance impact.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>This new style format is specifically targeted towards more advanced use cases like forwarding to remote hosts that might be partially offline.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">obsolete legacy</xhtml:span> - previously known simply as the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">legacy</xhtml:span> format, this format is exactly what its name implies: it is obsolete and should not be used when writing new configurations. It was created in the early days (up to rsyslog version 5) where we expected that rsyslog would extend sysklogd just mildly. Consequently, it was primarily aimed at small additions to the original sysklogd format.
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Practice has shown that it was notoriously hard to use for more advanced use cases, and thus we replaced it with the advanced format.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>In essence, everything that needs to be written on a single line that starts with a dollar sign is legacy format. Users of this format are encouraged to migrate to the basic or advanced formats.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> This section only applies if <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> is the chosen method for client side logging. Do not apply this section if <xhtml:span class="inline_block">journald</xhtml:span> is used.</xhtml:p>

Utilities exist to accept remote export of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-journald</xhtml:span> logs, however, use of the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> service provides a consistent means of log collection and export.</xhtml:p>

metadata.notes: <xhtml:p>As noted in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-journald</xhtml:span> man pages, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-journald</xhtml:span> logs may be exported to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> either through the process mentioned here, or through a facility like <xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-journald.service</xhtml:span>.  There are trade-offs involved in each implementation, where <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ForwardToSyslog</xhtml:span> will immediately capture all events (and forward to an external log server, if properly configured), but may not capture all boot-up activities.  Mechanisms such as <xhtml:span class="inline_block">systemd-journald.service</xhtml:span>, on the other hand, will record bootup events, but may delay sending the information to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span>, leading to the potential for log manipulation prior to export.  Be aware of the limitations of all tools employed to secure a system.</xhtml:p>
