Rule.title: Ensure rsyslog log file creation mode is configured
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> will create logfiles that do not already exist on the system.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">global()</xhtml:span> configuration object <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span>, available in rsyslog 8.26.0+, sets the rsyslogd process’ umask. If not specified, the system-provided default is used. The value given must always be a 4-digit octal number, with the initial digit being zero.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The legacy <xhtml:span class="inline_block">$umask</xhtml:span> parameter sets the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslogd</xhtml:span> process' umask. If not specified, the system-provided default is used. The value given must always be a 4-digit octal number, with the initial digit being zero.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The legacy <xhtml:span class="inline_block">$FileCreateMode</xhtml:span> parameter allows the setting of the mode with which <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslogd</xhtml:span> creates new files. If not specified, the value <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0644</xhtml:span> is used. The value given must always be a 4-digit octal number, with the initial digit being zero. Please note that the actual permission depend on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslogd</xhtml:span> process <xhtml:span class="inline_block">umask</xhtml:span>. If in doubt, use <xhtml:span class="inline_block">$umask 0000</xhtml:span> right at the beginning of the configuration file to remove any restrictions.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The legacy <xhtml:span class="inline_block">$FileCreateMode</xhtml:span> may be specified multiple times. If so, it specifies the creation mode for all selector lines that follow until the next <xhtml:span class="inline_block">$FileCreateMode</xhtml:span> parameter. Order of lines is vitally important.</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure rsyslog logging is configured
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> and configuration files specifies rules for logging and which files are to be used to log certain classes of messages.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Collect Audit Logs
Activate audit logging
Enable Detailed Logging

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>A great deal of important security-related information is sent via <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> (e.g., successful and failed su attempts, failed login attempts, root login attempts, etc.).</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: See the rsyslog.conf(5) man page for more information.
NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: AU-2, AU-7, AU-12

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit the following lines in the configuration file(s) returned by the audit as appropriate for your environment.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> The below configuration is shown for example purposes only. Due care should be given to how the organization wishes to store log data.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">*.emerg                                  :omusrmsg:*<br />auth,authpriv.*                          /var/log/secure<br />mail.*                                  -/var/log/mail<br />mail.info                               -/var/log/mail.info<br />mail.warning                            -/var/log/mail.warn<br />mail.err                                 /var/log/mail.err<br />cron.*                                   /var/log/cron<br />*.=warning;*.=err                       -/var/log/warn<br />*.crit                                   /var/log/warn<br />*.*;mail.none;news.none                 -/var/log/messages<br />local0,local1.*                         -/var/log/localmessages<br />local2,local3.*                         -/var/log/localmessages<br />local4,local5.*                         -/var/log/localmessages<br />local6,local7.*                         -/var/log/localmessages
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to reload the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslogd</xhtml:span> configuration:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl reload-or-restart rsyslog
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Review the contents of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/rsyslog.conf</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/rsyslog.d/*.conf</xhtml:span> files to ensure appropriate logging is set. In addition, run the following command and verify that the log files are logging information as expected:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following script and review the output from the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> configuration to ensure appropriate logging is set an in accordance with local site policy.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   l_analyze_cmd="$(readlink -f /bin/systemd-analyze)" l_include='\$IncludeConfig' a_config_files=("rsyslog.conf")<br />   while IFS= read -r l_file; do<br />      l_conf_loc="$(awk '$1~/^\s*'"$l_include"'$/ {print $2}' "$(tr -d '# ' <<< "$l_file")" | tail -n 1)"<br />      [ -n "$l_conf_loc" ] && break<br />   done < <($l_analyze_cmd cat-config "${a_config_files[@]}" | tac | grep -Pio '^\h*#\h*\/[^#\n\r\h]+\.conf\b')<br />   if [ -d "$l_conf_loc" ]; then<br />      l_dir="$l_conf_loc" l_ext="*"<br />   elif  grep -Psq '\/\*\.([^#/\n\r]+)?\h*$' <<< "$l_conf_loc" || [ -f "$(readlink -f "$l_conf_loc")" ]; then<br />      l_dir="$(dirname "$l_conf_loc")" l_ext="$(basename "$l_conf_loc")"<br />   fi<br />   while read -r -d $'\0' l_file_name; do<br />      [ -f "$(readlink -f "$l_file_name")" ] && a_config_files+=("$(readlink -f "$l_file_name")")<br />   done < <(find -L "$l_dir" -type f -name "$l_ext" -print0 2>/dev/null)<br />   for l_logfile in "${a_config_files[@]}"; do<br />      grep -PHs -- '^\h*[^#\n\r\/:]+\/var\/log\/.*$' "$l_logfile"<br />   done<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example output:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">/etc/rsyslog.d/60-rsyslog.conf:auth,authpriv.*           /var/log/secure<br />/etc/rsyslog.d/60-rsyslog.conf:mail.*                    -/var/log/mail<br />/etc/rsyslog.d/60-rsyslog.conf:mail.info                 -/var/log/mail.info<br />/etc/rsyslog.d/60-rsyslog.conf:mail.warning              -/var/log/mail.warn<br />/etc/rsyslog.d/60-rsyslog.conf:mail.err                  /var/log/mail.err<br />/etc/rsyslog.d/60-rsyslog.conf:cron.*                    /var/log/cron<br />/etc/rsyslog.d/60-rsyslog.conf:*.=warning;*.=err         -/var/log/warn<br />/etc/rsyslog.d/60-rsyslog.conf:*.crit                    /var/log/warn<br />/etc/rsyslog.d/60-rsyslog.conf:*.*;mail.none;news.none   -/var/log/messages<br />/etc/rsyslog.d/60-rsyslog.conf:local0,local1.*           -/var/log/localmessages<br />/etc/rsyslog.d/60-rsyslog.conf:local2,local3.*           -/var/log/localmessages<br />/etc/rsyslog.d/60-rsyslog.conf:local4,local5.*           -/var/log/localmessages<br />/etc/rsyslog.d/60-rsyslog.conf:local6,local7.*           -/var/log/localmessages<br />/etc/rsyslog.d/50-default.conf:auth,authpriv.*           /var/log/auth.log #<- Will be ignored<br />/etc/rsyslog.d/50-default.conf:*.*;auth,authpriv.none    -/var/log/syslog<br />/etc/rsyslog.d/50-default.conf:kern.*                    -/var/log/kern.log<br />/etc/rsyslog.d/50-default.conf:mail.*                    -/var/log/mail.log #<- Will be ignored<br />/etc/rsyslog.d/50-default.conf:mail.err                  /var/log/mail.err #<- Will be ignored
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Output is generated as <CONFIGURATION_FILE>:<PARAMETER></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Files are listed in order of precedence. If the same parameter is listed multiple times, only the first occurrence will be used be the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> daemon</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure rsyslog is configured to send logs to a remote log host
Rule.description: <xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> supports the ability to send log events it gathers to a remote log host or to receive messages from remote hosts, thus enabling centralized log management.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Collect Audit Logs
Activate audit logging
Enable Detailed Logging

metadata.notes: <xhtml:p>In addition, see the <xhtml:a href="https://www.rsyslog.com/doc/master/tutorials/tls.html">rsyslog documentation</xhtml:a> for implementation details of TLS.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Storing log data on a remote host protects log integrity from local attacks. If an attacker gains root access on the local system, they could tamper with or remove log data that is stored on the local system.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: See the rsyslog.conf(5) man page for more information.

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> configuration and add the following line (where <xhtml:span class="inline_block">loghost.example.com</xhtml:span> is the name of your central log host). The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">target</xhtml:span> directive may either be a fully qualified domain name or an IP address.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example script to create a drop-in configuration file:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_parameters=('*.* action(type="omfwd" target="loghost.example.com" port="514" protocol="tcp"' \<br />   '           action.resumeRetryCount="100"' '           queue.type="LinkedList" queue.size="1000")')<br />   [ ! -d "/etc/rsyslog.d/" ] && mkdir /etc/rsyslod.d/<br />   printf '%s\n' "" "${a_parameters[@]}" >> /etc/rsyslog.d/60-rsyslog.conf<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to reload <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog.service</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl reload-or-restart rsyslog.service
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script and review the output of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> configuration. Verify that logs are sent to a central host used by your organization:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>basic format</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   l_analyze_cmd="$(readlink -f /bin/systemd-analyze)" l_include='\$IncludeConfig' a_config_files=("rsyslog.conf")<br />   while IFS= read -r l_file; do<br />      l_conf_loc="$(awk '$1~/^\s*'"$l_include"'$/ {print $2}' "$(tr -d '# ' <<< "$l_file")" | tail -n 1)"<br />      [ -n "$l_conf_loc" ] && break<br />   done < <($l_analyze_cmd cat-config "${a_config_files[@]}" | tac | grep -Pio '^\h*#\h*\/[^#\n\r\h]+\.conf\b')<br />   if [ -d "$l_conf_loc" ]; then<br />      l_dir="$l_conf_loc" l_ext="*"<br />   elif  grep -Psq '\/\*\.([^#/\n\r]+)?\h*$' <<< "$l_conf_loc" || [ -f "$(readlink -f "$l_conf_loc")" ]; then<br />      l_dir="$(dirname "$l_conf_loc")" l_ext="$(basename "$l_conf_loc")"<br />   fi<br />   while read -r -d $'\0' l_file_name; do<br />      [ -f "$(readlink -f "$l_file_name")" ] && a_config_files+=("$(readlink -f "$l_file_name")")<br />   done < <(find -L "$l_dir" -type f -name "$l_ext" -print0 2>/dev/null)<br />   for l_logfile in "${a_config_files[@]}"; do<br />      grep -Hs -- "^*.*[^I][^I]*@" "$l_logfile"<br />   done<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Output should include <xhtml:span class="inline_block">@@<FQDN or IP of remote loghost></xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example output:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">/etc/rsyslog.d/60-rsyslog.conf:*.* @@loghost.example.com
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong>
Run the following script and review the output of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> configuration. Verify that logs are sent to a central host used by your organization:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>advanced format</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   l_analyze_cmd="$(readlink -f /bin/systemd-analyze)" l_include='\$IncludeConfig' a_config_files=("rsyslog.conf")<br />   while IFS= read -r l_file; do<br />      l_conf_loc="$(awk '$1~/^\s*'"$l_include"'$/ {print $2}' "$(tr -d '# ' <<< "$l_file")" | tail -n 1)"<br />      [ -n "$l_conf_loc" ] && break<br />   done < <($l_analyze_cmd cat-config "${a_config_files[@]}" | tac | grep -Pio '^\h*#\h*\/[^#\n\r\h]+\.conf\b')<br />   if [ -d "$l_conf_loc" ]; then<br />      l_dir="$l_conf_loc" l_ext="*"<br />   elif  grep -Psq '\/\*\.([^#/\n\r]+)?\h*$' <<< "$l_conf_loc" || [ -f "$(readlink -f "$l_conf_loc")" ]; then<br />      l_dir="$(dirname "$l_conf_loc")" l_ext="$(basename "$l_conf_loc")"<br />   fi<br />   while read -r -d $'\0' l_file_name; do<br />      [ -f "$(readlink -f "$l_file_name")" ] && a_config_files+=("$(readlink -f "$l_file_name")")<br />   done < <(find -L "$l_dir" -type f -name "$l_ext" -print0 2>/dev/null)<br />   for l_logfile in "${a_config_files[@]}"; do<br />      grep -PHsi -- '^\s*([^#]+\s+)?action\(([^#]+\s+)?\btarget=\"?[^#"]+\"?\b' "$l_logfile"<br />   done<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Output should include <xhtml:span class="inline_block">target=<FQDN or IP of remote loghost></xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example output:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">/etc/rsyslog.d/60-rsyslog.conf:*.* action(type="omfwd" target="loghost.example.com" port="514" protocol="tcp"
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure rsyslog is not configured to receive logs from a remote client
Rule.description: <xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> supports the ability to receive messages from remote hosts, thus acting as a log server. Clients should not receive data from other hosts.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software
Ensure Only Approved Ports, Protocols and Services Are Running

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>If a client is configured to also receive data, thus turning it into a server, the client system is acting outside its operational boundary.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: AU-2, AU-7, AU-12, CM-6

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Unless the system's primary function is to serve as a logfile server , modify the files returned by the Audit Procedure and remove the specific lines highlighted by the audit. Verify none of the following entries are present in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> configuration.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>advanced format</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">module(load="imtcp")<br />input(type="imtcp" port="514")
</xhtml:code>

<xhtml:code class="code_block">$ModLoad imtcp<br />$InputTCPServerRun
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Reload the service:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl reload-or-restart rsyslog

Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Unless the system's primary function is to serve as a logfile server, run the following script to review the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span> configuration and verify that the system is not configured to accept incoming logs.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>advanced format</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_output2=()<br />   l_analyze_cmd="$(readlink -f /bin/systemd-analyze)" l_include='\$IncludeConfig' a_config_files=("rsyslog.conf")<br />   while IFS= read -r l_file; do<br />      l_conf_loc="$(awk '$1~/^\s*'"$l_include"'$/ {print $2}' "$(tr -d '# ' <<< "$l_file")" | tail -n 1)"<br />      [ -n "$l_conf_loc" ] && break<br />   done < <($l_analyze_cmd cat-config "${a_config_files[@]}" | tac | grep -Pio '^\h*#\h*\/[^#\n\r\h]+\.conf\b')<br />   if [ -d "$l_conf_loc" ]; then<br />      l_dir="$l_conf_loc" l_ext="*"<br />   elif  grep -Psq '\/\*\.([^#/\n\r]+)?\h*$' <<< "$l_conf_loc" || [ -f "$(readlink -f "$l_conf_loc")" ]; then<br />      l_dir="$(dirname "$l_conf_loc")" l_ext="$(basename "$l_conf_loc")"<br />   fi<br />   while read -r -d $'\0' l_file_name; do<br />      [ -f "$(readlink -f "$l_file_name")" ] && a_config_files+=("$(readlink -f "$l_file_name")")<br />   done < <(find -L "$l_dir" -type f -name "$l_ext" -print0 2>/dev/null)<br />   for l_logfile in "${a_config_files[@]}"; do<br />      l_fail="$(grep -Psi -- '^\h*module\(load=\"?imtcp\"?\)' "$l_logfile")"<br />      [ -n "$l_fail" ] && a_output2+=("- Advanced format entry to accept incoming logs: \"$l_fail\"" "found in: \"$l_logfile\"")<br />      l_fail="$(grep -Psi -- '^\h*input\(type=\"?imtcp\"?\b' "$l_logfile")"<br />      [ -n "$l_fail" ] && a_output2+=("- Advanced format entry to accept incoming logs: \"$l_fail\"" "found in: \"$l_logfile\"")<br />      l_fail="$(grep -Psi -- '^\h*module\(load=\"?imtcp\"?\)' "$l_logfile")"<br />      [ -n "$l_fail" ] && a_output2+=("- Obsolete format entry to accept incoming logs: \"$l_fail\"" "found in: \"$l_logfile\"")<br />      l_fail="$(grep -Psi -- '^\h*input\(type=\"?imtcp\"?\b' "$l_logfile")"<br />      [ -n "$l_fail" ] && a_output2+=("- Obsolete format entry to accept incoming logs: \"$l_fail\"" "found in: \"$l_logfile\"")<br />   done<br />   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le "0" ]; then<br />      printf '%s\n'  "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" " - No entries to accept incoming logs found"<br />   else<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" " - Reason(s) for audit failure:" "${a_output2[@]}"<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure logrotate is configured
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The system includes the capability of rotating log files regularly to avoid filling up the system with logs or making the logs unmanageably large. The file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/logrotate.d/rsyslog</xhtml:span> is the configuration file used to rotate log files created by <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rsyslog</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Ensure Adequate Audit Log Storage
Ensure adequate storage for logs

metadata.notes: <xhtml:p>If no <xhtml:span class="inline_block">maxage</xhtml:span> setting is set for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">logrotate</xhtml:span> a situation can occur where <xhtml:span class="inline_block">logrotate</xhtml:span> is interrupted and fails to delete rotated log files.  It is recommended to set this to a value greater than the longest any log file should exist on your system to ensure that any such log file is removed but standard rotation settings are not overridden.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>By keeping the log files smaller and more manageable, a system administrator can easily archive these files to another system and spend less time looking through inordinately large log files.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/logrotate.conf</xhtml:span>, or the appropriate configuration file provided by the script in the Audit Procedure, as necessary to ensure logs are rotated according to site policy.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to analyze the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">logrotate</xhtml:span> configuration:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   l_analyze_cmd="$(readlink -f /bin/systemd-analyze)" l_config_file="/etc/logrotate.conf"<br />   l_include="$(awk '$1~/^\s*include$/{print$2}' "$l_config_file" 2>/dev/null)"<br />   [ -d "$l_include" ] && l_include="$l_include/*"<br />   $l_analyze_cmd cat-config "$l_config_file" $l_include<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> The last occurrence of a argument is the one used for the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">logrotate</xhtml:span> configuration</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.description:

<xhtml:p>In general log files are found in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/var/log/</xhtml:span>, although application can be configured to store logs elsewhere. Should your application store logs in another, ensure to run the same test on that location.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>It is important that log files have the correct permissions to ensure that sensitive data is protected and that only the appropriate users / groups have access to them.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to update permissions and ownership on files in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/var/log</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Although the script is not destructive, ensure that the output of the audit procedure is captured in the event that the remediation causes issues.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_output2=()<br />   f_file_test_fix()<br />   {<br />      a_out2=()<br />      maxperm="$( printf '%o' $(( 0777 & ~$perm_mask)) )"<br />      if [ $(( $l_mode & $perm_mask )) -gt 0 ]; then<br />         a_out2+=("   o Mode: \"$l_mode\" should be \"$maxperm\" or more restrictive" "     x Removing excess permissions")<br />         chmod "$l_rperms" "$l_fname"<br />      fi<br />      if [[ ! "$l_user" =~ $l_auser ]]; then<br />         a_out2+=("   o Owned by: \"$l_user\" and should be owned by \"${l_auser//|/ or }\"" "     x Changing ownership to: \"$l_fix_account\"")<br />         chown "$l_fix_account" "$l_fname"<br />      fi<br />      if [[ ! "$l_group" =~ $l_agroup ]]; then<br />         a_out2+=("   o Group owned by: \"$l_group\" and should be group owned by \"${l_agroup//|/ or }\"" "     x Changing group ownership to: \"$l_fix_account\"")<br />         chgrp "$l_fix_account" "$l_fname"<br />      fi<br />      [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=(" - File: \"$l_fname\" is:" "${a_out2[@]}")<br />   }<br />   l_fix_account='root'<br />   while IFS= read -r -d $'\0' l_file; do<br />      while IFS=: read -r l_fname l_mode l_user l_group; do<br />         if grep -Pq -- '\/(apt)\h*$' <<< "$(dirname "$l_fname")"; then<br />            perm_mask='0133' l_rperms="u-x,go-wx" l_auser="root" l_agroup="(root|adm)"; f_file_test_fix<br />         else<br />            case "$(basename "$l_fname")" in<br />               lastlog | lastlog.* | wtmp | wtmp.* | wtmp-* | btmp | btmp.* | btmp-* | README)<br />                  perm_mask='0113' l_rperms="ug-x,o-wx" l_auser="root" l_agroup="(root|utmp)"<br />                  f_file_test_fix ;;<br />               cloud-init.log* | localmessages* | waagent.log*)<br />                  perm_mask='0133' l_rperms="u-x,go-wx" l_auser="(root|syslog)" l_agroup="(root|adm)"<br />                  file_test_fix ;;<br />               secure | auth.log | syslog | messages)<br />                  perm_mask='0137' l_rperms="u-x,g-wx,o-rwx" l_auser="(root|syslog)" l_agroup="(root|adm)"<br />                  f_file_test_fix ;;<br />               SSSD | sssd)<br />                  perm_mask='0117' l_rperms="ug-x,o-rwx" l_auser="(root|SSSD)" l_agroup="(root|SSSD)"<br />                  f_file_test_fix ;;<br />               gdm | gdm3)<br />                  perm_mask='0117' l_rperms="ug-x,o-rwx" l_auser="root" l_agroup="(root|gdm|gdm3)"<br />                  f_file_test_fix ;;<br />               *.journal | *.journal~)<br />                  perm_mask='0137' l_rperms="u-x,g-wx,o-rwx" l_auser="root" l_agroup="(root|systemd-journal)"       <br />                  f_file_test_fix ;;<br />               *)<br />                  perm_mask='0137' l_rperms="u-x,g-wx,o-rwx" l_auser="(root|syslog)" l_agroup="(root|adm)"<br />                  if [ "$l_user" = "root" ] || ! grep -Pq -- "^\h*$(awk -F: '$1=="'"$l_user"'" {print $7}' /etc/passwd)\b" /etc/shells; then<br />                     ! grep -Pq -- "$l_auser" <<< "$l_user" && l_auser="(root|syslog|$l_user)"<br />                     ! grep -Pq -- "$l_agroup" <<< "$l_group" && l_agroup="(root|adm|$l_group)"<br />                  fi<br />                  f_file_test_fix ;;<br />            esac<br />         fi<br />      done < <(stat -Lc '%n:%#a:%U:%G' "$l_file")<br />   done < <(find -L /var/log -type f \( -perm /0137 -o ! -user root -o ! -group root \) -print0)<br />   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then # If all files passed, then we report no changes<br />      a_output+=("  - All files in \"/var/log/\" have appropriate permissions and ownership")<br />      printf '\n%s' "- All files in \"/var/log/\" have appropriate permissions and ownership" "  o No changes required" ""<br />   else<br />      printf '\n%s' "${a_output2[@]}" ""<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> You may also need to change the configuration for your logging software or services for any logs that had incorrect permissions.</xhtml:p>

</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Group.title: System Auditing
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>The Linux Auditing System operates on a set of rules that collects certain types of system activity to facilitate incident investigation, detect unauthorized access or modification of data.  By default events will be logged to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/var/log/audit/audit.log</xhtml:span>, which can be configured in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/auditd.conf</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The following types of audit rules can be specified:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Control rules: Configuration of the auditing system.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>File system rules: Allow the auditing of access to a particular file or a directory. Also known as file watches.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>System call rules: Allow logging of system calls that any specified program makes.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>Audit rules can be set:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>On the command line using the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">auditctl</xhtml:span> utility. These rules are not persistent across reboots.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>In <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules</xhtml:span>. These rules have to be merged and loaded before they are active.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Notes:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>For 64 bit systems that have <xhtml:span class="inline_block">arch</xhtml:span> as a rule parameter, you will need two rules: one for 64 bit and one for 32 bit systems calls.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>If the auditing system is configured to be locked (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">-e 2</xhtml:span>), a system reboot will be required in order to load any changes.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Key names are optional on the rules and will not be used as a compliance auditing. The usage of key names is highly recommended as it facilitates organization and searching, as such, all remediation steps will have key names supplied.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>It is best practice to store the rules, in number prepended files, in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/rules.d/</xhtml:span>. Rules must end in a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.rules</xhtml:span> suffix. This then requires the use of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">augenrules</xhtml:span> to merge all the rules into <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/audit.rules</xhtml:span> based on their their alphabetical (lexical) sort order. All benchmark recommendations follow this best practice for remediation, specifically using the prefix of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">50</xhtml:span> which is centre weighed if all rule sets make use of the number prepending naming convention.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Your system may have been customized to change the default <xhtml:span class="inline_block">UID_MIN</xhtml:span>. All samples output uses <xhtml:span class="inline_block">1000</xhtml:span>, but this value will not be used in compliance auditing. To confirm the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">UID_MIN</xhtml:span> for your system, run the following command: <xhtml:span class="inline_block">awk '/^\s*UID_MIN/{print $2}' /etc/login.defs</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Normalization</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The Audit system normalizes some entries, so when you look at the sample output keep in mind that:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>With regards to users whose login UID is not set, the values <xhtml:span class="inline_block">-1</xhtml:span> / <xhtml:span class="inline_block">unset</xhtml:span> / <xhtml:span class="inline_block">4294967295</xhtml:span> are equivalent and normalized to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">-1</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>When comparing field types and both sides of the comparison is valid fields types, such as<xhtml:span class="inline_block">euid!=uid</xhtml:span>, then the auditing system may normalize such that the output is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">uid!=euid</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Some parts of the rule may be rearranged whilst others are dependant on previous syntax. For example, the following two statements are the same:</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execve -C uid!=euid -F auid!=-1 -F key=user_emulation
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>and</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -C euid!=uid -F auid!=unset -S execve -k user_emulation
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Capacity planning</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The recommendations in this section implement auditing policies that not only produces large quantities of logged data, but may also negatively impact system performance. Capacity planning is critical in order not to adversely impact production environments.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Disk space. If a significantly large set of events are captured, additional on system or off system storage may need to be allocated. If the logs are not sent to a remote log server, ensure that log rotation is implemented else the disk will fill up and the system will halt. Even when logs are sent to a log server, ensure sufficient disk space to allow caching of logs in the case of temporary network outages.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Disk IO. It is not just the amount of data collected that should be considered, but the rate at which logs are generated.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>CPU overhead. System call rules might incur considerable CPU overhead. Test the systems open/close syscalls per second with and without the rules to gauge the impact of the rules.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># find /boot -type f -name 'grub.cfg' -exec grep -Ph -- '^\h*linux' {} + | grep -v 'audit=1'
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure audit_backlog_limit is sufficient
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>In the kernel-level audit subsystem, a socket buffer queue is used to hold audit events. Whenever a new audit event is received, it is logged and prepared to be added to this queue.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The kernel boot parameter <xhtml:span class="inline_block">audit_backlog_limit=N</xhtml:span>, with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">N</xhtml:span> representing the amount of messages, will ensure that a queue cannot grow beyond a certain size. If an audit event is logged which would grow the queue beyond this limit, then a failure occurs and is handled according to the system configuration</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Collect Audit Logs
Activate audit logging
Enable Detailed Logging

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>If an audit event is logged which would grow the queue beyond the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">audit_backlog_limit</xhtml:span>, then a failure occurs, auditd records will be lost, and potential malicious activity could go undetected.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: AU-2, AU-3, AU-12

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/default/grub</xhtml:span> and add <xhtml:span class="inline_block">audit_backlog_limit=N</xhtml:span> to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX. The recommended size for <xhtml:span class="inline_block">N</xhtml:span> is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">8192</xhtml:span> or larger.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Example:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="audit_backlog_limit=8192"
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to update the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">grub2</xhtml:span> configuration:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># update-grub
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command and verify the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">audit_backlog_limit=</xhtml:span> parameter is set:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># find /boot -type f -name 'grub.cfg' -exec grep -Ph -- '^\h*linux' {} + | grep -Pv 'audit_backlog_limit=\d+\b'
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

artifact_expression.artifact_title: Script Check Engine Check "nix_grub_option_exist_chk.sh" passing "audit_backlog_limit=\d+" as "XCCDF_VALUE_REGEX"

Group.title: Configure Data Retention
Group.description: <xhtml:p>When auditing, it is important to carefully configure the storage requirements for audit logs. By default, auditd will max out the log files at 5MB and retain only 4 copies of them. Older versions will be deleted. It is possible on a system that the 20 MBs of audit logs may fill up the system causing loss of audit data. While the recommendations here provide guidance, check your site policy for audit storage requirements.</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure audit log storage size is configured
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>Configure the maximum size of the audit log file. Once the log reaches the maximum size, it will be rotated and a new log file will be started.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Ensure Adequate Audit Log Storage
Ensure adequate storage for logs

metadata.notes:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">max_log_file</xhtml:span> parameter is measured in megabytes.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Other methods of log rotation may be appropriate based on site policy.  One example is time-based rotation strategies which don't have native support in auditd configurations.  Manual audit of custom configurations should be evaluated for effectiveness and completeness.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>It is important that an appropriate size is determined for log files so that they do not impact the system and audit data is not lost.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Set the following parameter in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/auditd.conf</xhtml:span>  in accordance with site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">max_log_file = <MB>
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command and ensure output is in compliance with site policy:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Po -- '^\h*max_log_file\h*=\h*\d+\b' /etc/audit/auditd.conf<br /><br />max_log_file = <MB>
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

artifact_expression.artifact_title: Ensure at least one file named /etc/audit/auditd.conf exists and matches pattern ^\h*max_log_file\h*=\h*\d+\b.*$

Rule.title: Ensure audit logs are not automatically deleted
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">max_log_file_action</xhtml:span>  setting determines how to handle the audit log file reaching the max file size. A value of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">keep_logs</xhtml:span>  will rotate the logs but never delete old logs.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Ensure Adequate Audit Log Storage
Ensure adequate storage for logs

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>In high security contexts, the benefits of maintaining a long audit history exceed the cost of storing the audit history.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Set the following parameter in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/auditd.conf:</xhtml:span></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">max_log_file_action = keep_logs
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command and verify output matches:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep max_log_file_action /etc/audit/auditd.conf<br /><br />max_log_file_action = keep_logs
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

artifact_expression.artifact_title: Ensure at least one file named /etc/audit/auditd.conf exists and matches pattern ^\s*max_log_file_action\s*=\s*keep_logs\s*(\s+#.*)?$

Rule.title: Ensure system is disabled when audit logs are full
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">auditd</xhtml:span> daemon can be configured to halt the system or put the system in single user mode, if no free space is available or an error is detected on the partition that holds the audit log files.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">disk_full_action</xhtml:span> parameter tells the system what action to take when no free space is available on the partition that holds the audit log files. Valid values are <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ignore</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rotate</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">exec</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">suspend</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">single</xhtml:span>, and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">halt</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">ignore</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will issue a syslog message but no other action is taken</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will issue a warning to syslog</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">rotate</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will rotate logs, losing the oldest to free up space</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">exec</xhtml:span>,   /path-to-script will execute the script. You cannot pass parameters to the script. The script is also responsible for telling the auditd daemon to resume logging once its completed its action</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">suspend</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will stop writing records to the disk</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">single</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will put the computer system in single user mode</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">halt</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will shut down the system</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">disk_error_action</xhtml:span> parameter tells the system what action to take when an error is detected on the partition that holds the audit log files. Valid values are <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ignore</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">exec</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">suspend</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">single</xhtml:span>, and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">halt</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">ignore</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will not take any action</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will issue no more than 5 consecutive warnings to syslog</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">exec</xhtml:span>,   /path-to-script will execute the script. You cannot pass parameters to the script</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">suspend</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will stop writing records to the disk</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">single</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will put the computer system in single user mode</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">halt</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will shut down the system</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

safeguard.title: Collect Audit Logs
Ensure Adequate Audit Log Storage

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>In high security contexts, the risk of detecting unauthorized access or nonrepudiation exceeds the benefit of the system's availability.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: AU-2, AU-8, AU-12, SI-5

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Set one of the following parameters in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/auditd.conf</xhtml:span> depending on your local security policies.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">disk_full_action = <halt|single><br />disk_error_action = <syslog|single|halt>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">disk_full_action = halt<br />disk_error_action = halt
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">disk_full_action</xhtml:span> parameter:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Set to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">halt</xhtml:span> - the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">auditd</xhtml:span> daemon will shutdown the system when the disk partition containing the audit logs becomes full.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Set to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">single</xhtml:span> - the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">auditd</xhtml:span> daemon will put the computer system in single user mode when the disk partition containing the audit logs becomes full.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">disk_error_action</xhtml:span> parameter:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Set to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">halt</xhtml:span> - the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">auditd</xhtml:span> daemon will shutdown the system when an error is detected on the partition that holds the audit log files.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Set to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">single</xhtml:span> - the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">auditd</xhtml:span> daemon will put the computer system in single user mode when an error is detected on the partition that holds the audit log files.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Set to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog</xhtml:span> - the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">auditd</xhtml:span> daemon will issue no more than 5 consecutive warnings to syslog when an error is detected on the partition that holds the audit log files.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command and verify the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">disk_full_action</xhtml:span> is set to either <xhtml:span class="inline_block">halt</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">single</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pi -- '^\h*disk_full_action\h*=\h*(halt|single)\b' /etc/audit/auditd.conf<br /><br />disk_full_action = <halt|single>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command and verify the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">disk_error_action</xhtml:span> is set to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">single</xhtml:span>, or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">halt</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># grep -Pi -- '^\h*disk_error_action\h*=\h*(syslog|single|halt)\b' /etc/audit/auditd.conf<br /><br />disk_error_action = <syslog|single|halt>
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

artifact_expression.artifact_title: Ensure at least one file named /etc/audit/auditd.conf exists and matches pattern (?i)^\h*disk_full_action\h*=\h*(halt|single)\b
Ensure at least one file named /etc/audit/auditd.conf exists and matches pattern (?i)^\h*disk_error_action\h*=\h*(syslog|single|halt)\b

Rule.title: Ensure system warns when audit logs are low on space
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">auditd</xhtml:span> daemon can be configured to halt the system, put the system in single user mode or send a warning message, if the partition that holds the audit log files is low on space.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">space_left_action</xhtml:span> parameter tells the system what action to take when the system has detected that it is starting to get low on disk space. Valid values are <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ignore</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rotate</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">email</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">exec</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">suspend</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">single</xhtml:span>, and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">halt</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">ignore</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon does nothing</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will issue a warning to syslog</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">rotate</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will rotate logs, losing the oldest to free up space</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">email</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will send a warning to the email account specified in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">action_mail_acct</xhtml:span> as well as sending the message to syslog</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">exec</xhtml:span>,   /path-to-script will execute the script. You cannot pass parameters to the script. The script is also responsible for telling the auditd daemon to resume logging once its completed its action</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">suspend</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will stop writing records to the disk</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">single</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will put the computer system in single user mode</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">halt</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will shut down the system</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">admin_space_left_action</xhtml:span> parameter tells the system what action to take when the system has detected that it is  low on disk space. Valid values are <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ignore</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">rotate</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">email</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">exec</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">suspend</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">single</xhtml:span>, and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">halt</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">ignore</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon does nothing</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">syslog</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will issue a warning to syslog</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">rotate</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will rotate logs, losing the oldest to free up space</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">email</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will send a warning to the email account specified in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">action_mail_acct</xhtml:span> as well as sending the message to syslog</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">exec</xhtml:span>,   /path-to-script will execute the script. You cannot pass parameters to the script. The script is also responsible for telling the auditd daemon to resume logging once its completed its action</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">suspend</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will stop writing records to the disk</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">single</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will put the computer system in single user mode</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">halt</xhtml:span>, the audit daemon will shut down the system</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

Group.title: Configure auditd Rules
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>The Audit system operates on a set of rules that define what is to be captured in the log files.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The following types of Audit rules can be specified:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Control rules: Allow the Audit system's behavior and some of its configuration to be modified.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>File system rules: Allow the auditing of access to a particular file or a directory. (Also known as file watches)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>System call rules: Allow logging of system calls that any specified program makes.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>Audit rules can be set:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>on the command line using the auditctl utility. Note that these rules are not persistent across reboots.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>in a file ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.rules</xhtml:span> in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/rules.d/</xhtml:span> directory.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> The Linux Benchmarks are written and tested against x86_64 processor architecture. If you are running a different processor type, please review and update the audit rules for the processor architecture of the system</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure changes to system administration scope (sudoers) is collected
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>Monitor scope changes for system administrators. If the system has been properly configured to force system administrators to log in as themselves first and then use the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">sudo</xhtml:span> command to execute privileged commands, it is possible to monitor changes in scope. The file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers</xhtml:span>, or files in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers.d</xhtml:span>, will be written to when the file(s) or related attributes have changed. The audit records will be tagged with the identifier "scope".</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Collect Detailed Audit Logs
Log and Alert on Changes to Administrative Group Membership

metadata.notes:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Potential reboot required</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>If the auditing configuration is locked (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">-e 2</xhtml:span>), then <xhtml:span class="inline_block">augenrules</xhtml:span> will not warn in any way that rules could not be loaded into the running configuration. A system reboot will be required to load the rules into the running configuration.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>System call structure</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>For performance (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">man 7 audit.rules</xhtml:span>) reasons it is preferable to have all the system calls on one line. However, your configuration may have them on one line each or some other combination. This is important to understand for both the auditing and remediation sections as the examples given are optimized for performance as per the man page.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Changes in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/sudoers.d</xhtml:span> files can indicate that an unauthorized change has been made to the scope of system administrator activity.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit or create a file in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/rules.d/</xhtml:span> directory, ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.rules</xhtml:span> extension, with the relevant rules to monitor scope changes for system administrators.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># printf "<br />-w /etc/sudoers -p wa -k scope<br />-w /etc/sudoers.d -p wa -k scope<br />" >> /etc/audit/rules.d/50-scope.rules
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Merge and load the rules into active configuration:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># augenrules --load
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Check if reboot is required.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># if [[ $(auditctl -s | grep "enabled") =~ "2" ]]; then printf "Reboot required to load rules\n"; fi
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>On disk configuration</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to check the on disk rules:</xhtml:p>

Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>Record changes to network environment files or system calls. The below parameters monitors the following system calls, and write an audit event on system call exit:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">sethostname</xhtml:span> - set the systems host name</xhtml:li>

</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>The files being monitored are:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/issue</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/issue.net</xhtml:span> - messages displayed pre-login</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/hosts</xhtml:span> - file containing host names and associated IP addresses</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/networks</xhtml:span> - symbolic names for networks</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/network/</xhtml:span> - directory containing network interface scripts and configurations files</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/netplan/</xhtml:span> - central location for YAML networking configurations files</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

Rule.title: Ensure use of privileged commands are collected
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>Monitor privileged programs, those that have the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">setuid</xhtml:span> and/or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">setgid</xhtml:span> bit set on execution, to determine if unprivileged users are running these commands.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Collect Detailed Audit Logs
Activate audit logging

metadata.notes:
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Potential reboot required</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>If the auditing configuration is locked (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">-e 2</xhtml:span>), then <xhtml:span class="inline_block">augenrules</xhtml:span> will not warn in any way that rules could not be loaded into the running configuration. A system reboot will be required to load the rules into the running configuration.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>System call structure</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>For performance (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">man 7 audit.rules</xhtml:span>) reasons it is preferable to have all the system calls on one line. However, your configuration may have them on one line each or some other combination. This is important to understand for both the auditing and remediation sections as the examples given are optimized for performance as per the man page.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Execution of privileged commands by non-privileged users could be an indication of someone trying to gain unauthorized access to the system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Edit or create a file in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/rules.d/</xhtml:span> directory, ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.rules</xhtml:span> extension, with the relevant rules to monitor the use of privileged commands.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example script:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />  UID_MIN=$(awk '/^\s*UID_MIN/{print $2}' /etc/login.defs)<br />  AUDIT_RULE_FILE="/etc/audit/rules.d/50-privileged.rules"<br />  NEW_DATA=()<br />  for PARTITION in $(findmnt -n -l -k -it $(awk '/nodev/ { print $2 }' /proc/filesystems | paste -sd,) | grep -Pv "noexec|nosuid" | awk '{print $1}'); do<br />    readarray -t DATA < <(find "${PARTITION}" -xdev -perm /6000 -type f | awk -v UID_MIN=${UID_MIN} '{print "-a always,exit -F path=" $1 " -F perm=x -F auid>="UID_MIN" -F auid!=unset -k privileged" }')<br />      for ENTRY in "${DATA[@]}"; do<br />        NEW_DATA+=("${ENTRY}")<br />      done<br />  done<br />  readarray &> /dev/null -t OLD_DATA < "${AUDIT_RULE_FILE}"<br />  COMBINED_DATA=( "${OLD_DATA[@]}" "${NEW_DATA[@]}" )<br />  printf '%s\n' "${COMBINED_DATA[@]}" | sort -u > "${AUDIT_RULE_FILE}"<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Merge and load the rules into active configuration:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># augenrules --load
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Check if reboot is required.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># if [[ $(auditctl -s | grep "enabled") =~ "2" ]]; then printf "Reboot required to load rules\n"; fi
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Special mount points</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>If there are any special mount points that are not visible by default from just scanning <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/</xhtml:span>, change the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PARTITION</xhtml:span> variable to the appropriate partition and re-run the remediation.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p class="bold">Impact:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Both the audit and remediation section of this recommendation will traverse all mounted file systems that is not mounted with either <xhtml:span class="inline_block">noexec</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">nosuid</xhtml:span> mount options. If there are large file systems without these mount options, <xhtml:strong>such traversal will be significantly detrimental to the performance of the system.</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Before running either the audit or remediation section, inspect the output of the following command to determine exactly which file systems will be traversed:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># findmnt -n -l -k -it $(awk '/nodev/ { print $2 }' /proc/filesystems | paste -sd,) | grep -Pv "noexec|nosuid"
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>To exclude a particular file system due to adverse performance impacts, update the audit and remediation sections by adding a sufficiently unique string to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">grep</xhtml:span> statement. The above command can be used to test the modified exclusions.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>On disk configuration</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following script to check on disk rules:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   for PARTITION in $(findmnt -n -l -k -it $(awk '/nodev/ { print $2 }' /proc/filesystems | paste -sd,) | grep -Pv "noexec|nosuid" | awk '{print $1}'); do<br />      for PRIVILEGED in $(find "${PARTITION}" -xdev -perm /6000 -type f); do<br />         grep -qr "${PRIVILEGED}" /etc/audit/rules.d && printf "OK: '${PRIVILEGED}' found in auditing rules.\n" || printf "Warning: '${PRIVILEGED}' not found in on disk configuration.\n"<br />      done<br />   done<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Verify that all output is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">OK</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Running configuration</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following script to check loaded rules:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   RUNNING=$(auditctl -l)<br />   [ -n "${RUNNING}" ] && for PARTITION in $(findmnt -n -l -k -it $(awk '/nodev/ { print $2 }' /proc/filesystems | paste -sd,) | grep -Pv "noexec|nosuid" | awk '{print $1}'); do<br />      for PRIVILEGED in $(find "${PARTITION}" -xdev -perm /6000 -type f); do<br />         printf -- "${RUNNING}" | grep -q "${PRIVILEGED}" && printf "OK: '${PRIVILEGED}' found in auditing rules.\n" || printf "Warning: '${PRIVILEGED}' not found in running configuration.\n"<br />      done<br />   done \<br />   || printf "ERROR: Variable 'RUNNING' is unset.\n"<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Verify that all output is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">OK</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Special mount points</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>If there are any special mount points that are not visible by default from <xhtml:span class="inline_block">findmnt</xhtml:span> as per the above audit, said file systems would have to be manually audited.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure unsuccessful file access attempts are collected
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>Monitor for unsuccessful attempts to access files. The following parameters are associated with system calls that control files:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>creation - <xhtml:span class="inline_block">creat</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>opening - <xhtml:span class="inline_block">open</xhtml:span> , <xhtml:span class="inline_block">openat</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>truncation - <xhtml:span class="inline_block">truncate</xhtml:span> , <xhtml:span class="inline_block">ftruncate</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>An audit log record will only be written if all of the following criteria is met for the user when trying to access a file:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>a non-privileged user (auid>=UID_MIN)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>is not a Daemon event (auid=4294967295/unset/-1)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>if the system call returned EACCES (permission denied) or EPERM (some other permanent error associated with the specific system call)</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Failed attempts to open, create or truncate files could be an indication that an individual or process is trying to gain unauthorized access to the system.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Create audit rules</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Edit or create a file in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/audit/rules.d/</xhtml:span> directory, ending in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.rules</xhtml:span> extension, with the relevant rules to monitor unsuccessful file access attempts.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># {<br />UID_MIN=$(awk '/^\s*UID_MIN/{print $2}' /etc/login.defs)<br />[ -n "${UID_MIN}" ] && printf "<br />-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S creat,open,openat,truncate,ftruncate -F exit=-EACCES -F auid>=${UID_MIN} -F auid!=unset -k access<br />-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S creat,open,openat,truncate,ftruncate -F exit=-EPERM -F auid>=${UID_MIN} -F auid!=unset -k access<br />-a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S creat,open,openat,truncate,ftruncate -F exit=-EACCES -F auid>=${UID_MIN} -F auid!=unset -k access<br />-a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S creat,open,openat,truncate,ftruncate -F exit=-EPERM -F auid>=${UID_MIN} -F auid!=unset -k access<br />" >> /etc/audit/rules.d/50-access.rules || printf "ERROR: Variable 'UID_MIN' is unset.\n"<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Load audit rules</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>

<xhtml:code class="code_block"># if [[ $(auditctl -s | grep "enabled") =~ "2" ]]; then printf "Reboot required to load rules\n"; fi
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure events that modify user/group information are collected
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>Record events affecting the modification of user or group information, including that of passwords and old passwords if in use.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/group</xhtml:span> - system groups</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> - system users</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/gshadow</xhtml:span> - encrypted password for each group</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span> - system user passwords</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/security/opasswd</xhtml:span> - storage of old passwords if the relevant PAM module is in use</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/nsswitch.conf</xhtml:span> - file configures how the system uses various databases and name resolution mechanisms</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.conf</xhtml:span> - file determines the authentication services to be used, and the order in which the services are used.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/pam.d</xhtml:span> - directory contains the PAM configuration files for each PAM-aware application.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>The parameters in this section will watch the files to see if they have been opened for write or have had attribute changes (e.g. permissions) and tag them with the identifier "identity" in the audit log file.</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure discretionary access control permission modification events are collected
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>Monitor changes to file permissions, attributes, ownership and group. The parameters in this section track changes for system calls that affect file permissions and attributes. The following commands and system calls effect the permissions, ownership and various attributes of files.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">chmod</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">fchmod</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">fchmodat</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">chown</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">fchown</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">fchownat</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">lchown</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">setxattr</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">lsetxattr</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">fsetxattr</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">removexattr</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">lremovexattr</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">fremovexattr</xhtml:span></xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>In all cases, an audit record will only be written for non-system user ids and will ignore Daemon events. All audit records will be tagged with the identifier "perm_mod."</xhtml:p>

Rule.description: <xhtml:p>Monitor the use of the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">mount</xhtml:span> system call. <xhtml:p>If the auditing configuration is locked (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">-e 2</xhtml:span>), then <xhtml:span class="inline_block">augenrules</xhtml:span> will not warn in any way that rules could not be loaded into the running configuration. <xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>System call structure</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>For performance (<xhtml:span class="inline_block">man 7 audit.rules</xhtml:span>) reasons it is preferable to have all the system calls on one line. This is important to understand for both the auditing and remediation sections as the examples given are optimized for performance as per the man page.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>It is highly unusual for a non privileged user to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">mount</xhtml:span> file systems to the system. While tracking <xhtml:span class="inline_block">mount</xhtml:span> commands gives the system administrator evidence that external media may have been mounted (based on a review of the source of the mount and confirming it's an external media type), it does not conclusively indicate that data was exported to the media. System administrators who wish to determine if data were exported, would also have to track successful <xhtml:span class="inline_block">open</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">creat</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">truncate</xhtml:span> system calls requiring write access to a file under the mount point of the external media file system. This could give a fair indication that a write occurred. The only way to truly prove it, would be to track successful writes to the external media. Tracking write system calls could quickly fill up the audit log and is not recommended. Recommendations on configuration options to track data export to media is beyond the scope of this document.</xhtml:p>

<xhtml:code class="code_block"># if [[ $(auditctl -s | grep "enabled") =~ "2" ]]; then printf "Reboot required to load rules\n"; fi
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure kernel module loading unloading and modification is collected
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>Monitor the loading and unloading of kernel modules. All the loading / listing / dependency checking of modules is done by <xhtml:span class="inline_block">kmod</xhtml:span> via symbolic links.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The following system calls control loading and unloading of modules:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">init_module</xhtml:span> - load a module</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">finit_module</xhtml:span> - load a module (used when the overhead of using cryptographically signed modules to determine the authenticity of a module can be avoided)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">delete_module</xhtml:span> - delete a module</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">create_module</xhtml:span> - create a loadable module entry</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">query_module</xhtml:span> - query the kernel for various bits pertaining to modules</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>Any execution of the loading and unloading module programs and system calls will trigger an audit record with an identifier of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">modules</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>

A system reboot will be required to load the rules into the running configuration.</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure AIDE is installed

metadata.notes:
<xhtml:p>The checking in this recommendation occurs every day at 5am. Alter the frequency and time of the checks in compliance with site policy</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>systemd timers, timer file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">aidecheck.timer</xhtml:span> and service file <xhtml:span class="inline_block">aidecheck.service</xhtml:span>, have been included as an optional alternative to using <xhtml:span class="inline_block">cron</xhtml:span></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Ubuntu advises using <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/bin/aide.wrapper</xhtml:span> rather than calling <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/bin/aide</xhtml:span> directly in order to protect the database and prevent conflicts</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Periodic file checking allows the system administrator to determine on a regular basis if critical files have been changed in an unauthorized fashion.</xhtml:p>

<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl unmask dailyaidecheck.timer dailyaidecheck.service
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to enable and start <xhtml:span class="inline_block">dailyaidecheck.timer</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># systemctl --now enable dailyaidecheck.timer

</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
