Rule.title: Ensure cryptographic mechanisms are used to protect the integrity of audit tools
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>Audit tools include, but are not limited to, vendor-provided and open source audit tools needed to successfully view and manipulate audit information system activity and records. Audit tools include custom queries and report generators.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">aide.conf</xhtml:span> is case-sensitive. Leading and trailing white spaces are ignored. Each config lines must end with new line.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">AIDE</xhtml:span> uses the backslash character <xhtml:span class="inline_block">\</xhtml:span> as escape character for '<xhtml:span class="inline_block"> </xhtml:span>' (space), '@' and '' (backslash) (e.g. '\ ' or '@'). To literally match a '' in  a  file path with a regular expression you have to escape the backslash twice (i.e. '\\').</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>There  are  three  types  of lines in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">aide.conf</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>The configuration options which are used to set configuration parameters and define groups.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>(restricted) rules that are used to indicate which files are added to the database.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Macro lines define or undefine variables within the config file.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> Lines beginning with <xhtml:span class="inline_block">#</xhtml:span> are ignored as comments.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">@@include</xhtml:span> <xhtml:em><FILE></xhtml:em> - Include <xhtml:em><FILE></xhtml:em>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>The content of the file is used as if it were inserted in this part of the config file.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The maximum depth of nested includes is 16.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>`@@include <xhtml:em><DIRECTORY></xhtml:em> <xhtml:em><REGEX></xhtml:em> - [RULE_PREFIX] (added in AIDE v0.17)</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Include all (regular) files found in <DIRECTORY> matching regular expression <REGEX> (sub-directories are ignored).</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The file are included in lexical sort order.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>If <xhtml:span class="inline_block">RULE_PREFIX</xhtml:span> is set, all rules included by the statement are prefixed with given <RULE_PREFIX> (added in AIDE v0.18). Prefixes  from  nested  include statements are concatenated.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The content of the files is used as if it were inserted in this part of the config file.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">@x_include</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>is identical to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">@@include</xhtml:span>, except that if a config file is executable is is run and the output is used as config.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>If the executable file exits with status greater than zero or writes to stderr aide stops with an error.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>For security reasons <xhtml:em><DIRECTORY></xhtml:em> and each executable config file must be owned by the current user or root. They must not be group- or world-writable.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">@@x_include _<FILE>_</xhtml:span> (added in AIDE v0.17):</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>`@@x_include <xhtml:em><DIRECTORY></xhtml:em> <xhtml:em><REGEX></xhtml:em> [RULE_PREFIX]  (added in AIDE v0.17)</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">@@x_include_setenv</xhtml:span> <xhtml:em><VAR></xhtml:em> <xhtml:em><VALUE></xhtml:em> (added in AIDE v0.17)</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Adds the variable <xhtml:em><VAR></xhtml:em> with the value <xhtml:em><VALUE></xhtml:em> to the environment used for config file execution.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Environment variable names are limited to alphanumeric characters (A-Za-z0-9) and the underscore '_' and must not begin with a digit.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>Protecting the integrity of the tools used for auditing purposes is a critical step toward ensuring the integrity of audit information. Audit information includes all information (e.g., audit records, audit settings, and audit reports) needed to successfully audit information system activity.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Attackers may replace the audit tools or inject code into the existing tools with the purpose of providing the capability to hide or erase system activity from the audit logs.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Audit tools should be cryptographically signed in order to provide the capability to identify when the audit tools have been modified, manipulated, or replaced. An example is a checksum hash of the file or files.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to determine the absolute path to the non-symlinked version on the audit tools:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># readlink -f /sbin
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>The output will be either <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/usr/sbin</xhtml:span> <xhtml:strong>- OR -</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/sbin</xhtml:span>. Ensure the correct path is used.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/aide/aide.conf</xhtml:span> and add or update the following selection lines replacing <xhtml:span class="inline_block"><PATH></xhtml:span> with the correct path returned in the command above:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># Audit Tools <br /><PATH>/auditctl p+i+n+u+g+s+b+acl+xattrs+sha512 <br /><PATH>/auditd p+i+n+u+g+s+b+acl+xattrs+sha512 <br /><PATH>/ausearch p+i+n+u+g+s+b+acl+xattrs+sha512 <br /><PATH>/aureport p+i+n+u+g+s+b+acl+xattrs+sha512 <br /><PATH>/autrace p+i+n+u+g+s+b+acl+xattrs+sha512 <br /><PATH>/augenrules p+i+n+u+g+s+b+acl+xattrs+sha512
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># printf '%s\n' "" "# Audit Tools" "$(readlink -f /sbin/auditctl) p+i+n+u+g+s+b+acl+xattrs+sha512" "$(readlink -f /sbin/auditd) p+i+n+u+g+s+b+acl+xattrs+sha512" "$(readlink -f /sbin/ausearch) p+i+n+u+g+s+b+acl+xattrs+sha512" "$(readlink -f /sbin/aureport) p+i+n+u+g+s+b+acl+xattrs+sha512" "$(readlink -f /sbin/autrace) p+i+n+u+g+s+b+acl+xattrs+sha512" "$(readlink -f /sbin/augenrules) p+i+n+u+g+s+b+acl+xattrs+sha512" >> /etc/aide/aide.conf
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note: - IF -</xhtml:strong> <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/aide/aide.conf</xhtml:span> includes a <xhtml:span class="inline_block">@@x_include</xhtml:span> statement:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:em><DIRECTORY></xhtml:em> and each executable config file must be owned by the current user or root</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>They must not be group or world-writable</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">@@x_include /etc/aide.conf.d ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Verify that Advanced Intrusion Detection Environment (AIDE) is properly configured .</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Run the following script to verify:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>AIDE is configured to use cryptographic mechanisms to protect the integrity of audit tools:</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The following audit tool files include the options "p, i, n, u, g, s, b, acl, xattrs and sha512"
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>auditctl</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>auditd</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>ausearch</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>aureport</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>autrace</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>augenrules</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_output=() a_output2=() l_tool_dir="$(readlink -f /sbin)"<br />   a_items=("p" "i" "n" "u" "g" "s" "b" "acl" "xattrs" "sha512")<br />   l_aide_cmd="$(whereis aide | awk '{print $2}')"<br />   a_audit_files=("auditctl" "auditd" "ausearch" "aureport" "autrace" "augenrules")<br />   if [ -f "$l_aide_cmd" ] && command -v "$l_aide_cmd" &>/dev/null; then<br />      a_aide_conf_files=("$(find -L /etc -type f -name 'aide.conf')")<br />      f_file_par_chk()<br />      {<br />         a_out2=()<br />         for l_item in "${a_items[@]}"; do<br />            ! grep -Psiq -- '(\h+|\+)'"$l_item"'(\h+|\+)' <<< "$l_out" && \<br />            a_out2+=("  - Missing the \"$l_item\" option")<br />         done<br />         if [ "${#a_out2[@]}" -gt "0" ]; then<br />            a_output2+=(" - Audit tool file: \"$l_file\"" "${a_out2[@]}")<br />         else<br />            a_output+=(" - Audit tool file: \"$l_file\" includes:" "   \"${a_items[*]}\"")<br />         fi<br />      }<br />      for l_file in "${a_audit_files[@]}"; do<br />         if [ -f "$l_tool_dir/$l_file" ]; then<br />            l_out="$("$l_aide_cmd" --config "${a_aide_conf_files[@]}" -p f:"$l_tool_dir/$l_file")"<br />            f_file_par_chk<br />         else<br />            a_output+=("  - Audit tool file \"$l_file\" doesn't exist")<br />         fi<br />      done<br />   else<br />      a_output2+=("  - The command \"aide\" was not found"  "    Please install AIDE")<br />   fi<br />   if [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -le 0 ]; then<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** PASS **" "${a_output[@]}" ""<br />   else<br />      printf '%s\n' "" "- Audit Result:" "  ** FAIL **" " - Reason(s) for audit failure:" "${a_output2[@]}"<br />      [ "${#a_output[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "" "- Correctly set:" "${a_output[@]}" ""<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> The script is written to read the "winning" configuration setting, to include any configuration settings in files included as part of the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">@@x_include</xhtml:span> setting.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Group.title: System Maintenance
Group.description: <xhtml:p>Recommendations in this section are intended as maintenance and are intended to be checked on a frequent basis to ensure system stability. Many recommendations do not have quick remediations and require investigation into the cause and best fix available and may indicate an attempted breach of system security.</xhtml:p>

Group.title: System File Permissions
Group.description: <xhtml:p>This section provides guidance on securing aspects of system files and directories.</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure permissions on /etc/passwd are configured
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> file contains user account information that is used by many system utilities and therefore must be readable for these utilities to operate.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Protect Information through  Access Control Lists

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>It is critical to ensure that the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> file is protected from unauthorized write access. Although it is protected by default, the file permissions could be changed either inadvertently or through malicious actions.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following commands to remove excess permissions, set owner, and set group on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># chmod u-x,go-wx /etc/passwd<br /># chown root:root /etc/passwd
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> is mode 644 or more restrictive, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Uid</xhtml:span> is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0/root</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Gid</xhtml:span> is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0/root</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># stat -Lc 'Access: (%#a/%A)  Uid: ( %u/ %U) Gid: ( %g/ %G)'  /etc/passwd<br /><br />Access: (0644/-rw-r--r--)  Uid: ( 0/ root) Gid: ( 0/ root)
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure permissions on /etc/shadow are configured
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span> file is used to store the information about user accounts that is critical to the security of those accounts, such as the hashed password and other security information.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Protect Information through  Access Control Lists

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>If attackers can gain read access to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span> file, they can easily run a password cracking program against the hashed password to break it. Other security information that is stored in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span> file (such as expiration) could also be useful to subvert the user accounts.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run <xhtml:strong>one</xhtml:strong> of the following commands to set ownership of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span> to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span> and group to either <xhtml:span class="inline_block">root</xhtml:span> or <xhtml:span class="inline_block">shadow</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># chown root:shadow /etc/shadow<br />  -OR-<br /># chown root:root /etc/shadow
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Run the following command to remove excess permissions form <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># chmod u-x,g-wx,o-rwx /etc/shadow
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to verify <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span> is mode 640 or more restrictive, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Uid</xhtml:span> is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0/root</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">Gid</xhtml:span> is <xhtml:span class="inline_block">0/root</xhtml:span> or ({GID}/ shadow):</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># stat -Lc 'Access: (%#a/%A)  Uid: ( %u/ %U) Gid: ( %g/ %G)'  /etc/shadow
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:em>Example:</xhtml:em></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">Access: (0640/-rw-r-----)  Uid: ( 0/ root) Gid: ( 42/ shadow)
</xhtml:code>

Rule.title: Ensure world writable files and directories are secured
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>World writable files are the least secure. Data in world-writable files can be modified and compromised by any user on the system. World writable files may also indicate an incorrectly written script or program that could potentially be the cause of a larger compromise to the system's integrity. See the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chmod(2)</xhtml:span> man page for more information.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Setting the sticky bit on world writable directories prevents users from deleting or renaming files in that directory that are not owned by them.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists

Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>Data in world-writable files can be modified and compromised by any user on the system. World writable files may also indicate an incorrectly written script or program that could potentially be the cause of a larger compromise to the system's integrity.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>This feature prevents the ability to delete or rename files in world writable directories (such as <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/tmp</xhtml:span> ) that are owned by another user.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>World Writable Files:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>It is recommended that write access is removed from <xhtml:span class="inline_block">other</xhtml:span> with the command ( <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chmod o-w <filename></xhtml:span> ), but always consult relevant vendor documentation to avoid breaking any application dependencies on a given file.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>World Writable Directories:
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Set the sticky bit on all world writable directories with the command ( <xhtml:span class="inline_block">chmod a+t <directory_name></xhtml:span> )</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>Run the following script to:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Remove other write permission from any world writable files</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Add the sticky bit to all world writable directories</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The owner of a file can set the file's permissions to run with the owner's or group's permissions, even if the user running the program is not the owner or a member of the group. The most common reason for a SUID or SGID program is to enable users to perform functions (such as changing their password) that require root privileges.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Protect Information through  Access Control Lists

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>There are valid reasons for SUID and SGID programs, but it is important to identify and review such programs to ensure they are legitimate. Review the files returned by the action in the audit section and check to see if system binaries have a different checksum than what from the package. This is an indication that the binary may have been replaced.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: CM-1, CM-2, CM-6, CM-7, IA-5, AC-3, MP-2

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Ensure that no rogue SUID or SGID programs have been introduced into the system. Review the files returned by the action in the Audit section and confirm the integrity of these binaries.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

(( ${#a_suid[@]} > 0 )); then<br />      l_output="$l_output

$(printf '%s

Group.title: Local User and Group Settings
Group.description:
<xhtml:p>This section provides guidance on securing aspects of the local users and groups.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong> The recommendations in this section check local users and groups.  Any users or groups from other sources such as LDAP will not be audited.  In a domain environment similar checks should be performed against domain users and groups.</xhtml:p>

Rule.title: Ensure accounts in /etc/passwd use shadowed passwords
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>Local accounts can uses shadowed passwords.  With shadowed passwords, The passwords are saved in shadow password file, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span>, encrypted by a salted one-way hash. Accounts with a shadowed password have an <xhtml:span class="inline_block">x</xhtml:span> in the second field in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Encrypt Sensitive Data at Rest
Encrypt or Hash all Authentication Credentials

metadata.notes:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pwconv</xhtml:span> command creates shadow from <xhtml:span class="inline_block">passwd</xhtml:span> and an optionally existing <xhtml:span class="inline_block">shadow</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pwunconv</xhtml:span> command creates <xhtml:span class="inline_block">passwd</xhtml:span> from <xhtml:span class="inline_block">passwd</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">shadow</xhtml:span> and then removes <xhtml:span class="inline_block">shadow</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">grpconv</xhtml:span> command creates <xhtml:span class="inline_block">gshadow</xhtml:span> from <xhtml:span class="inline_block">group</xhtml:span> and an optionally existing <xhtml:span class="inline_block">gshadow</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">grpunconv</xhtml:span> command creates <xhtml:span class="inline_block">group</xhtml:span> from <xhtml:span class="inline_block">group</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">gshadow</xhtml:span> and then removes <xhtml:span class="inline_block">gshadow</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>These four programs all operate on the normal and shadow password and group files: <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/group</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span>, and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/gshadow</xhtml:span>.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>Each program acquires the necessary locks before conversion. <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pwconv</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">grpconv</xhtml:span> are similar. First, entries in the shadowed file which don't exist in the main file are removed. Then, shadowed entries which don't have <xhtml:span class="inline_block">x' as the password in the main file are updated. Any missing shadowed entries are added. Finally, passwords in the main file are replaced with </xhtml:span>x'. These programs can be used for initial conversion as well to update the shadowed file if the main file is edited by hand.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">pwconv</xhtml:span> will use the values of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_MIN_DAYS</xhtml:span>, <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_MAX_DAYS</xhtml:span>, and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">PASS_WARN_AGE</xhtml:span> from /etc/login.defs when adding new entries to /etc/shadow.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:span class="inline_block">pwunconv</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">grpunconv</xhtml:span> are similar. Passwords in the main file are updated from the shadowed file. Entries which exist in the main file but not in the shadowed file are left alone. Finally, the shadowed file is removed. Some password aging information is lost by <xhtml:span class="inline_block">pwunconv</xhtml:span>. It will convert what it can.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale:
<xhtml:p>The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> file also contains information like user ID's and group ID's that are used by many system programs. Therefore, the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> file must remain world readable. In spite of encoding the password with a randomly-generated one-way hash function, an attacker could still break the system if they got access to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> file. This can be mitigated by using shadowed passwords, thus moving the passwords in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> file to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span>. The <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span> file is set so only root will be able to read and write. This helps mitigate the risk of an attacker gaining access to the encoded passwords with which to perform a dictionary attack.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p><xhtml:strong>Note:</xhtml:strong></xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>All accounts must have passwords or be locked to prevent the account from being used by an unauthorized user.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>A user account with an empty second field in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> allows the account to be logged into by providing only the username.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to set accounts to use shadowed passwords and migrate passwords in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> to <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># pwconv
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Investigate to determine if the account is logged in and what it is being used for, to determine if it needs to be forced off.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command and verify that no output is returned:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># awk -F: '($2 != "x" ) { print "User: \"" $1 "\" is not set to shadowed passwords "}' /etc/passwd
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure /etc/shadow password fields are not empty
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>An account with an empty password field means that anybody may log in as that user without providing a password.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Use Unique Passwords
Use Unique Passwords

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>All accounts must have passwords or be locked to prevent the account from being used by an unauthorized user.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>If any accounts in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span> file do not have a password, run the following command to lock the account until it can be determined why it does not have a password:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># passwd -l <username>
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Also, check to see if the account is logged in and investigate what it is being used for to determine if it needs to be forced off.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command and verify that no output is returned:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># awk -F: '($2 == "" ) { print $1 " does not have a password "}' /etc/shadow
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure all groups in /etc/passwd exist in /etc/group
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>Over time, system administration errors and changes can lead to groups being defined in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> but not in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/group</xhtml:span> .</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Train Workforce Members on Recognizing and Reporting Security Incidents

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Groups defined in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> file but not in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/group</xhtml:span> file pose a threat to system security since group permissions are not properly managed.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: CM-1, CM-2, CM-6, CM-7, IA-5

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Analyze the output of the Audit step above and perform the appropriate action to correct any discrepancies found.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script to verify all GIDs in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> exist in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/group</xhtml:span>:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_passwd_group_gid=("$(awk -F: '{print $4}' /etc/passwd | sort -u)")<br />   a_group_gid=("$(awk -F: '{print $3}' /etc/group | sort -u)")<br />   a_passwd_group_diff=("$(printf '%s\n' "${a_group_gid[@]}" "${a_passwd_group_gid[@]}" | sort | uniq -u)")<br />   while IFS= read -r l_gid; do<br />      awk -F: '($4 == '"$l_gid"') {print "  - User: \"" $1 "\" has GID: \"" $4 "\" which does not exist in /etc/group" }' /etc/passwd<br />   done < <(printf '%s\n' "${a_passwd_group_gid[@]}" "${a_passwd_group_diff[@]}" | sort | uniq -D | uniq)<br />   unset a_passwd_group_gid; unset a_group_gid; unset a_passwd_group_diff<br />}
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Nothing should be returned</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure shadow group is empty
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The shadow group allows system programs which require access the ability to read the /etc/shadow file. No users should be assigned to the shadow group.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Protect Information through  Access Control Lists

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Any users assigned to the shadow group would be granted read access to the /etc/shadow file. If attackers can gain read access to the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span> file, they can easily run a password cracking program against the hashed passwords to break them. Other security information that is stored in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/shadow</xhtml:span> file (such as expiration) could also be useful to subvert additional user accounts.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following command to remove all users from the shadow group</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># sed -ri 's/(^shadow:[^:]*:[^:]*:)([^:]+$)/\1/' /etc/group
</xhtml:code>
<xhtml:p>Change the primary group of any users with shadow as their primary group.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># usermod -g <primary group> <user>
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following commands and verify no results are returned:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block"># awk -F: '($1=="shadow") {print $NF}' /etc/group<br /># awk -F: '($4 == '"$(getent group shadow | awk -F: '{print $3}' | xargs)"') {print "  - user: \"" $1 "\" primary group is the shadow group"}' /etc/passwd
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

artifact_expression.artifact_title: Ensure no file named /etc/group exists and matches pattern ^shadow:[^:]*:[^:]*:[^:]+$

Rule.title: Ensure no duplicate UIDs exist
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>Although the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">useradd</xhtml:span> program will not let you create a duplicate User ID (UID), it is possible for an administrator to manually edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> file and change the UID field.</xhtml:p>
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Users must be assigned unique UIDs for accountability and to ensure appropriate access protections.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: CM-1, CM-2, CM-6, CM-7, IA-5

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Based on the results of the audit script, establish unique UIDs and review all files owned by the shared UIDs to determine which UID they are supposed to belong to.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script and verify no results are returned:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />  while read -r l_count l_uid; do<br />    if [ "$l_count" -gt 1 ]; then<br />      echo -e "Duplicate UID: \"$l_uid\" Users: \"$(awk -F: '($3 == n) { print $1 }' n=$l_uid /etc/passwd | xargs)\""<br />    fi<br />  done < <(cut -f3 -d":" /etc/passwd | sort -n | uniq -c)<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure no duplicate GIDs exist
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>Although the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">groupadd</xhtml:span> program will not let you create a duplicate Group ID (GID), it is possible for an administrator to manually edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/group</xhtml:span> file and change the GID field.</xhtml:p>

metadata.notes: <xhtml:p>You can also use the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">grpck</xhtml:span> command to check for other inconsistencies in the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/group</xhtml:span> file.</xhtml:p>

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>User groups must be assigned unique GIDs for accountability and to ensure appropriate access protections.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: CM-1, CM-2, CM-6, CM-7, IA-5

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Based on the results of the audit script, establish unique GIDs and review all files owned by the shared GID to determine which group they are supposed to belong to.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script and verify no results are returned:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   while read -r l_count l_gid; do<br />      if [ "$l_count" -gt 1 ]; then<br />      echo -e "Duplicate GID: \"$l_gid\" Groups: \"$(awk -F: '($3 == n) { print $1 }' n=$l_gid /etc/group | xargs)\""<br />    fi<br />  done < <(cut -f3 -d":" /etc/group | sort -n | uniq -c)<br />} 
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

Rule.title: Ensure no duplicate user names exist
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>Although the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">useradd</xhtml:span> program will not let you create a duplicate user name, it is possible for an administrator to manually edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> file and change the user name.</xhtml:p>
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>If a user is assigned a duplicate user name, it will create and have access to files with the first UID for that username in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> . For example, if "test4" has a UID of 1000 and a subsequent "test4" entry has a UID of 2000, logging in as "test4" will use UID 1000. Effectively, the UID is shared, which is a security problem.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: CM-1, CM-2, CM-6, CM-7, IA-5

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Based on the results of the audit script, establish unique user names for the users. File ownerships will automatically reflect the change as long as the users have unique UIDs.</xhtml:p>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Run the following script and verify no results are returned:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   while read -r l_count l_user; do<br />      if [ "$l_count" -gt 1 ]; then<br />         echo -e "Duplicate User: \"$l_user\" Users: \"$(awk -F: '($1 == n) { print $1 }' n=$l_user /etc/passwd | xargs)\""<br />      fi<br />   done < <(cut -f1 -d":" /etc/group | sort -n | uniq -c)<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>

artifact_expression.artifact_title: Script Check Engine Check "nix_duplicate_username.sh"

Rule.description: <xhtml:p>Although the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">groupadd</xhtml:span> program will not let you create a duplicate group name, it is possible for an administrator to manually edit the <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/group</xhtml:span> file and change the group name.</xhtml:p>
Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>If a group is assigned a duplicate group name, it will create and have access to files with the first GID for that group in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/group</xhtml:span> . Effectively, the GID is shared, which is a security problem.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: CM-1, CM-2, CM-6, CM-7, IA-5

Rule.fixtext:

</xhtml:code>

Rule.title: Ensure local interactive user home directories are configured
Rule.description: <xhtml:p>The user home directory is space defined for the particular user to set local environment variables and to store personal files.  While the system administrator can establish secure permissions for users' home directories, the users can easily override these. Users can be defined in <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> without a home directory or with a home directory that does not actually exist.</xhtml:p>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Protect Information through  Access Control Lists

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>Since the user is accountable for files stored in the user home directory, the user must be the owner of the directory. Group or world-writable user home directories may enable malicious users to steal or modify other users' data or to gain another user's system privileges. If the user's home directory does not exist or is unassigned, the user will be placed in "/" and will not be able to write any files or have local environment variables set.</xhtml:p>
Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>If a local interactive users' home directory is undefined and/or doesn't exist, follow local site policy and perform one of the following:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Lock the user account</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Remove the user from the system</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>create a directory for the user.  If undefined, edit <xhtml:span class="inline_block">/etc/passwd</xhtml:span> and add the absolute path to the directory to the last field of the user.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:p>Run the following script to:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>Remove excessive permissions from local interactive users home directories</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>Update the home directory's owner</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   l_output2=""<br />   l_valid_shells="^($( awk -F/ '$NF != "nologin" {print}' /etc/shells | sed -rn '/^//{s,/,\\/,g;p}' | paste -s -d '|' - ))$"<br />   unset a_uarr && a_uarr=() # Clear and initialize array<br />   while read -r l_epu l_eph; do # Populate array with users and user home location<br />      a_uarr+=("$l_epu $l_eph")<br />   done <<< "$(awk -v pat="$l_valid_shells" -F: '$(NF) ~ pat { print $1 " " $(NF-1) }' /etc/passwd)"<br />   l_asize="${#a_uarr[@]}" # Here if we want to look at number of users before proceeding <br />   [ "$l_asize " -gt "10000" ] && echo -e "
  ** INFO **
  - "$l_asize" Local interactive users found on the system
  - This may be a long running process
"<br />   while read -r l_user l_home; do<br />      if [ -d "$l_home" ]; then<br />         l_mask='0027'<br />         l_max="$( printf '%o' $(( 0777 & ~$l_mask)) )"<br />         while read -r l_own l_mode; do<br />            if [ "$l_user" != "$l_own" ]; then<br />               l_output2="$l_output2
  - User: "$l_user" Home "$l_home" is owned by: "$l_own"
  -  changing ownership to: "$l_user"
"<br />               chown "$l_user" "$l_home"<br />            fi<br />            if [ $(( $l_mode & $l_mask )) -gt 0 ]; then<br />               l_output2="$l_output2
  - User: "$l_user" Home "$l_home" is mode: "$l_mode" should be mode: "$l_max" or more restrictive
  -  removing excess permissions
"<br />               chmod g-w,o-rwx "$l_home"<br />            fi<br />         done <<< "$(stat -Lc '%U %#a' "$l_home")"<br />      else<br />         l_output2="$l_output2
  - User: "$l_user" Home "$l_home" Doesn't exist
  -  Please create a home in accordance with local site policy"<br />      fi<br />   done <<< "$(printf '%s
' "${a_uarr[@]}")"<br />   if [ -z "$l_output2" ]; then # If l_output2 is empty, we pass<br />      echo -e " - No modification needed to local interactive users home directories"<br />   else<br />      echo -e "
$l_output2"<br />   fi<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
Rule.auditcheck:

Rule.title: Ensure local interactive user dot files access is configured
Rule.description:
<xhtml:p>While the system administrator can establish secure permissions for users' "dot" files, the users can easily override these.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">.forward</xhtml:span> file specifies an email address to forward the user's mail to.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">.rhost</xhtml:span> file provides the "remote authentication" database for the rcp, rlogin, and rsh commands and the rcmd() function. These files bypass the standard password-based user authentication mechanism. They specify remote hosts and users that are considered trusted (i.e. are allowed to access the local system without supplying a password)</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">.netrc</xhtml:span> file contains data for logging into a remote host or passing authentication to an API.</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li><xhtml:span class="inline_block">.bash_history</xhtml:span> file keeps track of the user’s commands.</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>

safeguard.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists
Protect Information through  Access Control Lists

Rule.rationale: <xhtml:p>User configuration files with excessive or incorrect access may enable malicious users to steal or modify other users' data or to gain another user's system privileges.</xhtml:p>

idents.systemValue: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: CM-1, CM-2, CM-6, CM-7, IA-5

Rule.fixtext:
<xhtml:div><xhtml:p><xhtml:p>Making global modifications to users' files without alerting the user community can result in unexpected outages and unhappy users. Therefore, it is recommended that a monitoring policy be established to report user dot file permissions and determine the action to be taken in accordance with site policy.</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:p>The following script will:</xhtml:p>
<xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:li>remove excessive permissions on <xhtml:span class="inline_block">dot</xhtml:span> files within interactive users' home directories</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>change ownership of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">dot</xhtml:span> files within interactive users' home directories to the user</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>change group ownership of <xhtml:span class="inline_block">dot</xhtml:span> files within interactive users' home directories to the user's primary group</xhtml:li>
<xhtml:li>list <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.forward</xhtml:span> and <xhtml:span class="inline_block">.rhost</xhtml:span> files to be investigated and manually deleted</xhtml:li>
</xhtml:ul>
<xhtml:code class="code_block">#!/usr/bin/env bash<br /><br />{<br />   a_output2=(); a_output3=()<br />   l_maxsize="1000" # Maximum number of local interactive users before warning (Default 1,000)<br />   l_valid_shells="^($( awk -F\/ '$NF != "nologin" {print}' /etc/shells | sed -rn '/^\//{s,/,\\\\/,g;p}' | paste -s -d '|' - ))$"<br />   a_user_and_home=() # Create array with local users and their home directories<br />   while read -r l_local_user l_local_user_home; do # Populate array with users and user home location<br />      [[ -n "$l_local_user" && -n "$l_local_user_home" ]] && a_user_and_home+=("$l_local_user:$l_local_user_home")<br />   done <<< "$(awk -v pat="$l_valid_shells" -F: '$(NF) ~ pat { print $1 " " $(NF-1) }' /etc/passwd)"<br />   l_asize="${#a_user_and_home[@]}" # Here if we want to look at number of users before proceeding <br />   [ "${#a_user_and_home[@]}" -gt "$l_maxsize" ] && printf '%s\n' "" "  ** INFO **" \<br />   "  - \"$l_asize\" Local interactive users found on the system" \<br />   "  - This may be a long running check" ""<br />   file_access_fix()<br />   {<br />      a_access_out=()<br />      l_max="$( printf '%o' $(( 0777 & ~$l_mask)) )"<br />      if [ $(( $l_mode & $l_mask )) -gt 0 ]; then<br />         printf '%s\n' "" "  - File: \"$l_hdfile\" is mode: \"$l_mode\" and should be mode: \"$l_max\" or more restrictive" \<br />         "     Updating file: \"$l_hdfile\" to be mode: \"$l_max\" or more restrictive"<br />         chmod "$l_change" "$l_hdfile"<br />      fi<br />      if [[ ! "$l_owner" =~ ($l_user) ]]; then<br />         printf '%s\n' "" "  - File: \"$l_hdfile\" owned by: \"$l_owner\" and should be owned by \"${l_user//|/ or }\"" \<br />         "     Updating file: \"$l_hdfile\" to be owned by \"${l_user//|/ or }\""<br />         chown "$l_user" "$l_hdfile"<br />      fi<br />      if [[ ! "$l_gowner" =~ ($l_group) ]]; then<br />         printf '%s\n' "" "  - File: \"$l_hdfile\" group owned by: \"$l_gowner\" and should be group owned by \"${l_group//|/ or }\"" \<br />         "     Updating file: \"$l_hdfile\" to be group owned by \"${l_group//|/ or }\""<br />         chgrp "$l_group" "$l_hdfile"<br />      fi<br />   }<br />   while IFS=: read -r l_user l_home; do<br />      a_dot_file=(); a_netrc=(); a_netrc_warn=(); a_bhout=(); a_hdirout=()<br />      if [ -d "$l_home" ]; then<br />         l_group="$(id -gn "$l_user" | xargs)";l_group="${l_group// /|}"<br />         while IFS= read -r -d $'\0' l_hdfile; do<br />            while read -r l_mode l_owner l_gowner; do<br />               case "$(basename "$l_hdfile")" in<br />                  .forward | .rhost )<br />                     a_dot_file+=("  - File: \"$l_hdfile\" exists" "    Please review and manually delete this file") ;;<br />                  .netrc )<br />                     l_mask='0177'; l_change="u-x,go-rwx"; file_access_fix<br />                     a_netrc_warn+=("   - File: \"$l_hdfile\" exists") ;;<br />                  .bash_history )<br />                     l_mask='0177'; l_change="u-x,go-rwx"; file_access_fix ;;<br />                  * )<br />                     l_mask='0133'; l_change="u-x,go-wx"; file_access_fix ;;<br />               esac<br />            done < <(stat -Lc '%#a %U %G' "$l_hdfile")<br />         done < <(find "$l_home" -xdev -type f -name '.*' -print0)<br />      fi<br />      [ "${#a_dot_file[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output2+=(" - User: \"$l_user\" Home Directory: \"$l_home\"" "${a_dot_file[@]}")<br />      [ "${#a_netrc_warn[@]}" -gt 0 ] && a_output3+=(" - User: \"$l_user\" Home Directory: \"$l_home\"" "${a_netrc_warn[@]}")<br />   done <<< "$(printf '%s\n' "${a_user_and_home[@]}")"<br />   [ "${#a_output3[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "" "  ** WARNING **" "${a_output3[@]}" ""<br />   [ "${#a_output2[@]}" -gt 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "" "${a_output2[@]}"<br />}
</xhtml:code>
</xhtml:p></xhtml:div>
